# UAVmatrix Docs (full)

# What is UAVcast-Pro?

> UAVcast-Pro turns a Raspberry Pi or Linux companion computer into a 4G/LTE link for MAVLink telemetry and H.264 video. See how it works with Fleet Manager.

UAVcast-Pro is software for a companion computer on your drone, usually a Raspberry Pi. It reads MAVLink from any MAVLink flight controller (ArduPilot or PX4), streams H.264 video from one or two cameras, and sends both to your ground control station over Wi-Fi, Ethernet or a 4G/LTE modem. You set it up and monitor it from a web interface that runs on the drone.

UAVmatrix Fleet Manager is the cloud dashboard that goes with it. Pair a drone running UAVcast-Pro with Fleet Manager and you can see the whole fleet on one map, open a remote terminal, plan missions and route video and telemetry to ground stations without port forwarding. Fleet Manager is included with every UAVcast-Pro license.

## How the pieces connect

```text
 Flight controller ──USB/UART──►  Companion computer running UAVcast-Pro
 (ArduPilot, PX4)                  │  MAVLink router, camera server, modem,
 Camera(s) ──CSI/USB────────────►  │  VPN, NTRIP client, recorder, web UI
                                   │
                                   ├── UDP 14550 (telemetry) ─┐
                                   ├── UDP 5600  (video)    ──┼─► Mission Planner / QGroundControl
                                   │                          │   over LAN, VPN or 4G
                                   └── MQTT/TLS 8883 ─────────┴─► Fleet Manager (optional)
```

- **On the drone**: UAVcast-Pro owns the flight controller's serial port and forwards MAVLink to every ground station you add. The camera server encodes H.264 and sends RTP over UDP to the same ground stations. Nothing listens for incoming telemetry connections unless you add it.
- **Between drone and ground**: on a local network the ground station's own IP is enough. Over 4G the drone has no public address, so you put both ends on a VPN. The [Fleet Manager VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/vpn/), included with every license, does this for you; UAVcast-Pro can also join your own Tailscale or ZeroTier network.
- **In the cloud**: when paired, the drone keeps an outbound, certificate-authenticated MQTT connection to Fleet Manager. See [Pair a drone with Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/fleet-pairing/).

## What you can do with it

| Area | What it does | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Telemetry | Auto-detects the flight controller port and baud rate, routes MAVLink to any number of ground stations, optional read-only destinations | [Flight controller](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/), [Ground control stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/) |
| Video | Raspberry Pi CSI and USB cameras, two cameras with RC switching or dual stream, audio, custom GStreamer pipelines | [Camera & video](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/) |
| Recording | Records each flight's video and telemetry on the drone, with a flight review player | [Recordings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/recordings/) |
| Flight map | Live map, cockpit HUD, arm/disarm, RTL and loiter, mission planner, MAVLink inspector, log analysis | [Flight map](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-map/) |
| Connectivity | 4G/LTE modems with automatic APN, the Fleet Manager VPN or your own Tailscale or ZeroTier network, dynamic DNS, Wi-Fi vs modem priority | [Connectivity](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/) |
| RTK | NTRIP client that sends RTCM3 corrections to the flight controller | [NTRIP / RTK](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/ntrip-rtk/) |
| Custom data | Bridge sensors and scripts into MAVLink and chart them | [Injectors](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/injectors/), [Data Streams](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/data-streams/) |

## What you need

- A 64-bit Linux companion computer (arm64 or amd64). Raspberry Pi 3, 4, 5 and Zero 2 W are the common choice; x86 mini PCs work too, and NVIDIA Jetson, Orange Pi and other arm64 boards from UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3. See [Hardware requirements](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/hardware-requirements/).
- A MAVLink flight controller: ArduPilot or PX4. Flight-mode buttons follow ArduPilot's mode names.
- A UAVcast-Pro license from the [UAVmatrix store](https://uavmatrix.com/products/). See [Licensing & activation](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/).
- For flights beyond Wi-Fi range: a 4G/LTE modem and a data SIM.

## Next steps

[Quick startFrom a fresh Raspberry Pi to telemetry and video in Mission Planner or QGroundControl.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/quick-start/)[Install UAVcast-ProOne command on Raspberry Pi OS, Debian or Ubuntu (arm64 and amd64).](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/installation/)[Activate your licenseActivate on a device, check device slots and move the license to new hardware.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/overview/

# Quick start

> Connect a MAVLink flight controller to UAVcast-Pro and get telemetry and live video in Mission Planner or QGroundControl, first on your LAN, then over 4G/LTE.

This guide takes a drone with UAVcast-Pro installed to live telemetry and video in Mission Planner or QGroundControl. You'll do it on your local network first, where there are fewer things that can go wrong, and then switch to 4G/LTE. The local part takes about 10 minutes.

## Before you begin

- UAVcast-Pro installed and the device rebooted. See [Installation](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/installation/).
- Your license key. See [Licensing & activation](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/).
- The flight controller connected to the companion computer over USB or a TELEM port, and powered.
- A camera connected (optional).
- A laptop with Mission Planner or QGroundControl on the **same network** as the drone. Note the laptop's IP address (`ipconfig` on Windows, `ip a` on Linux, **System Settings → Network** on macOS).

## 1. Activate the license

> You need a UAVcast-Pro license to activate the drone. Buy one in the UAVmatrix store.
>
> [Buy UAVcast-Pro](https://uavmatrix.com/checkout) · [See plans and pricing](https://uavmatrix.com/products)

1. Open `http://<drone-ip>` in a browser. You land on **Application**.
2. Paste your key into **Enter License Key** and select **Validate**.

The sidebar unlocks. Now go to **Users**, select **Add User** and create an admin account, so the web interface isn't open to anyone on the network.

## 2. Connect the flight controller

1. Go to **Flight Controller → Connection**.
2. Under **Link type**, pick **USB** or **UART / Serial** to match your wiring.
3. Leave **Port** and **Baud rate** on **Automatic**.
4. If the status panel says **Link stopped**, select **Connect**.
5. Wait for the state to change to **Connected**. **Mavlink Information** fills with the vehicle type, flight mode, GPS and battery, and the top bar shows **FC Connected**.

![Flight Controller Connection page showing Connected over USB, the Connection check with four passed steps, and the MAVLink Inspector](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/flight-controller.webp)

*Flight Controller → Connection with a working USB link.*

Stuck on **Waiting for device**, **Detecting baud rate** or **No heartbeat**? Select **Auto-detect** and read the **Connection check** panel: it names the first thing that's wrong. More in [Flight controller](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/).

## 3. Send telemetry and video to your laptop

1. Go to **Ground Control Stations**. There is already one empty destination card.
2. Enter a **Name**, for example `Laptop`.
3. In **Destination IP or Host**, enter your laptop's IPv4 address, for example `192.168.1.20`, and press Enter. A green check means it's saved.
4. Leave **Telemetry Port** at `14550` and **Video Port** at `5600`.
5. Turn on **Enable Telemetry**.
6. Turn on **Enable Video** if you have a camera.

Fields save as you leave them. There is no Save button.

## 4. Start the camera

Skip this if you have no camera.

1. Go to **Camera → Camera settings**.
2. Set **Enable Camera?** to **Yes**.
3. Click the **CAM 1** slot and choose your camera, for example *Raspberry Pi Camera - imx708 (CSI)* or your USB webcam.
4. Under **Camera Settings**, pick a **Resolution**. Start with `1280x720` or the closest size your camera offers.
5. Leave **Select FPS** on **Auto** and **Bitrate** at `0` (auto).
6. Under **Stream Settings**, tick **Enable Live Preview?** and select **Start**. **Live Preview** shows the picture.

## 5. Open your ground station

**QGroundControl**

QGroundControl listens on UDP 14550 by default, so the drone appears by itself within a few seconds.

For video: click the **Q** icon → **Application Settings** → **Video** (in older versions, the **Video** section of **General**). Set **Source** to **UDP h.264 Video Stream** and keep the default UDP port `5600`. The video shows in the Fly view.

**Mission Planner**

In the top-right corner choose **UDP**, select **Connect** and accept port `14550`.

![Mission Planner Flight Data view connected over UDP: the top-right connection box shows UDP, the link UDP14550-1-QUADRO and the DISCONNECT button; the HUD shows DISARMED, Unhealthy AHRS and GPS: No Fix](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/gcs/mission-planner--connected.webp)

*Mission Planner connected over UDP 14550: the connection box (top right) shows the link and DISCONNECT. Bench setup without GPS, hence Unhealthy AHRS and GPS: No Fix on the HUD.*

For video: right-click the HUD → **Video** → **Set GStreamer Source**, and paste:

```text
udpsrc port=5600 caps="application/x-rtp, media=video, clock-rate=90000, encoding-name=H264, payload=96" ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! video/x-raw,format=BGRA ! appsink name=outsink
```

Full walkthroughs with screenshots and fixes: [Mission Planner](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/mission-planner/), [QGroundControl](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/qgroundcontrol/), [Android](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/android/), and GStreamer on [Windows](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-windows/), [Linux](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-linux/) or [macOS](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-macos/).

> **Windows firewall**
>
> Windows blocks incoming UDP unless the app asked for an exception. If telemetry or video doesn't arrive, allow Mission Planner or QGroundControl through the firewall for **private and public** networks, or open UDP 14550 and 5600.

You now have telemetry and video on your local network. The dashboard's **Ground station** row reads *Sending · … packets/s*.

## 6. Fly over 4G/LTE

Over a cellular network the drone has no address your laptop can reach, so both join the same VPN. The Fleet Manager VPN is included with your license.

1. Plug in the modem. On **Modem**, set **Modem type** to **HiLink** or **Traditional (PPP)**. Leave **Access Point Name** empty: UAVcast-Pro finds the APN. See [Cellular modem](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/cellular-modem/).
2. Sign in to [Fleet Manager](https://fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/), open **Network** and select **Enable VPN Network** if it isn't on yet.
3. Pair the drone: in UAVcast-Pro, **Management → Fleet Management → Connect to Fleet Manager**, then enter the code in Fleet Manager under **Fleet → Pair Device**. Keep **Enable VPN for this UAV** ticked.
4. Put the laptop on the VPN: install Tailscale and run the **GCS Connection Command** from Fleet Manager's **Network** page, then mark the laptop as a **Ground Control Station (GCS)**.
5. In **Network → Stream Bindings**, add a binding from the drone to the laptop. Fleet Manager sends the destination to the drone, and the **Ports** column shows which ports to listen on.
6. On **Networks**, select **Modem Priority (Outdoor Mode)** so traffic goes over the modem when Wi-Fi drops.

Full walkthrough: [Fly beyond visual range over 4G](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/bvlos-4g/). Already run your own Tailscale or ZeroTier network? Join the drone and the laptop to it instead and use the laptop's VPN IP as the destination: see [VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/vpn/).

> **Set a GCS failsafe before flying over LTE**
>
> Cellular links drop. Make sure the flight controller has a GCS failsafe configured (`FS_GCS_ENABLE` on ArduPilot, `NAV_DLL_ACT` on PX4). The top bar shows **GCS Failsafe Enabled** or **GCS Failsafe Disabled**.

## Next steps

- [Two cameras, RC switching and dual stream](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/multi-camera/)
- [Record every flight on the drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/recordings/)
- [RTK corrections over 4G with NTRIP](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/ntrip-rtk/)
- [Pair the drone with Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/fleet-pairing/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/quick-start/

# Hardware requirements

> Which Raspberry Pi or Linux computer, flight controller, camera and 4G/LTE modem work with UAVcast-Pro, plus wiring, power and storage requirements.

UAVcast-Pro runs on a 64-bit Linux companion computer connected to any MAVLink flight controller (ArduPilot or PX4). Add a camera for video and a 4G/LTE modem for flights beyond Wi-Fi range. A Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 with a Pi camera and a USB modem is the most common setup.

## Companion computer

UAVcast-Pro installs on any **64-bit** Linux board or PC with an **arm64** or **amd64 (x86-64)** CPU running Raspberry Pi OS, Debian or Ubuntu. 32-bit systems (`armv7l`, `i686`) are not supported.

| Board | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Raspberry Pi 5 | Supported | No hardware H.264 encoder. Video is encoded in software, so watch the **System load** indicator on the Camera page with high resolutions or two streams. |
| Raspberry Pi 4 | Supported, recommended | Good balance of CPU, power draw and price. 2 GB RAM or more. |
| Raspberry Pi 3 / 3B+ | Supported | Fine for telemetry and one 720p stream. Installation takes about 30 minutes. |
| Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W | Supported | Smallest and lightest. Installation takes about 30 minutes; keep video modest. |
| Raspberry Pi Compute Module 3+/4 | Supported | Same as the matching Pi model. |
| NVIDIA Jetson, Orange Pi, Banana Pi and other arm64 boards | Supported | Use the vendor's 64-bit Ubuntu or Debian image. UAVcast-Pro recognises these boards and suggests their serial ports for the flight controller. Use a USB camera (Raspberry Pi CSI cameras need a Pi). |
| x86-64 PC (Intel NUC, mini PC, laptop) | Supported | Uses the amd64 build. USB serial adapters show up as `/dev/ttyUSB*` or `/dev/ttyACM*`. |

Run `uname -m` on the board to check the architecture. You want `aarch64` or `x86_64`.

> **Non-Raspberry Pi arm64 boards**
>
> Jetson, Orange Pi, Banana Pi and other arm64 boards that aren't a Raspberry Pi need UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3 or later. Older installers stop on them with *Device is not a Raspberry Pi*.

### Storage

- **Minimum 500 MB free** on the root disk, or the installer stops. An 8 GB or larger card is the practical minimum; use 32 GB or more if you record video on the drone.
- Use a good A1/A2-rated microSD card, or boot from SSD. Recordings can also go to a USB drive or SSD (see [Recordings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/recordings/)).

> **The license is tied to the storage device**
>
> UAVcast-Pro identifies a device by its CPU serial number plus the serial number of the boot disk (SD card or SSD). Moving to a new SD card counts as a new device. Unregister the old one first. See [Move your license to new hardware](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/#move-to-new-hardware).

### Power

The Raspberry Pi needs a stable **5.1 V** supply that can carry the Pi plus everything on its USB ports. A 4G modem can draw well over 500 mA when it transmits, and a USB camera adds more.

- Power the Pi from a dedicated 5 V BEC or regulator sized for the whole load. A flight controller's TELEM or USB port cannot power the Pi.
- If the modem browns out the Pi, power it from a powered USB hub or a separate 5 V supply.
- Check the **Power supply** row on the [Dashboard](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/dashboard/). *Voltage too low - use a stronger power supply* means the Pi is under-voltage right now. *Slowed down (heat or power)* means the CPU is throttling.

## Flight controller

UAVcast-Pro works with **any MAVLink flight controller**: ArduPilot (Copter, Plane, Rover, Sub) and PX4, on Pixhawk and Cube families, Matek, Holybro, CUAV, mRo and most other boards. MAVLink 2 is recommended.

Flight-mode names and the mode buttons (in the Flight Map and in Fleet Manager) use ArduPilot's modes for Copter, Plane, Rover and Sub. On a PX4 flight controller, telemetry, video, routing to ground stations, the map and the HUD work the same way; use your ground station to change PX4 flight modes.

Connect it in one of two ways:

| Link | Wiring | When to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **USB** | USB cable from the flight controller's USB port to the companion computer. | Easiest. No baud rate to set. Use a short, good-quality data cable. |
| **UART / Serial** | TELEM port TX → computer RX, RX → computer TX, GND → GND. Or a USB-serial (FTDI) cable. | When the USB port is used for something else, or for a cleaner install. Enable MAVLink on that port: `SERIALx_PROTOCOL = 2` (MAVLink2) on ArduPilot, `MAV_x_CONFIG` on PX4. |

**Raspberry Pi only:** the GPIO UART is `/dev/serial0` (GPIO 14 TX, GPIO 15 RX). The installer frees it for the flight controller: it disables the serial login console and, on Pi 3, 4 and Zero 2 W, moves Bluetooth off the UART. Never connect the flight controller's 5 V pin to the Pi when both have their own supply.

On other boards, use the board's UART (for example `ttyTHS*` on Jetson, `ttyS*` on Orange Pi) or a USB-serial adapter.

| Flight controller TELEM port | Raspberry Pi GPIO header |
| --- | --- |
| TX | GPIO 15 (RXD), pin 10 |
| RX | GPIO 14 (TXD), pin 8 |
| GND | GND, for example pin 6 |

TX always goes to RX. Leave the TELEM port's 5 V pin unconnected.

UAVcast-Pro finds the port and baud rate automatically. See [Connect the flight controller](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/).

## Cameras

| Camera | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Raspberry Pi camera modules (v1, v2, v3, HQ, Global Shutter) and other libcamera CSI cameras | Best latency. Raspberry Pi 5 and Compute Modules can run two CSI cameras. |
| USB (UVC) webcams such as Logitech C920 or C615 | Plug and play. Picked up as `/dev/video*`. |
| HDMI sources (GoPro, camera gimbals) | Through an HDMI-to-CSI bridge (shows up as a CSI camera) or a USB HDMI capture stick (shows up as a USB camera). |
| IP cameras and anything else GStreamer can read | Through a [custom pipeline](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/custom-pipeline/). |

Two cameras can run at the same time, either switched from an RC channel or streamed together. See [Two cameras and RC switching](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/multi-camera/). For audio, any USB microphone or a webcam with a built-in mic works. See [Audio](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/audio/).

## 4G/LTE modems

UAVcast-Pro supports two kinds of USB modem:

| Type | How it works | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **HiLink** | The modem is a small router. It shows up as a network card (usually `eth1` or `usb0`) and connects by itself. Nothing to configure in UAVcast-Pro. | Huawei E3372**h** (HiLink firmware), E8372, most "LTE USB dongle with web UI" sticks |
| **Traditional (PPP)** | Managed by ModemManager and NetworkManager. UAVcast-Pro connects it, finds the APN and reconnects after drops. | Huawei E3372**s** (stick firmware), Quectel EC25 / EG25 / EM06 and Sierra Wireless modules in a USB adapter |

Any modem on the [ModemManager supported devices list](https://www.freedesktop.org/wiki/Software/ModemManager/SupportedDevices/) should work as a Traditional modem. Use a SIM with a data plan for your region, and check whether your operator blocks inbound traffic (a VPN works around this). See [Cellular modem](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/cellular-modem/).

## Ground station computer

Any computer that runs Mission Planner, QGroundControl or another MAVLink ground station. It receives telemetry on UDP 14550 and video on UDP 5600 by default. For video in Mission Planner you need GStreamer installed; QGroundControl has it built in.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/hardware-requirements/


---

# Install UAVcast-Pro

> Install UAVcast-Pro with one command on a 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS, Debian or Ubuntu system (arm64 or amd64), then open the web interface and create an admin user.

Install in one command

```bash
curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | sudo bash
```

Run it on the companion computer (64-bit Raspberry Pi OS, Debian or Ubuntu, with internet). The steps below explain what it does and how to prepare the device.

> You need a UAVcast-Pro license to activate the drone. Buy one in the UAVmatrix store.
>
> [Buy UAVcast-Pro](https://uavmatrix.com/checkout) · [See plans and pricing](https://uavmatrix.com/products)

UAVcast-Pro installs with one command on any 64-bit, Debian-based Linux system: Raspberry Pi OS, Debian or Ubuntu, on arm64 or amd64. The installer downloads the latest release, installs its dependencies and services, and prints the address of the web interface when it's done. It takes about 10 minutes, or about 30 minutes on a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, 2 or 3.

## Before you begin

- A 64-bit OS on the companion computer. Check with `uname -m`: it must print `aarch64` or `x86_64`.
- At least 500 MB free on the root disk (`df -h /`).
- Internet access on the device during the install.
- SSH or a keyboard and screen on the device, and a user with `sudo` rights.

## Step 1: Flash the operating system

**Raspberry Pi**

1. Open [Raspberry Pi Imager](https://www.raspberrypi.com/software/) and choose your Pi model.
2. Choose **Raspberry Pi OS (64-bit)**. The **Lite** version is enough and leaves more CPU for video.
3. Open the OS customisation settings. Set a hostname, a username and password, your Wi-Fi network and country, and enable SSH.
4. Write the card, put it in the Pi and power it up.

Ubuntu Server 64-bit for Raspberry Pi also works.

**Other arm64 boards**

Flash the vendor's 64-bit Ubuntu or Debian image (for example JetPack's Ubuntu on NVIDIA Jetson), complete the first-boot setup and enable SSH.

Arm64 boards other than a Raspberry Pi need UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3 or later; older installers stop with *Device is not a Raspberry Pi*.

**x86-64 PC**

Install a 64-bit Debian or Ubuntu (Server or Desktop). The installer doesn't check the release version, so use a current, supported release, for example Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or newer.

Then log in over SSH and update the system:

```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt full-upgrade -y
```

## Step 2: Run the installer

On the drone:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | sudo bash
```

The installer:

1. Detects the architecture and downloads the matching release to `/opt/uavcast-pro`.
2. Installs the system packages it needs: NetworkManager, ModemManager, GStreamer, v4l-utils, Redis, Python and more.
3. On a Raspberry Pi, frees the GPIO UART for the flight controller (removes the serial console from `cmdline.txt`, moves Bluetooth off the UART) and raises the camera memory pool for two-camera setups. Your original `config.txt` and `cmdline.txt` are backed up first.
4. Installs ZeroTier, Tailscale, mavlink-router and MediaMTX.
5. Installs and starts the UAVcast-Pro services.
6. Checks that the key tools are present and prints the web address.

When it finishes you see:

```text
✅ Installation completed successfully!

Please reboot your device to complete the installation.

To access the UAVcast-Pro web interface, open your browser and navigate to:
http://192.168.1.50
```

Reboot so the UART and camera changes take effect:

```bash
sudo reboot
```

> **Let slow boards finish**
>
> On a Pi Zero 2 W the progress bar can sit still for minutes while apt works. Don't start a second install: the installer refuses to run twice and a second copy only slows the first one down. The full log is in `/opt/uavcast-pro/installer.log`.

### Install a specific version

List the versions available for your architecture:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | bash -s -- -l
```

Install one of them with `-b`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | sudo bash -s -- -b 6.5.2
```

You can also switch versions later from the web interface. See [Update UAVcast-Pro](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/updating/).

## Step 3: Open the web interface

On a computer on the same network, open a browser and go to the address the installer printed, for example `http://192.168.1.50`. The web interface runs on port **80**.

If you don't know the address:

- Try the hostname you set in Raspberry Pi Imager, for example `http://raspberrypi.local`. This needs mDNS, which works on most home networks and on macOS, Linux and Windows 10 or newer.
- Look for the device in your router's list of connected clients.
- On the device, run `hostname -I`.

The first page you see is **Application**, because UAVcast-Pro has no license yet. The sidebar stays greyed out (*Feature requires license*) until the device is licensed.

## Step 4: Activate your license

On **Application → License Manager**, paste your key into **Enter License Key** and select **Validate**. The device needs internet access for this. The full flow, device slots and moving a license are covered in [Licensing & activation](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/).

## Step 5: Create an admin user

A fresh install has **no users and no login**: anyone who can reach the web interface has full admin access. Create an admin account before the drone goes on a shared network or the internet.

1. Go to **Users** in the sidebar (under **Management**).
2. Select **Add User**.
3. Enter a **Username** (at least 3 characters) and a **Password** (at least 6 characters). The first user is always **Admin**.
4. Select **Create User**.

From now on the web interface asks for a login. Sessions last 7 days. See [Users & access](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/users/) for read-only accounts.

## What gets installed

| Item | Location |
| --- | --- |
| Application, binaries, database (`uavcast.db`), logs | `/opt/uavcast-pro` |
| Installer log | `/opt/uavcast-pro/installer.log` |
| systemd services | `uavcast-web`, `uavcast-factory`, `mavlink-manager`, `uavcast-camera`, `uavcast-ntrip`, `uavcast-dns`, `mediamtx`, `internet-check` |
| MAVLink router config | `/etc/mavlink-router/main.conf` (generated by UAVcast-Pro, don't edit) |

Check that the web service is running:

```bash
sudo systemctl status uavcast-web
```

## Uninstall

The installer binary has an uninstall mode. It stops and removes all UAVcast-Pro services, the settings database and the program files in `/opt/uavcast-pro`, and purges ZeroTier, Tailscale and Redis if UAVcast-Pro installed them. General packages such as NetworkManager, ModemManager and GStreamer stay.

```bash
sudo /opt/uavcast-pro/factory/ApplicationInstaller --uninstall
```

From UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3, flight recordings in `/opt/uavcast-pro/recordings` are kept. Add `--delete-recordings` to remove them too, or `--purge-deps` to also remove ZeroTier, Tailscale and Redis that were installed before UAVcast-Pro. On earlier versions, uninstalling deletes the whole `/opt/uavcast-pro` folder, recordings included, so copy recordings you want to keep first.

> **Unregister the license first**
>
> Uninstalling doesn't free the license slot. Unregister the device on **Application → License Manager** before you wipe it, or you can't free the slot without another device. See [Licensing & activation](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/#unregister-a-device).

## Upgrading from UAVcast-Pro 4.x or 5.x

Version 6 is a complete rewrite and can't import settings from 4.x or 5.x. Write down your ground station, camera and modem settings, flash a fresh 64-bit OS and install version 6.

If the installer reports *An older version of UAVcast-Pro has been detected at /opt/UAVcast-Pro*, remove it first. This deletes the old settings:

```bash
sudo rm -rf /opt/UAVcast-Pro
```

## If the install fails

| Message or symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| *No installation candidate for … found!* | The OS is 32-bit or the architecture isn't supported. Check `uname -m` and reflash with a 64-bit image. |
| *Not enough free space. … need 500MB* | Free space or use a bigger card. |
| *Another process is currently using the system package manager* | An automatic update is running. Wait a few minutes and run the installer again. |
| *Another installer is already running* | Let the first one finish. |
| *Installation completed with errors* with a red ✗ | Run the installer again. If it repeats, send `/opt/uavcast-pro/installer.log` to [support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com). |
| Web page doesn't load | Check `sudo systemctl status uavcast-web`, try the IP instead of the hostname, and make sure nothing else uses port 80. |

More fixes: [Installation fails](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/installation-fails/) and [Web interface won't open](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/web-interface-wont-open/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/installation/


---

# Licensing & activation

> How to buy a UAVcast-Pro license, activate it on a drone, check device slots, renew it, and move it to a new Raspberry Pi or SD card by unregistering the old device.

UAVcast-Pro needs an activated license key on every drone. You buy a license in the UAVmatrix store, paste the key into **Application → License Manager** on the drone and select **Validate**. Each license has a number of device slots. Activating a drone uses one slot; unregistering it frees the slot for another drone.

> You need a UAVcast-Pro license to activate the drone. Buy one in the UAVmatrix store.
>
> [Buy UAVcast-Pro](https://uavmatrix.com/checkout) · [See plans and pricing](https://uavmatrix.com/products)

## Buy a license

Licenses are sold at [uavmatrix.com/products](https://uavmatrix.com/products/). Every license includes updates for its whole period and [Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/), including its VPN for reaching the drone over 4G.

| Plan | Device slots | Valid for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Basic | 1 | 1 year |
| Silver | 2 | 1 year |
| Gold | 4 | 2 years |

The store page always shows the current plans and prices. There is no free trial license.

After payment you get an order confirmation email with the **license key**, five groups of four characters.

The key is also in your store account under **Licenses**, with its device slots and expiry date.

> **The license period starts at first activation**
>
> A license bought today and activated next month expires one period after the activation date, not the purchase date.

## Activate the license on a drone

The drone needs internet access while you activate it (Wi-Fi, Ethernet or the modem).

1. Open the UAVcast-Pro web interface. An unlicensed device always opens on **Application**.
2. In **License Manager**, paste the key into **Enter License Key**.
3. Select **Validate**. You see *License activated successfully* and the rest of the sidebar unlocks.

![UAVcast-Pro License Manager showing an active license with registered name, allowed and remaining devices, expiration date and the activated devices table](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/application--license-activated.webp)

*Application → License Manager after activation. The current device is marked Current in Activated Devices.*

**License Details** shows:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Registered Name** | The store account the license belongs to. |
| **License Status** | **Active**, **Inactive** or **Expired**. |
| **Allowed Devices** | Total device slots. |
| **Remaining Devices** | Free slots. |
| **Activation Date** / **Expiration Date** | When the license period started and ends. |

**Activated Devices** lists every drone on this license with its **Device Name**, **Hostname** and **Activation Date**. The drone you're on is marked **Current**. Select **Edit** to give a device a name you'll recognise.

### Activation errors

| Message | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| *Maximum activations reached. Please deactivate another device first or upgrade your license.* | All slots are in use. [Unregister a device](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/#unregister-a-device) or add slots. |
| *Invalid license key* | Check for typos or extra spaces. Copy the key from your store account. |
| *License already activated on this device* | Nothing to do. This device already has a slot (for example after a reinstall on the same SD card). |
| *Network error! Could not fetch license details…* | The device has no internet. Check **Networks** and try again. |

## How the license is checked

- The drone checks the license with the UAVmatrix license server every **4 hours**.
- If the server can't be reached, the drone keeps its last known status. You can fly with no internet connection at all; nothing locks while you're offline.
- A device is identified by its CPU serial number and the serial number of its boot disk (SD card or SSD). Reinstalling on the same Pi and the same card keeps the same identity and slot. A new SD card or SSD counts as a **new device**.
- The license data on the drone is encrypted with that identity, so a [database backup](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/application-settings/#database) restored onto other hardware needs the license activated again.

## Unregister a device

Unregistering frees a slot immediately. You can unregister **any** device on the license from **any** drone where the license is active, not only the drone you're on.

1. Go to **Application → License Manager → Activated Devices**.
2. Find the device and select **Unregister**. You see *Device unregistered successfully*.

If you unregister the drone you're working on, it becomes unlicensed and the web interface locks to the **Application** page until you activate a key again.

> **You can't unregister from the store**
>
> The store shows registered devices but can't remove them. Unregister from UAVcast-Pro on one of the license's devices. If every device on the license is lost or wiped, email [support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com) with your license key.

## Move to new hardware

Use this when you replace the Pi, swap the SD card, or move from a test bench to the aircraft.

1. On the **old** device, go to **Application → License Manager** and select **Unregister** next to it. Do this before you wipe the card.
2. Install UAVcast-Pro on the new hardware. See [Installation](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/installation/).
3. Activate the same key on the new device.

If the old device is dead, unregister it from another drone on the same license, or contact support.

## Renew or upgrade

From your store account, open the license and select **Upgrade Options**:

- **Extend subscription** adds another period. If the license is still valid, the new period is added to the current expiry date; if it has expired, it starts on the renewal date. The key stays the same.
- **Add devices** adds slots to the license. An expired license must be renewed first.
- **Upgrade tier** moves the license to a plan with more slots.

The drone picks up the new expiry date and slots at its next check, within 4 hours. To refresh it right away, select **Change** in **License Manager**, enter the same key and select **Validate**.

## When a license expires

> **An expired license locks UAVcast-Pro**
>
> When a license expires, UAVcast-Pro can no longer be used on any of its drones. It does not keep running on the installed version.

When the license server reports the license as expired, the drone marks itself unlicensed: the web interface only opens **Application**, and telemetry, video, NTRIP and Dynamic DNS stop at the next restart of their services. Renew the license before the expiry date to avoid downtime, and validate the key again on the drone (or wait for its next check, within 4 hours) to unlock it.

## Licenses and Fleet Manager

Fleet Manager is included with your UAVcast-Pro license and uses the same license. A drone can only be paired with an organization if its license belongs to a member of that organization. If you bought the license with a different email than the one you sign in to Fleet Manager with, add that email in Fleet Manager (see [Licenses in Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/)). See [Pair a drone with Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/fleet-pairing/).

Activation problems: see [License activation failed](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/license-activation-failed/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/


---

# Update UAVcast-Pro

> Update UAVcast-Pro from the web interface or the command line, install an older version, and what happens to your settings, server port and recordings.

Update UAVcast-Pro from **Application → Update Application** in the web interface, or by running the installer again over SSH. Both keep your settings, users, license and recordings. The drone needs internet access, and you must reboot when the update finishes.

> **Never update before a flight**
>
> An update stops all UAVcast-Pro services, including telemetry and video, and needs a reboot. Update on the ground with the aircraft disarmed.

## Update from the web interface

1. Go to **Application**. The **Update Application** card shows **Current Version** and **Latest Version**. A green *New version … available* banner appears when there is a newer release.
2. Leave **Select version to update** on the latest version, or pick another one.
3. Select **Update to …** (or **Update Now**). **Progress** shows the download and install steps. This takes a few minutes, longer on a Pi Zero 2 W or Pi 3.
4. When the **Pending Restart** banner appears, select **Restart Now**. The device reboots.
5. Open the web interface again and check **Current Version**.

![Update Application card with current and latest version, a New version available banner and the Update button](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/application--update-available.webp)

*Application → Update Application with a newer version available.*

## Update from the command line

Run the installer again. It replaces the program files and keeps the database:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | sudo bash
sudo reboot
```

To install a particular version, list the versions (no root needed), then install one with `-b`:

```bash
# List the versions available for this device
curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | bash -s -- -l

# Install a specific version
curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | sudo bash -s -- -b 6.5.1
```

## Go back to an older version

Pick the older version in **Select version to update** and update as usual, or use `-b` on the command line. Settings made in a newer version may not exist in the older one.

## What an update keeps and replaces

| Kept | Replaced |
| --- | --- |
| Settings database (`/opt/uavcast-pro/uavcast.db`): ground stations, camera, modem, VPN, users, license | Program files in `/opt/uavcast-pro` (`build`, `dist`, `factory`, `install`) |
| Recordings and telemetry logs | systemd service files |
| ZeroTier and Tailscale membership | System packages UAVcast-Pro depends on (updated by apt) |

From UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3, a custom **Server Port** set on the Application page is kept when you update. Earlier versions reset it to 80: after updating from one of them, open the web interface on port 80 and save your port again.

## See what changed

Each release is listed with its changes in the [changelog](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/changelog/). Read it before updating a drone that flies operationally.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/updating/

# UAVcast-Pro

> Reference for the UAVcast-Pro web interface: dashboard, flight controller, flight map, ground stations, camera, modem, VPN, Fleet Manager pairing, users and settings.

This section explains every page of the UAVcast-Pro web interface, in the order of the app's sidebar. Each page tells you what the screen is for, how to set it up, and lists every setting with its default. New to UAVcast-Pro? Start with the [Quick start](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/quick-start/).

## Operations

[DashboardHealth of the flight controller, GPS, links, video and power at a glance.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/dashboard/)[Data StreamsCustom live dashboards for any MAVLink or sensor value.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/data-streams/)[Flight ControllerUSB or UART link with automatic port and baud detection, NTRIP/RTK and injectors.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/)[Flight MapLive map, cockpit HUD, arm/disarm, modes, missions, radio, inspector and log analysis.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-map/)[Ground stations and videoDestinations, plus step-by-step Mission Planner, QGroundControl, GStreamer, Android and VLC setup.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/)

## Connectivity

[ModemHiLink and traditional 4G/LTE modems with automatic APN.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/cellular-modem/)[Virtual Private NetworkThe Fleet Manager VPN, or your own Tailscale or ZeroTier network.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/vpn/)[Dynamic DNSKeep a hostname pointed at the drone's public IP.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/dynamic-dns/)[NetworksInterfaces and Wi-Fi vs modem priority.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/networks/)

## Media

[Camera settingsCSI and USB cameras, resolution, bitrate, low-latency H.264 over UDP.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/)[Two camerasRC channel switching or dual stream.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/multi-camera/)[AudioMicrophone audio in the preview and to ground stations.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/audio/)[RecordingsOn-drone video and telemetry recording with flight review.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/recordings/)

## Management

[Fleet ManagementPair the drone with UAVmatrix Fleet Manager.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/fleet-pairing/)[UsersAdmin login and read-only users.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/users/)[ApplicationPort, language, logs for support, database backup and restore.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/application-settings/)

## Ports at a glance

| Port | Direction | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TCP 80 | Browser → drone | Web interface (configurable) and HTTP injectors |
| UDP 14550 | Drone → ground station | MAVLink telemetry (per destination, configurable) |
| UDP 5600 | Drone → ground station | Video, camera 1 (per destination, configurable) |
| UDP 5601 | Drone → ground station | Video, camera 2 with dual stream (Video Port + 1 by default) |
| UDP 5602 | Drone → ground station | Audio (Video Port + 2) |
| TCP 8889, UDP 8189 | Browser → drone | Live preview (WebRTC signalling and media) |
| TCP 8883 | Drone → Fleet Manager | Fleet Manager connection (MQTT over TLS) |
| TCP 2101 | Drone → NTRIP caster | RTK corrections (caster's port) |
| UDP 14600 | Sensor → drone | UDP injector (default, configurable) |

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/

# Dashboard

> Read the UAVcast-Pro dashboard to check the flight controller, GPS, battery, ground station link, cellular, VPN, RTK, video and Raspberry Pi power, temperature and throttling.

The dashboard is the pre-flight checklist for the companion computer. One status card tells you whether the flight controller, GPS, battery, ground station link, modem, VPN, RTK, video and power supply are healthy, with a summary such as *All systems normal* or *2 problems*. Below it you find system information, network traffic, memory and storage. Open **Dashboard** in the sidebar.

![UAVcast-Pro dashboard with the status card showing 2 problems, system information with temperature, and the network traffic chart](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/dashboard.webp)

*Dashboard on a bench unit: two problems (no GPS fix, VPN not connected), system information and network traffic.*

## Status card

The card has three groups. Each row has a coloured dot: green is fine, amber is a warning, red is a problem.

| Row | Example values | What to do if it's not green |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Flight controller** | *Armed*, *Disarmed*, *Link stopped*, *Connecting…* | See [Flight controller](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/). |
| **GPS** | *3D fix · 14 satellites*, *RTK fixed*, *No fix*, *No GPS* | Wait for a fix outdoors, or check the GPS wiring. |
| **Battery** | voltage and percentage | Charge or check the flight controller's battery monitor setup. |
| **Ground station** | *Sending to 2 · 16 packets/s*, *Not sending*, *1 set up · waiting for flight controller*, *None set up* | See [Ground control stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/). |
| **Cellular** | operator and signal, *No modem detected* | See [Cellular modem](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/cellular-modem/). |
| **VPN** | *Connected*, *Not connected*, *Turned off* | See [VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/vpn/). |
| **RTK corrections** | *Connecting…*, *Error - check settings*, *Turned off* | See [NTRIP / RTK](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/ntrip-rtk/). |
| **Video** | *Running*, *Stopped*, *Turned off* | See [Camera](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/). |
| **Dynamic DNS** | *Running*, *Turned off* | See [Dynamic DNS](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/dynamic-dns/). |
| **Power supply** | *Stable*, *Voltage too low - use a stronger power supply*, *Slowed down (heat or power)*, *Voltage dropped since start-up* | See [Power](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/dashboard/#power-and-temperature). |

*Service failed - restarting* on any row means the service crashed and is being restarted automatically. If it keeps showing, download the logs from **Application → Logging**.

## Power and temperature

On a Raspberry Pi, **System Information** shows **Power**, **CPU throttling** and **Temperature**:

- **Voltage too low - use a stronger power supply**: the Pi is under-voltage right now. This causes USB resets, so the modem or flight controller can drop out. Fix the supply before flying.
- **Voltage dropped since start-up**: it happened at some point since boot. Often caused by the modem's transmit peaks.
- **Slowed down (heat or power)**: the CPU is throttled. Video encoding suffers first. Add a heatsink or airflow, or fix the supply.

The temperature bar turns red as the Pi approaches its throttling point.

## Other cards

| Card | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| **System Information** | **Operating System**, **Hardware** (CPU and cores), **Uptime**, power and **Temperature**. |
| **Network Traffic** | Received and transmitted totals and rates per interface. Choose **Last 50** to **Last 1000** samples. Handy for checking how much the video uses on the modem. |
| **Memory Usage** | **Total**, **Used** and **Free**. Data is collected every 10 seconds. |
| **Storage** | **Total**, **Used** and **Free** per partition. |

The charts need a few minutes of data after boot before they show anything.

## Guided tour

The first time you open the web interface, a tour offers to walk you through the main pages. You can **Skip Tour** or choose **Never Show Again**. Start it again from **Application → Settings → Take a Tour**.

Power problems in detail: [Under-voltage and throttling](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/undervoltage-and-throttling/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/dashboard/

# Data Streams

> Create UAVcast-Pro Data Streams dashboards with charts, gauges and tiles for any MAVLink field or NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT sensor value, with thresholds, history and JSON import/export.

Data Streams lets you build your own live telemetry dashboards. Add numeric tiles, line charts, gauges, bars and status lights, and bind each one to any MAVLink value the flight controller sends or any `NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT` signal from a sensor or [injector](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/injectors/). Dashboards are stored on the drone, so everyone who opens the web interface sees the same boards. Open **Data Streams** in the sidebar.

Typical uses: a payload operator's screen with sensor readings, an LTE link panel with RSRP and SINR, or a battery and power board for long flights.

![Data Streams page with No dashboards yet and the Create dashboard button](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/mission-data.webp)

*Data Streams before the first dashboard: Create dashboard starts one.*

## Create a dashboard

1. Select **Create dashboard** (or **New dashboard** if you already have one), give it a **Name** and select **Create**.
2. Select **Edit** to enter edit mode, then **Add widget** and pick a type.
3. On the **Source** tab, search for a signal and pick it. A green dot means samples are arriving.
4. Set the title, units and decimals on **Display**, limits and colour thresholds on **Range**, and chart options on **Chart**. Select **Save**.
5. Drag and resize widgets, then select **Done**.

Only admins can create and edit dashboards. Read-only users can view them.

## Widget types

| Type | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Numeric tile** | The current value, large, with optional prefix and suffix. |
| **Sparkline** | A small trend line under the value. |
| **Line chart** | One or more signals over a time window. |
| **Gauge** | The value on a round scale with coloured thresholds. |
| **Bar indicator** | The value as a bar between min and max. |
| **Status** | A coloured state from thresholds, for example OK / warning / alarm. |
| **Named-value table** | Every `NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT` signal with **Value**, **Age** and **Src**. **Filter** accepts a substring or a `*.glob`. |

A widget shows **Stale** when no sample has arrived for 5 seconds, and *No samples yet* when the signal has never been seen.

## Signals

- **MAVLink fields**: every numeric field the flight controller sends (attitude, VFR HUD, battery, GPS, home, RTK, failsafe, heartbeat and status values) appears automatically, with friendly names and units where known.
- **Named values**: `NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT` signals, shown as `NAME@sysid:compid`, for example `LTE_RSRP@1:194`.

You can type a signal that isn't sending yet and press Enter to add it, so you can build the board before you wire up the sensor. Use the pencil icon on a selected source to give it a display name.

## Chart options

| Option | Values |
| --- | --- |
| **Window** | **1 min**, **5 min**, **15 min**, **1 hour**, or **Custom (seconds)** |
| **Curve** | **Linear**, **Smooth (monotone)**, **Step**, **Step before**, **Step after**, **Basis spline** |
| Other | **Show legend**, **Show grid**, **Line width**, **Area fill**, **Show data points**, **Threshold reference lines**, **Y-axis label** |

## History

UAVcast-Pro keeps a short history of every signal on the drone (up to 3600 samples per signal, about one hour at 1 Hz), so charts are filled as soon as you open a dashboard, even after a page refresh.

## Share dashboards

- **Export JSON** copies the dashboard to the clipboard.
- **Import JSON** creates a dashboard from pasted JSON. Use it to copy a board to another drone.
- **Duplicate** and **Rename** are in the toolbar; **Delete** removes a dashboard and its widgets.
- **Fullscreen** hides the rest of the interface, for a dedicated monitor.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/data-streams/


---

# Connect the flight controller

> Connect a Pixhawk or any other ArduPilot or PX4 flight controller to UAVcast-Pro over USB or UART, with automatic port and baud detection and a live connection check.

UAVcast-Pro reads MAVLink from your flight controller (ArduPilot, PX4 or any other MAVLink autopilot) over USB or a UART (TELEM port) and forwards it to every ground station you add. With **Port** and **Baud rate** on **Automatic**, the default, it finds the flight controller by itself, remembers what worked and reconnects after a reboot, USB glitch or late power-up. You'll find it under **Flight Controller → Connection**.

![Flight Controller Connection page showing Connected, the Connection check with four passed steps, and the MAVLink Inspector](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/flight-controller.webp)

*Flight Controller → Connection with a USB link to a Pixhawk.*

## Connect over USB

1. Plug the flight controller's USB port into the companion computer with a data-capable cable.
2. Go to **Flight Controller → Connection** and select **USB** under **Link type**.
3. Leave **Port** on **Automatic**. USB connections don't use a baud rate.
4. If the status panel says **Link stopped**, select **Connect**.

Within a few seconds the status reads **CONNECTED** with the vehicle type and system ID, for example *Connected to Quadrotor (system 1) on ArduPilot fmuv2 (ttyACM0)*.

## Connect over a TELEM port (UART)

1. Wire the TELEM port: flight controller **TX → RX** on the companion computer, **RX → TX**, and **GND → GND**. Don't connect 5 V if both boards have their own supply.
2. On the flight controller, set the port to MAVLink 2: for TELEM2 that's `SERIAL2_PROTOCOL = 2`. Note `SERIAL2_BAUD`.
3. In UAVcast-Pro, select **UART / Serial** under **Link type**.
4. Leave **Port** and **Baud rate** on **Automatic**, or pick the port (on a Raspberry Pi the GPIO UART is marked **recommended**) and the baud rate that matches `SERIALx_BAUD`.
5. Select **Connect** if the link is stopped.

Changes apply immediately. You don't need to restart anything.

> **Automatic baud rate**
>
> In automatic mode UAVcast-Pro tries 57600, 115200, 921600, 1500000, 460800, 230400 and 500000 baud, starting with the last rate that worked. If heartbeats stop for 20 seconds while data still arrives (for example after you change `SERIALx_BAUD`), it searches again.

## Settings reference

| Setting | Default | Values | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Link enabled** | On | On, off | Off releases the serial port and stops telemetry to all ground stations. |
| **Link type** | **USB** | **USB**, **UART / Serial** | Decides which ports **Automatic** searches. |
| **Port** | **Automatic** | **Automatic**, a detected port, **Custom path…** | Automatic prefers the stable `/dev/serial/by-id/…` path and follows the device if its number changes. Custom path takes any device such as `/dev/ttyAMA0`. Ports used by another program show *in use by …*. |
| **Baud rate** | **Automatic** | **Automatic** or a fixed rate | Ignored for USB. Must match `SERIALx_BAUD` when fixed. |

## Read the status panel

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Connected** | Heartbeats are arriving. **Connected for**, **Last heartbeat** and **Auto-reconnects** show the link's health. |
| **Waiting for device** | The port doesn't exist. The flight controller is unplugged, unpowered or still booting. |
| **Detecting baud rate** | Trying baud rates (*Trying 115200 baud (2 of 7)*). |
| **No heartbeat** | The port is open but no valid MAVLink arrives: wrong baud rate, TX/RX swapped, or the port isn't set to MAVLink. |
| **Reconnecting** | The link dropped and is coming back by itself. |
| **Searching** | **Auto-detect** is scanning every port and speed. This can take up to a minute. |
| **Off** / **Stopped** | The link is turned off or stopped. Select **Connect**. |

### Connection check

The **Connection check** card, updated every second, follows the data from the wire to the ground station. The first row that isn't green is the problem:

1. **Flight controller plugged in** (USB) or **Serial port available** (UART). *Not detected* usually means a charge-only USB cable or no power.
2. **Signal on the wire**: bytes arrive on the port.
3. **Readable flight controller data**: bytes decode as MAVLink. *% damaged* points to a loose or long wire, a missing ground or noise from power cables.
4. **Flight controller responding**: heartbeats from the vehicle.
5. **Sending to ground station**: packets per second to each enabled destination, or *No ground station set up*.

### Auto-detect

**Auto-detect** pauses the link, listens on every serial port at every baud rate, saves the port and speed it finds and starts the link with them. Use it when you don't know which port or baud rate the flight controller uses. **Show what was tried** lists every attempt.

## Mavlink Inspector panel

The right-hand column shows the live vehicle state: connection, **GCS Failsafe Information**, **Vehicle Information** (type, controller, flight mode, armed), **Battery Status**, **GPS Information** and flight data. If the panel shows **Warning - Failsafe Disabled**, the flight controller has no GCS failsafe. Enable it (`FS_GCS_ENABLE` on ArduPilot) before flying over a cellular link.

## Security: no open telemetry port

UAVcast-Pro doesn't accept incoming telemetry connections. The TCP server on port 5760 that mavlink-router normally opens is turned off, so only ground stations you add on [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/) get telemetry, and only while **Enable Telemetry** is on.

> **Coming from an older version**
>
> Earlier versions defaulted to `/dev/ttyACM0` at 57600 baud and accepted TCP connections on port 5760. Since v6.4.3 every device moves to **Automatic** once, with the old port and baud tried first. Since v6.5.0, TCP 5760 is closed: add your PC as a ground station and connect over UDP instead.

## Related

- [NTRIP / RTK corrections](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/ntrip-rtk/)
- [Injectors: send your own sensor data into MAVLink](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/injectors/)
- [Ground control stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/)
- [Troubleshooting: no MAVLink heartbeat](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/

# NTRIP / RTK corrections

> Stream RTCM3 corrections from an NTRIP caster over 4G/LTE to your flight controller for RTK Fixed positioning. Caster, mountpoint, VRS and GGA settings.

UAVcast-Pro has a built-in NTRIP client. It connects to an NTRIP v1 or v2 caster over the drone's internet link, receives RTCM3 corrections and passes them to the flight controller as MAVLink `GPS_RTCM_DATA`, the same way Mission Planner's "Inject GPS" does, but from the drone itself. You don't need a ground station or base station on site. Open it under **Flight Controller → NTRIP / RTK**.

## Before you begin

- An RTK-capable GPS on the flight controller: a multi-frequency, carrier-phase receiver such as u-blox F9P, Holybro H-RTK, CUAV C-RTK, Here3+ or Septentrio Mosaic. A standard M8/M10 GPS ignores corrections.
- An account with an NTRIP caster: a national CORS network, a commercial service (Trimble, Hexagon, Topcon and others) or [RTK2go](http://rtk2go.com/). You need the host, port, mountpoint, and usually a username and password.
- Internet on the drone and a connected flight controller.

## Set up the NTRIP client

1. Go to **Flight Controller → NTRIP / RTK**.
2. Under **Caster**, enter **Caster host** (for example `ntrip.example.com`) and **Port** (`2101` for most casters).
3. Enter **Username** and **Password** under **Authentication**. Select **Test connection** to check them: *Caster accepted the credentials.*
4. Select **Browse mountpoints**, pick the nearest one in the list and select **Select**. Or type it in **Mountpoint**.
5. If the mountpoint is a VRS or "nearest base" stream (the **NMEA** column says **Required**), keep **Send GGA upstream** on.
6. Turn on **Enable NTRIP client**.

The **Status** card changes to **Streaming corrections** and shows **Total received**, **Throughput**, **Last RTCM frame** and **Recent message types**. With a clear sky, **Flight controller RTK fix** goes from **3D fix** to **RTK Float** and then **RTK Fixed**, usually within a minute or two.

![NTRIP / RTK tab with the status panel showing Disabled and zero counters, and the GPS quality card](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/flight-controller--ntrip.webp)

*Flight Controller → NTRIP / RTK before a caster is set up: status Disabled, counters at zero and no GPS fix.*

## Settings reference

| Setting | Default | Values | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Enable NTRIP client** | Off | On, off |  |
| **Caster host** | empty | hostname or IP | Required. |
| **Port** | `2101` | 1–65535 | Some TLS casters use 2102 or 443. |
| **Mountpoint** | empty | caster's mountpoint name | Required. Use **Browse mountpoints** to read the caster's sourcetable. |
| **Use TLS (HTTPS)** | Off | On, off | For casters that require TLS. Most public casters use plain TCP. |
| **Username** / **Password** | empty |  | Leave empty for anonymous casters. RTK2go wants a real email address as username and no password. |
| **Send GGA upstream** | On | On, off | Sends your position as NMEA `$GPGGA` so VRS and nearest-mountpoint casters can make corrections for your location. |
| **Send interval (seconds)** | `10` | seconds | How often GGA is sent. |
| **Position source** | **Live position from flight controller** | **Live position from flight controller**, **Fixed manual position** |  |
| **Latitude** / **Longitude** / **Altitude (m)** | `0` |  | Manual position. Also used as a fallback until the flight controller has a GPS fix. |

## Read the GPS quality card

**GPS quality** shows the live fix from the flight controller plus a measurement that doesn't rely on the receiver's own estimate:

- **Fix type** and **Satellites**.
- **Horizontal accuracy** and **Vertical accuracy**: the receiver's own estimate.
- **Position stability (1σ)**: how much the position actually moves while the drone stands still, measured over a short window. It shows **Moving** in flight.
- **Last correction**: time since the last RTCM frame was forwarded. If this keeps growing, corrections have stopped.

If you see **No RTK status from receiver**, the flight controller has never reported RTK status. Usually the GPS isn't RTK-capable. Corrections are still forwarded.

## Over a cellular link

Corrections are small (typically 1 to 5 kbit/s), so they fit easily next to telemetry and video. After a short internet drop the client reconnects within seconds. A silent caster connection is detected within 15 seconds and reopened.

The [Dashboard](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/dashboard/) shows the client's state in the **RTK corrections** row.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Status **Error**, **Caster response** shows `401` | Wrong username or password, or the account isn't allowed on this mountpoint. |
| **Connected**, but no RTCM frames | The mountpoint needs GGA. Turn on **Send GGA upstream** and make sure the flight controller has a 3D fix, or set a manual position. |
| RTCM arrives, fix stays at **3D fix** | The GPS isn't RTK-capable, or the mountpoint's GNSS systems don't match your receiver. Check the **GNSS** column in the sourcetable. |
| **RTK Float**, never **Fixed** | Base too far away (aim for under 20 to 30 km), poor sky view or multipath. Try a closer mountpoint. |

The **NTRIP service log** at the bottom of the page shows every connect, reconnect and caster reply.

More checks: [RTK corrections not arriving](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/rtk-corrections-not-arriving/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/ntrip-rtk/


---

# Injectors

> Use UAVcast-Pro injectors to push sensor readings from scripts, Arduinos or the LTE modem into the MAVLink stream over HTTP, UDP or serial, so QGC and Mission Planner see them.

An injector feeds data from outside UAVcast-Pro, such as a Python script, an Arduino or a sensor on the network, into the MAVLink stream as `NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT` (or `NAMED_VALUE_INT`) messages. Every connected ground station receives the values as normal telemetry: Mission Planner shows them in the **Status** tab and QGroundControl in the MAVLink Inspector. They also appear automatically in [Data Streams](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/data-streams/) dashboards. Open **Flight Controller → Injectors**.

Typical uses: radiation, gas or weather sensors on the companion computer, LTE signal values (RSRP, SINR) for link monitoring, or values your own scripts compute.

## Pick a transport

| Type | How data arrives | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **HTTP** | POST JSON to a unique URL with a secret token | Easiest. Anything that can make an HTTP request. |
| **UDP** | Packets to a port on the drone, as `NAME=VALUE` lines or JSON | Lowest overhead, trusted local networks. No authentication. |
| **Serial** | Lines read from a `/dev/tty*` device | Hard-wired sensors such as an Arduino over USB. |

The type can't be changed after you create the injector.

## Create an injector

1. Go to **Flight Controller → Injectors** and select **Add injector**.
2. Enter a **Name** (only shown in the UI) and pick the **Input type**.
3. Keep **MAVLink sysid** `1` so the values belong to the same vehicle as the flight controller, and **MAVLink compid** `194` (user payload) unless you need something else.
4. Optional: set a **Name prefix**, for example `BAL_`, so `RAD1` is sent as `BAL_RAD1`.
5. For UDP or Serial, fill in the listener settings. Then select **Create**.
6. Select **Send test signal** on the injector's card to send a value and check it in your ground station.

![Injectors tab with No injectors yet, typical uses, the HTTP, UDP and Serial transports and the Add injector button](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/flight-controller--injectors.webp)

*Flight Controller → Injectors before the first injector: typical uses and the three transports.*

## Send data

**HTTP**

After you create an HTTP injector, its card shows the **HTTP endpoint**. The URL has the form `http://<drone-ip>/api/inject/<token>` and goes through the normal web interface port. **Copy URL** copies it.

```bash
curl -X POST http://192.168.1.50/api/inject/<token> \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"RAD1","value":0.077}'
```

```bash
curl -X POST http://192.168.1.50/api/inject/<token> \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"samples":[{"name":"TEMP","value":21.4},{"name":"HUM","value":48}]}'
```

The reply counts what happened: `{"accepted":2,"rateLimited":0,"rejected":0}`. The token is the only protection. If it leaks, select **Rotate token** and update your client.

**UDP**

The injector listens on **Port** `14600` and **Bind address** `0.0.0.0` (all interfaces) by default. Use `127.0.0.1` if the sender runs on the drone itself.

```bash
echo "RAD1=0.077" | nc -u -w1 192.168.1.50 14600
```

```python
import json, socket
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
s.sendto(json.dumps({"name": "RAD1", "value": 0.077}).encode(), ("192.168.1.50", 14600))
```

**Serial**

The injector reads newline-terminated lines from **Device path** (default `/dev/ttyUSB0`) at **Baud rate** (default `115200`). Each line is one sample: `NAME=VALUE` for the Key=Value protocol, or a JSON object. It reconnects by itself if the device is unplugged.

```cpp
void setup() { Serial.begin(115200); }
void loop() {
  Serial.print("LIGHT=");
  Serial.println(analogRead(A0));
  delay(200);
}
```

> **MAVLink names are 10 characters**
>
> `NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT` names are limited to 10 characters, prefix included. Keep the prefix short (up to 8 characters) and the names compact.

## Settings reference

| Setting | Default | Values | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Name** | empty | text | Label in the UI only. |
| **Input type** | **HTTP** | **HTTP**, **UDP**, **Serial** | Fixed after creation. |
| **Enabled** | On | On, off | Off keeps the configuration but stops the listener. |
| **MAVLink sysid** | `1` | 1–255 | Same as the flight controller groups the values with that vehicle. |
| **MAVLink compid** | `194` | 0–255 | 194 is common for user payload sensors. |
| **Name prefix** | empty | up to 8 ASCII characters | Added in front of every signal name. |
| **Rate limit (Hz per signal)** | `10` | samples per second | Extra samples are dropped and counted as **Rate-limited**. Protects the link from a runaway sender. |
| **Protocol** (UDP, Serial) | **Key=Value (line-delimited)** | **Key=Value (line-delimited)**, **JSON** (`{name, value}`) |  |
| **Port** (UDP) | `14600` | 1–65535 |  |
| **Bind address** (UDP) | `0.0.0.0` | IP address | `127.0.0.1` accepts only local senders. |
| **Device path** (Serial) | `/dev/ttyUSB0` | device path | Run `ls /dev/tty*` to find it. |
| **Baud rate** (Serial) | `115200` |  | Must match the sender. |

Each card shows **Accepted**, **Rate-limited** and **Rejected** counters, so you can see whether data arrives and whether it's valid.

Injectors run inside the UAVcast-Pro services and start at boot, so values keep flowing without the web interface open.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/injectors/


---

# Flight Map

> Track your drone live on the UAVcast-Pro Flight Map with a cockpit HUD, video windows, arm/disarm, flight modes, RTL, loiter, GCS failsafe and flight controller messages.

The Flight Map is a browser-based ground station built into UAVcast-Pro. It shows the drone on a map with its trail, the active mission and home position, a cockpit HUD, live video, and the flight controller's messages. You can arm and disarm, change flight mode, start a mission and trigger RTL or loiter, all behind confirmation dialogs. Open **Flight Map → Map view**.

It's meant for monitoring and simple commands from any phone, tablet or laptop. For full mission planning and parameter work, keep using Mission Planner or QGroundControl alongside it.

![Flight Map with the map, the cockpit HUD on the right and the Status tab with link, battery, flight controller, telemetry, GPS and attitude cards](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/flight-map.webp)

*Flight Map → Map view on a bench unit without a GPS fix, so the map shows no drone position.*

## Layout

- **Map** (left): the drone with heading, trail, home marker and mission. **Sats** shows the satellite count; **Auto-Pan** keeps the drone centred. Switch layers with the layer button (**Street Map**, **Satellite** and others). If the drone has no fix you see **No GPS Lock**: *At least 4 satellites required*.
- **Top bar**: the **Recording** buttons (**Telemetry**, **CAM 1**, **CAM 2**), free recording space, the telemetry update rate (**1 Hz** to **10 Hz**), the current data rate, and a button that opens the map in its own window.
- **Cockpit** (right): an attitude HUD with speed and altitude tapes, the current flight mode, the arm state, battery voltage and the latest pre-arm message.
- **Side tabs**: **Status**, **Gauge**, **Actions**, **Messages** and **Recordings**. Drag the panel edge to resize it; double-click the handle to reset.
- **Video windows**: one per active camera stream. Drag, maximize, minimize or hide them; hidden windows dock as tabs at the bottom of the map.

The top bar across every page also shows **FC Connected**, **Armed**/**Disarmed**, the vehicle type, the flight mode, and **GCS Failsafe Enabled** or **GCS Failsafe Disabled**.

## Arm and disarm

1. Open the **Actions** tab, or use the arm control under the cockpit.
2. Select **Arm**. The dialog warns *The propellers can start spinning. Make sure nobody is near the drone and the area around it is clear.*
3. Confirm with **Arm**.

The flight controller's own pre-arm checks still decide. If it refuses, you see *The drone refused to arm. Check the PreArm message on the screen.* The reason appears under the cockpit and in **Messages**.

**Disarm** stops the motors immediately. The flight controller refuses it while the drone is flying.

## Change flight mode

Pick a mode from the flight mode control. The list matches the vehicle type (Copter, Plane, Rover, Sub) and is grouped into **Safe Modes** (position hold and stabilization), **Navigation** (autonomous modes) and **Advanced** (manual and emergency modes). Modes with a higher risk are marked with a warning icon and ask for confirmation before the command is sent.

## Actions tab

| Group | Buttons | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Mission** | **Read**, **Hide**, **Start**, **Clear** | **Read** loads the mission from the flight controller onto the map. **Start** starts it (with confirmation). **Clear** deletes the mission from the flight controller and waits for its confirmation. |
| **Modes** | **Loiter Unl**, **RTL** | Quick mode changes. |
| **Pre Flight** | **Pre Flight Calibration**, **Load Mission**, **Clear Mission** | Calibration runs the flight controller's ground calibration (gyro, baro). Only on the ground. |
| **Emergency Commands** | **Return To Launch**, **Loiter Unlimited** | Behind a confirmation. RTL returns and lands or loiters per the flight controller's settings. Loiter Unlimited circles at the current position. |
| **Failsafe** | **GCS failsafe** switch | Writes `FS_GCS_ENABLE` (Copter) and `FS_GCS_ENABL` (Plane) on the flight controller. |

> **Turn on GCS failsafe for cellular flights**
>
> The GCS failsafe triggers when the flight controller stops receiving MAVLink heartbeats from a ground station. Over 4G/LTE the link can drop at any time. Configure what the failsafe does (`FS_GCS_ENABLE` action, `FS_GCS_TIMEOUT`) in your ground station before you rely on it.

Read-only users see the Actions tab but can't use it (*Read-only users can't control the drone*).

## Messages

**Messages** lists every text message from the flight controller. **Active alerts** shows the current problems (for example pre-arm failures) separately from the **Message log**. Turn on **Problems only** to hide routine messages, and **Clear the log** to start fresh. The tab shows a badge with the number of active alerts.

## Status and Gauge tabs

- **Status**: cards for **LINK** (packet loss, connected), **FLIGHT CONTROLLER** (armed, mode, vehicle), telemetry data rate, position, **GPS** (lock, satellites, **ALTITUDE (AGL)**, **ALTITUDE (AMSL)**) and **BATTERY**.
- **Gauge**: round instruments for the same data.

AGL is the height above the takeoff point; AMSL is above mean sea level.

## Map settings

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Auto-Pan** | Keeps the drone in the centre of the map. |
| **Show Aircraft Heading** | Draws a heading line from the drone. |
| **Trail Length** | Number of points kept in the flight path trail. |
| **Trail Color** | Colour of the trail. **Clear Trail Path** removes it. |
| **Show Distance from Home** | Shows the distance to the home marker. |
| **Reset to Defaults** | Restores all map settings. |

## Pop-out windows

- **Flight map window**: the button at the right of the top bar opens the map alone in a new window (`/flightmapwindow`), sized for a second monitor.
- **HUD window**: from the cockpit, open the HUD in its own window (`/hud`).

![Cockpit HUD with attitude indicator, speed and altitude tapes, heading and flight mode](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/hud.webp)

*The cockpit HUD at /hud. The horizon is upside down here because this bench unit's flight controller is mounted inverted.*

## Telemetry update rate

The rate selector in the top bar (**1 Hz**, **2 Hz**, **5 Hz**, **10 Hz**) sets how often UAVcast-Pro pushes telemetry to the browser. It doesn't change what your ground stations receive. Use a low rate on a slow connection to the web interface.

## Related

- [Mission Planner tab](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-map/mission-planner/)
- [Radio (RC channels)](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-map/radio/)
- [MAVLink Inspector](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-map/inspector/)
- [Flight Analytics](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-map/flight-analytics/)
- [Recordings and flight review](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/recordings/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-map/
