# Mission Planner tab

> Plan a waypoint mission in the UAVcast-Pro Mission Planner tab, set altitude frame and radius, save it as a .waypoints file and upload it to the ArduPilot flight controller.

The Mission Planner tab lets you plan a simple waypoint mission in the browser and upload it to the flight controller through UAVcast-Pro, from anywhere the web interface is reachable. Missions are saved in the same `.waypoints` format (QGC WPL 110) that Mission Planner and QGroundControl use, so you can move them between tools. Open **Flight Map → Mission Planner**.

![Mission Planner tab with a satellite map, an empty waypoint table and the Save, Load, Upload, Read and Clear buttons](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/flight-map--mission-planner.webp)

*Flight Map → Mission Planner before any waypoint is added. Click the map to add one.*

## Plan a mission

1. Click the map where the first waypoint should be. The first time, **Set Default Values** asks for **Default Altitude (meters)**, **Waypoint Radius (meters)** and **Altitude Frame**. Select **Continue**.
2. Keep clicking to add waypoints. Drag a marker to move it.
3. Adjust each waypoint in the table: **Alt (m)**, **Frame** and **Radius (m)**. Remove a waypoint in the **Action** column.
4. Check **Waypoints** and **Distance** for the total route.

| Default | Value | Options |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Default Altitude (meters)** | `100` | any |
| **Waypoint Radius (meters)** | `30` | any |
| **Altitude Frame** | **Relative** | **Relative** (above home), **Absolute** (above mean sea level), **Terrain** (above the ground, needs terrain data on the flight controller) |

In the table the frames are shortened to **Rel**, **Abs** and **Ter**. Waypoints are sent as `MAV_CMD_NAV_WAYPOINT`.

## Upload to the flight controller

1. Under **Flight Controller**, select **Upload**.
2. Confirm **Upload Mission**. The dialog warns that it replaces the mission on the flight controller.
3. You see *Mission uploaded to flight controller*.

- **Read** downloads the mission that's on the flight controller into the planner.
- **Clear** removes the waypoints from the planner.

To fly the mission, use **Start** in the Flight Map's **Actions** tab, or switch to AUTO from your transmitter or ground station.

## Save and load files

Under **Files**:

- **Save** downloads the mission as `mission.waypoints`.
- **Load** opens a `.waypoints` or `.txt` file in QGC WPL format, for example one saved from Mission Planner.

## Limits

This planner handles plain waypoints only. **Load** keeps each row's position, altitude, frame and radius, but turns every row into a plain waypoint: takeoff, land, loiter and DO commands (camera trigger, servo) are not kept, and a command without a position becomes a waypoint at 0, 0. For takeoff and land commands, DO commands, survey grids, fences and rally points, plan and upload from Mission Planner or QGroundControl directly.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-map/mission-planner/


---

# Radio tab

> See live RC channel PWM values and RSSI from your flight controller in the UAVcast-Pro Radio tab, to check transmitter switches and RC camera switching.

The Radio tab shows the RC input the flight controller receives from your transmitter: every channel's PWM value and the RSSI (signal strength). Use it to check switch assignments, for example the channel you use for [RC camera switching](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/multi-camera/), without connecting a ground station. Open **Flight Map → Radio**.

![Radio tab with the RSSI badge, the four primary channels and the auxiliary channels, all at 0](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/flight-map--radio.webp)

*Flight Map → Radio on a bench unit without an RC receiver, so every channel reads 0.*

## What you see

- **RSSI**: the receiver's signal strength from the flight controller, rated **No Signal**, **Weak**, **Fair**, **Good** or **Excellent**. It needs RSSI to be set up on the flight controller (`RSSI_TYPE` on ArduPilot).
- **Primary Controls**: **Channel 1 - Roll**, **Channel 2 - Pitch**, **Channel 3 - Throttle** and **Channel 4 - Yaw**, in the Mission Planner layout.
- **Auxiliary Channels**: the remaining channels.

PWM values typically range from 1000 (min) to 2000 (max). A channel that never moves means it isn't mapped on the transmitter, or the receiver doesn't send it.

The values come from the flight controller's `RC_CHANNELS` message, so they only update while the flight controller link is **Connected**.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-map/radio/


---

# MAVLink Inspector

> Use the UAVcast-Pro MAVLink Inspector to see every message from the flight controller with its rate, system ID and component ID, and debug telemetry and injectors.

The Inspector lists every MAVLink message UAVcast-Pro receives, grouped by vehicle, with its rate and latest field values. Use it to check that the flight controller sends what you expect, to find a message's exact field names, or to confirm that an [injector](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/injectors/) produces `NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT` messages. Open **Flight Map → Inspector**.

![MAVLink Inspector with connection status and the message list for system 1 showing message names, rates in Hz and counts](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/flight-map--inspector.webp)

*Flight Map → Inspector with the messages from the flight controller (system 1) and ATTITUDE expanded.*

## What you see

**MAVLink Connection Status** at the top: **Connection**, **Vehicle**, **GPS Satellites**, **Total Messages** and **System ID**.

**Message Inspector** below: one group per vehicle (*Vehicle (System ID: 1)*), and in it one row per message with:

- the message name,
- **COMP**: the component ID that sent it (1 = autopilot, 194 = the default for injectors),
- the rate in **Hz** and the number of messages received.

Open a message to see its fields and current values.

## Typical checks

| Question | Look for |
| --- | --- |
| Is the GPS sending data? | `GPS_RAW_INT` at 2 to 10 Hz, and `GPS_RTK` if you use [RTK](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/ntrip-rtk/). |
| Why is telemetry slow in the ground station? | Low rates on `ATTITUDE`, `VFR_HUD` or `GLOBAL_POSITION_INT`. Raise the `SRx_` stream rates on the flight controller's MAVLink port. |
| Does my injector work? | `NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT` under COMP 194 (or the compid you set). |

If the list says *Waiting for messages...*, the flight controller link isn't connected. See [Flight controller](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-map/inspector/


---

# Flight Analytics

> Graph live MAVLink telemetry or a recorded .tlog file in UAVcast-Pro Flight Analytics. Pick up to 10 parameters, compare them over time and review a flight on the drone.

Flight Analytics plots MAVLink values over time, either live from the flight controller or from a recorded `.tlog` file. Use it to check vibration, battery sag, altitude hold or signal values without copying logs to a PC. Open **Flight Map → Flight Analytics**.

![Flight Analytics tab with No Log File Loaded, the Open Log File button, the Live switch and the Parameters panel](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/flight-map--flight-analytics.webp)

*Flight Analytics before a log is loaded. Open Log File loads a .tlog.*

## Plot live telemetry

1. Select **Live**. The parameter list fills as messages arrive. If it stays on *Waiting for MAVLink Data*, connect the flight controller first.
2. Search **Parameters** and tick the values to plot. You can plot up to **10** at once.
3. Turn on **Accumulate Data** to keep every point (*Storing all data points*). Off, the chart keeps a rolling window (*Last … points*).

## Analyze a recorded log

1. Select **Open Log File**.
2. In **Select Log File**, pick a recorded `.tlog`. Telemetry logs come from [Recordings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/recordings/) (by default one per armed flight).
3. Tick parameters to plot. **Duration** and the number of **Parameters** in the file are shown at the top.

**Clear All** removes every plotted parameter.

## Where the logs come from

Telemetry is logged on the drone according to **Record telemetry** on **Camera → Recordings → Settings**: **While armed** (default), **Always while connected** or **Off**. The same `.tlog` files open in Mission Planner, MAVExplorer and UAV Log Viewer.

The Flight Map's **Recordings** side tab lists the same telemetry logs with **Messages**, **Max Alt** and **Distance**, and lets you **Download .tlog**, **Delete** or **Play** a log. Playback streams the recorded telemetry to the map as if the drone were flying.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-map/flight-analytics/


---

# Ground control stations

> Add ground station destinations in UAVcast-Pro to stream MAVLink telemetry (UDP 14550) and H.264 video (UDP 5600) to Mission Planner, QGroundControl or several PCs.

A destination tells UAVcast-Pro where to send telemetry and video. Each one is an IP address plus a telemetry port and a video port. UAVcast-Pro sends to every enabled destination at the same time over UDP, so Mission Planner on one laptop and QGroundControl on a tablet can both receive the drone. Open **Ground Control Stations** in the sidebar.

![Ground Control Station page with two destination cards and the Add Destination button](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/ground-control.webp)

*Two destination cards: a disabled, empty one and an enabled destination with telemetry and video on.*

## Add a destination

1. Select **Add Destination**. A new card appears. (A fresh install already has one empty card.)
2. Enter a **Name**, for example `Pilot laptop`.
3. Enter the ground station computer's IPv4 address in **Destination IP or Host** and press Enter. A green check means it's saved.
4. Check **Telemetry Port** (default `14550`) and **Video Port** (default `5600`). Use the ports your ground station listens on.
5. Turn on **Enable Telemetry** and, if you want video, **Enable Video**.

Every field saves when you press Enter or leave it. There is no Save button. Telemetry routing picks up the change within a few seconds.

> **Use an IPv4 address, not a hostname**
>
> Despite the label **Destination IP or Host**, UAVcast-Pro only accepts an IPv4 address such as `192.168.1.20` or a VPN address such as `10.147.17.5`. Hostnames are rejected with *Enter a valid IPv4 address, for example 192.168.1.10.*

## Which IP address to use

| Where the ground station is | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Same Wi-Fi or Ethernet network as the drone | The ground station's LAN address, for example `192.168.1.20`. |
| Anywhere, over 4G/LTE | The ground station's **VPN** address (ZeroTier, Tailscale or Fleet Manager). See [VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/vpn/). |
| Several computers | One destination per computer. |

## Destination settings

| Setting | Default | Values | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Enable Endpoint** | On | On, off | Master switch. Off stops telemetry, video and audio to this destination but keeps its settings. |
| **Name** | empty | up to 49 characters | Shown on the card and in the dashboard. |
| **Destination IP or Host** | empty | IPv4 address | Required before you can turn on telemetry or video. |
| **Telemetry Port** | `14550` | 1–65535 | UDP port the ground station listens on for MAVLink. |
| **Video Port** | `5600` | 1–65535 | UDP port for H.264 RTP video (camera 1). |
| **Video Port (Camera 2)** | empty = Video Port + 1 | 1–65535 | Only shown when [dual stream](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/multi-camera/) is on. |
| **Enable Video** | Off | On, off | Sends the camera stream to this destination. |
| **Enable Telemetry** | Off | On, off | Sends MAVLink to this destination and accepts commands back from it. |
| **Read Only** | Off | On, off | Needs **Enable Telemetry**. The ground station receives telemetry but can't change anything on the vehicle: commands, arming, mode changes, parameter writes, mission writes, RC override and manual control from it are blocked. This applies from UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3; on earlier versions, Read Only does not block parameter writes. |

Audio, when you turn on **Send audio to ground stations** on the Camera page, goes to every destination that receives video, on **Video Port + 2** (for example `5602`). See [Audio](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/audio/).

So each destination occupies three video-side ports: **Video Port**, + 1 (camera 2) and + 2 (audio). If two destinations point at the same computer, space their video ports 3 apart, for example `5600` and `5603`. See [Two stations on one computer](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/multiple-ground-stations/#3-two-stations-on-one-computer).

## Set up the receiving side

Pick the program you use on the ground. Each page has the exact settings, the firewall step and fixes for the usual errors.

| Ground station | Telemetry | Video | Page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mission Planner (Windows) | UDP 14550 | GStreamer source on 5600 | [Mission Planner](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/mission-planner/) |
| QGroundControl (Windows, macOS, Linux) | UDP 14550, connects by itself | UDP h.264 on 5600 | [QGroundControl](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/qgroundcontrol/) |
| Android tablet or phone | QGroundControl, UDP 14550 | UDP h.264 on 5600 | [Android](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/android/) |
| GStreamer on Windows | – | `gst-launch-1.0` on 5600 | [GStreamer on Windows](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-windows/) |
| GStreamer on Linux | – | `gst-launch-1.0` on 5600 | [GStreamer on Linux](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-linux/) |
| GStreamer on macOS | – | `gst-launch-1.0` on 5600 | [GStreamer on macOS](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-macos/) |
| VLC, or pulling RTSP from the drone | – | SDP file, or RTSP on 8554 | [VLC and RTSP](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/vlc-and-rtsp/) |

### What the drone sends

| Stream | Format | Port on the ground station |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Telemetry | MAVLink over UDP | **Telemetry Port** (default `14550`) |
| Camera 1 video | H.264 in RTP, payload type 96, over UDP | **Video Port** (default `5600`) |
| Camera 2 video (dual stream) | H.264 in RTP, payload type 96, over UDP | **Video Port (Camera 2)** (default Video Port + 1, `5601`) |
| Audio (optional) | Opus in RTP, payload type 97, 48 kHz, over UDP | Video Port + 2 (`5602`) |

The drone pushes every stream to the destination. Nothing needs to connect to the drone, but the ground station's firewall must let the UDP packets in.

## Several ground stations

Add one destination per computer. If two ground stations run on the **same** computer (for example QGroundControl and a logging tool), give them different telemetry ports, such as `14550` and `14551`, and set each application to its port.

Use **Read Only** for observers, payload operators or a second screen: they see everything but can't command the vehicle.

## Destinations from Fleet Manager

When the drone is paired with Fleet Manager and you create a stream binding there, Fleet Manager adds the destination for you. These cards show a cloud icon (*Managed by Fleet Manager*). Change them in Fleet Manager rather than here. See [Pair with Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/fleet-pairing/).

## Check that data is flowing

- The [Dashboard](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/dashboard/) **Ground station** row reads *Sending · 16 packets/s* or *Sending to 2 · … packets/s*.
- **Flight Controller → Connection → Connection check** lists each destination with its packet rate.
- *1 set up · waiting for flight controller* means the destination is fine but no telemetry comes from the flight controller yet.

Read-only users see this page but can't change it.

## Troubleshooting

- [No telemetry in the ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/)
- [No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/


---

# Mission Planner

> Connect Mission Planner to a UAVcast-Pro drone: MAVLink over UDP 14550, live H.264 video in the HUD with the exact GStreamer source, Windows firewall, a second camera and common errors.

Mission Planner receives UAVcast-Pro telemetry over UDP port 14550 and shows the live video in its HUD through a GStreamer source on port 5600. Telemetry needs one click; video needs a pipeline pasted once, which Mission Planner remembers.

## Before you begin

- On the drone, a destination on [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/) with this PC's IP address (the VPN address over 4G), **Enable Telemetry** on, and **Enable Video** on for video.
- The camera streaming on **Camera → Camera settings**.
- A current Mission Planner on Windows. Find this PC's IP with `ipconfig` in a Command Prompt.

## Connect telemetry

1. In the top-right corner of Mission Planner, choose **UDP** in the connection drop-down. The baud rate is ignored.
2. Select **Connect**.
3. When asked for the listen port, keep `14550` (or the **Telemetry Port** you set on the drone) and select **OK**.
4. Mission Planner downloads the parameters, and the drone appears on the map.

![Mission Planner Flight Data view connected over UDP: the top-right connection box shows UDP, the link UDP14550-1-QUADRO and the DISCONNECT button; the HUD shows DISARMED, Unhealthy AHRS and GPS: No Fix](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/gcs/mission-planner--connected.webp)

*Connected. The top-right box shows UDP and the link UDP14550-1-QUADRO, and the button now reads DISCONNECT. This is a bench setup without GPS, so the HUD shows DISARMED, Unhealthy AHRS and GPS: No Fix.*

## Show the video in the HUD

1. Right-click the HUD (the artificial horizon) and choose **Video → Set GStreamer Source**.

2. Paste this pipeline and select **OK**:

   ```text
   udpsrc port=5600 caps="application/x-rtp, media=video, clock-rate=90000, encoding-name=H264, payload=96" ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! video/x-raw,format=BGRA ! appsink name=outsink
   ```

3. The video replaces the HUD background within a few seconds. The flight data stays on top of it.

*Illustration of Mission Planner: right-click menu on the HUD with Video highlighted and its submenu item Set GStreamer Source.*

*Illustration Mission Planner, simplified. (1) Right-click the HUD, (2) Video, (3) Set GStreamer Source, then paste the pipeline.*

Mission Planner uses its own copy of GStreamer for the HUD, so you don't need the separate install from [GStreamer on Windows](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-windows/) for this. If Mission Planner offers to download GStreamer, let it.

Keep the end of the pipeline exactly as shown: Mission Planner needs `video/x-raw,format=BGRA ! appsink name=outsink` to draw the picture. Change only the port.

### Lower latency

`rtpjitterbuffer` smooths out packets that arrive late, at the cost of about 200 ms of delay. On a good link you can cut it down:

```text
udpsrc port=5600 caps="application/x-rtp, media=video, clock-rate=90000, encoding-name=H264, payload=96" ! rtpjitterbuffer latency=0 ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! video/x-raw,format=BGRA ! appsink name=outsink sync=false
```

On a weak 4G link, keep the default jitter buffer; the picture breaks up less.

## Allow Mission Planner through the Windows firewall

Windows asks the first time Mission Planner listens on the network. Allow it on **Private** and **Public** networks. A ZeroTier or Tailscale adapter is often classified as **Public**, so ticking only Private blocks the VPN.

If you dismissed the prompt, open the ports in an administrator PowerShell:

```powershell
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "UAVcast-Pro telemetry" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 14550 -Action Allow
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "UAVcast-Pro video" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 5600-5602 -Action Allow
```

## Second camera (dual stream)

With [dual stream](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/multi-camera/) on, camera 2 goes to **Video Port (Camera 2)**, by default `5601`. Mission Planner's HUD shows one source. Either switch the HUD source to port 5601 when you need camera 2, or watch camera 2 in a separate GStreamer window: see [GStreamer on Windows](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-windows/).

Audio (Video Port + 2) is ignored by Mission Planner. Play it with GStreamer.

## Common problems

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- |
| Connects on Wi-Fi, nothing over 4G | The destination uses the LAN IP. Use this PC's VPN IP. |
| *No heartbeat packets received* | The drone isn't sending to this PC: wrong IP, **Enable Telemetry** off, or the firewall blocks UDP 14550. |
| Telemetry works, HUD stays black | **Enable Video** is off for this destination, the camera isn't running, or UDP 5600 is blocked. Test with [GStreamer on Windows](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-windows/). |
| Video freezes or smears grey | Packet loss. Lower the bitrate on the drone and set **Stream Recovery Rate** to 15–30 frames. |
| Video stops when another program opens | Only one program can listen on a UDP port. Close the GStreamer window or QGroundControl that also uses 5600. |

More checks: [No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/) and [No telemetry in the ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/mission-planner/


---

# QGroundControl

> Get UAVcast-Pro telemetry and live H.264 video into QGroundControl on Windows, macOS or Linux: UDP 14550 auto-connect, Video Source UDP h.264 on port 5600, low latency mode and fixes.

QGroundControl listens for MAVLink on UDP port 14550 by default, so a UAVcast-Pro drone appears as soon as its telemetry arrives. For video, set the video source to **UDP h.264 Video Stream** on port 5600 once. QGroundControl has GStreamer built in, so there is nothing else to install. This works the same on Windows, macOS and Linux; for tablets see [Android](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/android/).

## Before you begin

- On the drone, a destination on [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/) with this computer's IP address (the VPN address over 4G), **Enable Telemetry** on, and **Enable Video** on for video.
- The camera streaming on **Camera → Camera settings**.
- QGroundControl from [qgroundcontrol.com](https://qgroundcontrol.com/).

## Telemetry

Start QGroundControl. Within a few seconds of the first packet the vehicle appears and the toolbar shows its flight mode and battery.

![QGroundControl Fly view connected to an ArduPilot vehicle: toolbar with Not Ready and Stabilize, a five-waypoint mission on the map with No GPS Lock for Vehicle, and the video window in the bottom-left corner showing WAITING FOR VIDEO](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/gcs/qgroundcontrol--fly-view.webp)

*Telemetry working: the toolbar shows the vehicle's state and flight mode (Not Ready, Stabilize). This is a bench setup without GPS, hence No GPS Lock for Vehicle. The video window (bottom left) says WAITING FOR VIDEO until video is set up below.*

Nothing appears? Check that automatic UDP connection is on: **Q** icon → **Application Settings**, then **AutoConnect to the following devices** → **UDP** ticked (the default). Depending on your QGroundControl version, the AutoConnect list is on the **Comm Links** page or on the **General** page. If you set a **Telemetry Port** other than 14550 on the drone, add a link instead: **Application Settings** → **Comm Links** → **Add**, type **UDP**, the port you chose, then **Connect**.

## Video

1. Click the **Q** icon (top left) → **Application Settings**.
2. Open the **Video** page. In older versions, video is a **Video** section on the **General** page.
3. Set **Source** to **UDP h.264 Video Stream**.
4. Check the UDP address. The default `0.0.0.0:5600` listens on port 5600, which matches the drone's default **Video Port**. If you changed **Video Port** on the drone, use that port here. Current versions call the field **UDP URL**; older ones show a **UDP Port** number.
5. Go back to the **Fly** view. The video appears in the small window in the corner. Click it to swap video and map.

*Illustration of QGroundControl Application Settings: the Video page with Source set to UDP h.264 Video Stream, the UDP address 0.0.0.0:5600 and Low Latency Mode.*

*Illustration QGroundControl, simplified. (1) Q icon → Application Settings, (2) Video, (3) Source UDP h.264 Video Stream, (4) UDP URL with port 5600.*

### Low latency mode

In the same video settings, turn on **Low Latency Mode**. QGroundControl then drops late frames instead of buffering them, which cuts the delay noticeably on a good link. On a weak 4G link it can make the picture stutter; turn it off again if it does.

## Firewall

- **Windows**: allow QGroundControl on **Private** and **Public** networks when Windows asks. VPN adapters (ZeroTier, Tailscale) are often classified as Public. To open the ports by hand, see [Mission Planner: Windows firewall](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/mission-planner/#allow-mission-planner-through-the-windows-firewall); the same rules apply.
- **macOS**: allow incoming connections for QGroundControl when macOS asks.
- **Linux**: if `ufw` is active, run `sudo ufw allow 14550/udp` and `sudo ufw allow 5600:5602/udp`.

## Second camera and audio

QGroundControl plays one video stream. With [dual stream](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/multi-camera/) on, camera 2 goes to port 5601: change the UDP port to `5601` to watch it, or open camera 2 in a GStreamer window ([Windows](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-windows/), [Linux](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-linux/), [macOS](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-macos/)) next to QGroundControl.

QGroundControl ignores audio. Play it with GStreamer on Video Port + 2 (`5602`).

## Common problems

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- |
| *Waiting For Vehicle Connection* | No telemetry reaches this computer. Check the destination IP (VPN IP over 4G), **Enable Telemetry**, and the firewall. |
| Telemetry works, video window says no video | **Enable Video** is off, the camera isn't running, the source isn't **UDP h.264 Video Stream**, or UDP 5600 is blocked. |
| Video appears, then freezes over 4G | Packet loss. Lower the bitrate on the drone, set **Stream Recovery Rate** to 15–30 frames, and turn **Low Latency Mode** off. |
| Vehicle appears twice | Two destinations point at this computer, or a second link duplicates the auto-connect. Remove one. |
| Video stops when you start a GStreamer test | Only one program can listen on a UDP port. Close one of them. |

More checks: [No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/qgroundcontrol/


---

# GStreamer on Windows

> Install GStreamer on Windows (MSVC 64-bit, Complete), add it to PATH and play UAVcast-Pro H.264 video and Opus audio with gst-launch-1.0 in PowerShell or cmd. Firewall and fixes.

GStreamer plays the UAVcast-Pro video stream in its own window, without a ground station program. Use it to test whether video reaches the PC, to watch a second camera next to Mission Planner or QGroundControl, or to hear the audio track. It takes about five minutes to set up.

## Before you begin

On the drone, add a destination on [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/) with this PC's IP address (`ipconfig` shows it; use the VPN address over 4G) and **Enable Video** on.

## Step 1: Install GStreamer

1. Go to [gstreamer.freedesktop.org/download](https://gstreamer.freedesktop.org/download/) and download the Windows **runtime** installer for **MSVC 64-bit** (not the development installer, and not MinGW).
2. Run it and choose **Complete** when asked for the installation type.
3. Note the install folder. Newer installers use `C:\Program Files\gstreamer\1.0\msvc_x86_64`, older ones `C:\gstreamer\1.0\msvc_x86_64`.

> **Choose Complete, not Typical**
>
> The **Typical** installation leaves out the H.264 decoder (`avdec_h264`). The command below then fails with *no element "avdec_h264"*. Run the installer again and pick **Complete**.

## Step 2: Add GStreamer to PATH

So you can run `gst-launch-1.0` from any folder, add its `bin` folder to your user PATH. In PowerShell (no administrator rights needed), with your install folder:

```powershell
$bin = "C:\Program Files\gstreamer\1.0\msvc_x86_64\bin"
$userPath = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "User")
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "$userPath;$bin", "User")
```

Close and reopen the terminal, then check:

```powershell
gst-launch-1.0 --version
```

Or use the Windows settings: search for **Edit environment variables for your account**, select **Path** → **Edit** → **New**, and paste the `bin` folder.

## Step 3: Play the video

**PowerShell**

```powershell
gst-launch-1.0 -v udpsrc port=5600 'caps=application/x-rtp,media=video,clock-rate=90000,encoding-name=H264,payload=96' ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! autovideosink sync=false
```

Keep the single quotes around `caps=…`: without them PowerShell splits the value at the commas.

**Command Prompt (cmd)**

```bat
gst-launch-1.0 -v udpsrc port=5600 caps="application/x-rtp, media=(string)video, clock-rate=(int)90000, encoding-name=(string)H264, payload=(int)96" ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! autovideosink sync=false
```

A window opens as soon as the first keyframe arrives. Close it, or press **Ctrl+C** in the terminal, to stop.

> **What you should see**
>
> 1. The terminal prints `Setting pipeline to PLAYING ...` and waits for video.
> 2. When the first packets arrive, `-v` prints lines containing `caps = application/x-rtp`.
> 3. A video window opens with the camera picture.
>
> If it stops after step 1, no video reaches this computer: see the troubleshooting table below.

For camera 2 in [dual stream](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/multi-camera/), run the same command in a second terminal with `port=5601`.

### Lower-latency variant

On a good link, drop the jitter buffer delay:

```powershell
gst-launch-1.0 udpsrc port=5600 'caps=application/x-rtp,media=video,clock-rate=90000,encoding-name=H264,payload=96' ! rtpjitterbuffer latency=0 ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! autovideosink sync=false
```

On 4G, keep the default jitter buffer (the first command); it hides late packets.

### A double-click shortcut

Save this as `uavcast-video.cmd` on the desktop and double-click it:

```bat
@echo off
gst-launch-1.0 -v udpsrc port=5600 caps="application/x-rtp, media=(string)video, clock-rate=(int)90000, encoding-name=(string)H264, payload=(int)96" ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! autovideosink sync=false
pause
```

If GStreamer isn't on PATH, add `cd /d "C:\Program Files\gstreamer\1.0\msvc_x86_64\bin"` as the second line.

## Hear the audio

Turn on **Audio** and **Send audio to ground stations** on the drone's **Camera** page. Audio arrives on Video Port + 2:

```powershell
gst-launch-1.0 udpsrc port=5602 'caps=application/x-rtp,media=audio,encoding-name=OPUS,clock-rate=48000,payload=97' ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtpopusdepay ! opusdec ! audioconvert ! autoaudiosink
```

## Allow it through the firewall

The first time `gst-launch-1.0` listens, Windows asks whether to allow it. Tick **Private** and **Public** (VPN adapters are often Public). To open the ports for any program instead, in an administrator PowerShell:

```powershell
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "UAVcast-Pro video and audio" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 5600-5602 -Action Allow
```

## Troubleshooting

| Message or symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| *'gst-launch-1.0' is not recognized…* | GStreamer isn't on PATH. Do step 2 and open a new terminal, or run it from the `bin` folder. |
| *WARNING: erroneous pipeline: no element "avdec_h264"* | Typical installation. Reinstall with **Complete**. |
| *no element "rtph264depay"* or *"udpsrc"* | Same cause: the plugin sets weren't installed. Reinstall with **Complete**. |
| Runs, but no window opens | Nothing arrives. Check the destination IP on the drone (VPN IP over 4G), **Enable Video**, the camera, and the firewall. With `-v`, a line with `caps = application/x-rtp` appears once packets arrive. |
| *Could not get/set settings from/on resource* or a bind error | Another program (Mission Planner, QGroundControl, a second GStreamer) already listens on that port. Close it. |
| Picture smears grey or freezes | Packet loss. Lower the bitrate on the drone and set **Stream Recovery Rate** to 15–30 frames. |
| *erroneous pipeline: could not parse caps* in PowerShell | The quotes around `caps=…` are missing or are double quotes with spaces. Use the PowerShell command exactly as shown. |

Linux or Mac? See [GStreamer on Linux](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-linux/) or [GStreamer on macOS](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-macos/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-windows/


---

# GStreamer on Linux

> Install GStreamer on Ubuntu, Debian or Fedora and play UAVcast-Pro H.264 drone video and Opus audio with gst-launch-1.0, including a second camera, low latency and ufw.

GStreamer plays the UAVcast-Pro video stream in a window with one command. Use it to test the video path, watch a second camera, or hear the audio. Works on any desktop Linux, including a Raspberry Pi used as a ground station.

## Before you begin

On the drone, add a destination on [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/) with this computer's IP address (`ip -4 addr`; use the VPN address over 4G) and **Enable Video** on.

## Install GStreamer

**Ubuntu / Debian / Raspberry Pi OS**

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install gstreamer1.0-tools gstreamer1.0-plugins-good gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad gstreamer1.0-libav
```

`gstreamer1.0-libav` provides the H.264 decoder (`avdec_h264`). Without it the command below fails.

**Fedora**

```bash
sudo dnf install gstreamer1 gstreamer1-plugins-good gstreamer1-plugins-bad-free gstreamer1-plugin-libav
```

Fedora's own repositories leave out most H.264 support for patent reasons, so `avdec_h264` may still be missing after this. If the check below fails, enable [RPM Fusion](https://rpmfusion.org/) and follow its multimedia guide to get the full codec libraries.

Check that the H.264 decoder is there:

```bash
gst-inspect-1.0 avdec_h264
```

It prints the element's details. *No such element or plugin* means the decoder is missing.

## Play the video

```bash
gst-launch-1.0 -v udpsrc port=5600 caps="application/x-rtp, media=(string)video, clock-rate=(int)90000, encoding-name=(string)H264, payload=(int)96" ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! autovideosink sync=false
```

A window opens once the first keyframe arrives. Press **Ctrl+C** to stop.

> **What you should see**
>
> 1. The terminal prints `Setting pipeline to PLAYING ...` and waits for video.
> 2. When the first packets arrive, `-v` prints lines containing `caps = application/x-rtp`.
> 3. A video window opens with the camera picture.
>
> If it stops after step 1, no video reaches this computer: see the troubleshooting table below.

- **Camera 2** in [dual stream](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/multi-camera/): run it again with `port=5601`.
- **Lower latency** on a good link: replace `rtpjitterbuffer` with `rtpjitterbuffer latency=0`. Keep the default on 4G.

## Hear the audio

With **Send audio to ground stations** on, audio arrives on Video Port + 2:

```bash
gst-launch-1.0 udpsrc port=5602 caps="application/x-rtp, media=(string)audio, clock-rate=(int)48000, encoding-name=(string)OPUS, payload=(int)97" ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtpopusdepay ! opusdec ! audioconvert ! autoaudiosink
```

## Firewall

Most desktop distributions don't block incoming UDP. If `ufw` is active:

```bash
sudo ufw allow 5600:5602/udp
sudo ufw allow 14550/udp
```

## Troubleshooting

| Message or symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| *no element "avdec_h264"* | Install `gstreamer1.0-libav`. |
| *no element "rtph264depay"* | Install `gstreamer1.0-plugins-good`. |
| Runs, but no window | Nothing arrives. Check the destination IP on the drone, **Enable Video**, and the firewall. `sudo tcpdump -ni any udp port 5600` shows whether packets reach the computer. |
| Bind error on start | Another program (QGroundControl, another GStreamer) listens on the port. Close it. |
| Window opens, picture smears grey | Packet loss. Lower the bitrate on the drone and set **Stream Recovery Rate** to 15–30 frames. |

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-linux/


---

# GStreamer on macOS

> Install GStreamer on a Mac with Homebrew or the official package and play UAVcast-Pro H.264 drone video and Opus audio with gst-launch-1.0, plus the macOS firewall prompt.

GStreamer plays the UAVcast-Pro video stream in a window from the Terminal. Use it to test the video path, watch a second camera next to QGroundControl, or hear the audio. Works on Apple silicon and Intel Macs.

## Before you begin

On the drone, add a destination on [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/) with this Mac's IP address (**System Settings → Network**; use the VPN address over 4G) and **Enable Video** on.

## Install GStreamer

**Homebrew**

```bash
brew install gstreamer
```

The Homebrew formula includes the base, good, bad, ugly and libav plugin sets, so `avdec_h264` is there.

**Official package**

1. Download the macOS **runtime** package from [gstreamer.freedesktop.org/download](https://gstreamer.freedesktop.org/download/) and install it.

2. Add it to your PATH in Terminal:

   ```bash
   echo 'export PATH="/Library/Frameworks/GStreamer.framework/Versions/1.0/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
   source ~/.zshrc
   ```

Check the install with `gst-launch-1.0 --version`, and check the H.264 decoder with `gst-inspect-1.0 avdec_h264` (it prints the element's details; *No such element or plugin* means it's missing).

## Play the video

```bash
gst-launch-1.0 -v udpsrc port=5600 caps="application/x-rtp, media=(string)video, clock-rate=(int)90000, encoding-name=(string)H264, payload=(int)96" ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! autovideosink sync=false
```

The first time, macOS asks whether `gst-launch-1.0` may accept incoming network connections. Select **Allow**. A window opens once the first keyframe arrives; press **Ctrl+C** in Terminal to stop.

> **What you should see**
>
> 1. The terminal prints `Setting pipeline to PLAYING ...` and waits for video.
> 2. When the first packets arrive, `-v` prints lines containing `caps = application/x-rtp`.
> 3. A video window opens with the camera picture.
>
> If it stops after step 1, no video reaches this computer: see the troubleshooting table below.

- **Camera 2** in [dual stream](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/multi-camera/): run it again with `port=5601`.
- **Lower latency** on a good link: replace `rtpjitterbuffer` with `rtpjitterbuffer latency=0`.
- If no window appears even though packets arrive, replace `autovideosink` with `osxvideosink`.

## Hear the audio

```bash
gst-launch-1.0 udpsrc port=5602 caps="application/x-rtp, media=(string)audio, clock-rate=(int)48000, encoding-name=(string)OPUS, payload=(int)97" ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtpopusdepay ! opusdec ! audioconvert ! autoaudiosink
```

Audio needs **Audio** and **Send audio to ground stations** turned on on the drone's **Camera** page.

## Troubleshooting

| Message or symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| *command not found: gst-launch-1.0* | Homebrew: run `brew doctor`. Official package: add the framework `bin` folder to PATH as shown above. |
| *no element "avdec_h264"* | The libav plugin is missing. Reinstall with Homebrew, or install the full official runtime package. |
| Runs, but no window | Nothing arrives. Check the destination IP, **Enable Video**, and that you allowed incoming connections (**System Settings → Network → Firewall → Options**). |
| Bind error on start | QGroundControl or another GStreamer already uses the port. Close it. |

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-macos/


---

# Android and tablets

> Receive UAVcast-Pro telemetry and live video on an Android phone or tablet with QGroundControl, over Wi-Fi or 4G through a VPN, plus the browser option for iPad.

QGroundControl for Android receives UAVcast-Pro telemetry on UDP 14550 and video on UDP 5600, exactly like the desktop version. Over 4G, install the Tailscale or ZeroTier app on the tablet so the drone can reach it.

## Set up QGroundControl on Android

1. Install **QGroundControl** from [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mavlink.qgroundcontrol).

2. Connect the tablet to the network the drone sends to:

   - **Same Wi-Fi**: find the tablet's IP under **Settings → Wi-Fi → (your network) → Advanced** or similar.
   - **Over 4G**: install the [ZeroTier One](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.zerotier.one) or [Tailscale](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.tailscale.ipn) app, join the same network as the drone (see [VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/vpn/)), and note the tablet's VPN address.

3. On the drone, add a destination on [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/) with the tablet's IP, **Enable Telemetry** and **Enable Video** on.

4. Open QGroundControl. The vehicle appears when telemetry arrives.

5. For video: **Q** icon → **Application Settings** → **Video** (on older versions, the **Video** section of **General**), set **Source** to **UDP h.264 Video Stream** and check that the UDP address uses port `5600`.

When it works, the **Fly** view shows the drone on the map with its flight mode and battery in the toolbar, and the camera picture in the small video window in the corner. Tap the window to swap video and map.

> **Keep the VPN app connected**
>
> Android may stop VPN apps in the background to save battery. Exclude ZeroTier or Tailscale from battery optimization, and keep the VPN switched on while flying.

Details on the video settings, low latency mode and common problems are on the [QGroundControl page](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/qgroundcontrol/).

## iPad, iPhone and other devices: use the browser

The UAVcast-Pro web interface runs in any modern browser. On an iPad or a phone, open `http://<drone-ip>` (the VPN address over 4G) and use the [Flight Map](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-map/): live map, cockpit HUD, camera video, arm/disarm and RTL. The video there is the live preview (WebRTC), so the browser must reach port 8889 on the drone.

## Common problems

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Vehicle never appears over 4G | The VPN app on the tablet is off or the destination uses the Wi-Fi IP. Use the tablet's VPN address. |
| Works until the screen turns off | Android paused the VPN app. Turn off battery optimization for it. |
| Telemetry works, no video | Check **Enable Video**, the camera, and the video source settings in QGroundControl. |

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/android/


---

# VLC and RTSP

> Play UAVcast-Pro H.264 RTP video in VLC with an SDP file, or pull the camera from the drone over RTSP on port 8554 for a recording PC, video wall or third-party software.

VLC can play the UAVcast-Pro stream with a small SDP file that describes it. If you'd rather pull the video from the drone than have it pushed to you, the drone's media server also offers each camera over RTSP. Both add more delay than QGroundControl, Mission Planner or GStreamer, so use them for watching and recording, not for flying.

## Play the UDP stream in VLC

1. On the drone, add a destination on [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/) with this computer's IP and **Enable Video** on.

2. Save this as `uavcast.sdp`:

   ```text
   v=0
   o=- 0 0 IN IP4 127.0.0.1
   s=UAVcast-Pro
   c=IN IP4 0.0.0.0
   t=0 0
   m=video 5600 RTP/AVP 96
   a=rtpmap:96 H264/90000
   ```

3. Open it in VLC with **Media → Open File**.

For camera 2 in dual stream, make a copy with `m=video 5601`. To add the audio track, append:

```text
m=audio 5602 RTP/AVP 97
a=rtpmap:97 opus/48000/2
```

To cut the delay, lower **Network caching** in VLC (**Tools → Preferences → Show settings: All → Input / Codecs**). Expect more delay than GStreamer anyway.

## Pull the video from the drone over RTSP

While the camera runs with **Enable Live Preview?** ticked or with camera recording enabled, the drone's media server publishes each camera over RTSP (TCP only) on port 8554:

```text
rtsp://<drone-ip>:8554/camera     # camera 1
rtsp://<drone-ip>:8554/camera2    # camera 2 (dual stream)
```

Open it in VLC (**Media → Open Network Stream**), in a video management system, or with GStreamer:

```bash
gst-launch-1.0 rtspsrc location=rtsp://192.168.1.50:8554/camera latency=100 ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! autovideosink sync=false
```

Use this on the local network or over the VPN. Don't forward port 8554 to the internet: the stream has no password.

## Which method should I use?

| You want | Use |
| --- | --- |
| To fly with video | [QGroundControl](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/qgroundcontrol/) or [Mission Planner](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/mission-planner/) |
| A quick test, a second camera window, or audio | GStreamer on [Windows](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-windows/), [Linux](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-linux/) or [macOS](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-macos/) |
| VLC because it's already installed | The SDP file above |
| A PC or system that should fetch the video itself | RTSP |

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/vlc-and-rtsp/


---

# Cellular modem (4G/LTE)

> Connect a HiLink or traditional 4G/LTE USB modem to UAVcast-Pro, with automatic APN detection, SIM PIN, auto-reconnect and modem signal information for flying over cellular.

A 4G/LTE modem gives the drone internet access wherever there's cellular coverage, so telemetry and video reach your ground station far beyond Wi-Fi range. UAVcast-Pro supports **HiLink** modems, which connect by themselves, and **Traditional (PPP)** modems, which UAVcast-Pro connects through ModemManager. For traditional modems it finds the APN automatically, connects at boot and reconnects after drops. Open **Modem** in the sidebar.

![Modem page with Traditional (PPP) selected, APN left on Automatic, and the No Modem Connected panel](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/modem.webp)

*Modem page with Traditional (PPP) selected and the APN left on Automatic, before a modem is plugged in.*

## Which type is my modem?

|  | HiLink | Traditional (PPP) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How it appears | A network card (`usb0` or `eth1`). The modem runs its own router and web page, often at `192.168.8.1`. | A modem device managed by ModemManager. The connection usually appears as `ppp0` or `wwan0`. |
| Who connects | The modem itself. | UAVcast-Pro, through ModemManager and NetworkManager. |
| Settings in UAVcast-Pro | None. Set the APN in the modem's own web page if needed. | APN (optional), username, password, PIN. |
| Examples | Huawei E3372h, E8372 | Huawei E3372s, Quectel EC25 / EG25, Sierra Wireless |

Not sure? Plug it in and run `mmcli -L` on the drone. If ModemManager lists it, use **Traditional (PPP)**. If not, and a new network interface appears in **Networks**, it's HiLink.

## Set up a traditional modem

1. Insert a data SIM and plug the modem into the companion computer.
2. Go to **Modem**. Set **Enable modem** to **Yes** and **Modem type** to **Traditional (PPP)**.
3. Leave **Access Point Name (Optional)** empty. UAVcast-Pro detects it.
4. Enter **PIN code (Optional)** if your SIM asks for one.
5. Wait 30 to 90 seconds. **Modem Information** shows the operator, technology and **IPv4 Information** once connected.

A plugged-in modem connects automatically. If you select **Disconnect**, it stays disconnected until you connect it again, also after a reboot.

### How the automatic APN works

With the APN field empty, UAVcast-Pro tries, in this order:

1. the APN that worked last time with this SIM's operator,
2. the network's default (empty APN),
3. the APN the modem attached to LTE with,
4. the operator's internet APNs from the mobile broadband provider database.

The first one that gets an internet address is saved for that operator. Put in a new SIM from another operator and it detects again. If your operator needs a special APN (private APN, M2M or corporate SIMs), type it in. A user-set APN is the only one tried.

## Set up a HiLink modem

1. Plug the modem in. Wait until its LED shows a solid connection.
2. On **Modem**, set **Enable modem** to **Yes** and **Modem type** to **HiLink**.
3. Check **Hilink Modem Information**: you should see the **Interface** and an **IP Address**.

HiLink modems connect, choose the network and reconnect on their own, so there are no connect buttons. Change the APN, PIN or network mode in the modem's own web page (browse to it from the drone's network, often `http://192.168.8.1`).

## Settings reference

| Setting | Default | Values | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Enable modem** | **Yes** | **Yes**, **No** |  |
| **Modem type** | **Traditional (PPP)** | **HiLink**, **Traditional (PPP)** |  |
| **Access Point Name (Optional)** | empty (**Automatic**) | APN from your operator | Traditional only. |
| **Username (Optional)** / **Password (Optional)** | empty |  | Traditional only. Most operators need neither. |
| **PIN code (Optional)** | empty | SIM PIN | Traditional only. Leave empty if the SIM has no PIN. |

## Modem information

For traditional modems, **Modem Information** shows **Signal Quality**, **Technology** (LTE, UMTS …), **Unlock Required**, **State**, **Manufacturer**, **IMEI**, the network (**Operator**, **Code**, **Registration**), **IPv4 Information** (**IP Address**, **Gateway**, **DNS**, **MTU**) and **Connection Properties** (**APN**, **IP Type**, **Roaming**).

The dashboard's **Cellular** row shows the same signal summary.

## Before flying over cellular

- On [Networks](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/networks/), select **Modem Priority (Outdoor Mode)** so traffic stays on the modem when Wi-Fi is still in range at take-off.
- Use a [VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/vpn/): cellular operators don't give the drone an address your ground station can reach.
- Turn on the GCS failsafe on the flight controller.
- Check signal at altitude: coverage is planned for the ground, and the signal changes as you climb.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| *No Modem Connected* | The modem isn't detected. Check the USB connection and the modem's power LED. Use a powered hub if the Pi resets when the modem connects. |
| **Unlock Required** shows *locked* | Enter the SIM PIN, or disable the PIN in a phone. |
| Registered, but no IP address | Wrong APN. Type the operator's APN instead of using automatic. |
| Connects, then drops under load | Usually power. Check the dashboard **Power supply** row. |

The **Action Logs** show each APN attempt and the reason it failed. For more help, see [Modem connected but no internet](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/modem-no-internet/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/cellular-modem/


---

# VPN

> Put your drone and ground station on one private network with the Fleet Manager VPN, or your own Tailscale or ZeroTier network, so telemetry and video work over 4G/LTE.

Over 4G/LTE your drone gets an address from the mobile operator that your ground station can't reach. A VPN fixes that: the drone and the ground station join the same private network and get fixed addresses on it, wherever they are and whatever network they use. Open **Virtual Private Network** in the sidebar.

The quickest way is the **Fleet Manager VPN**, which is included with your UAVcast-Pro license. If you already run your own Tailscale tailnet or ZeroTier network, UAVcast-Pro can join that instead.

![Virtual Private Network page with VPN enabled, Tailscale selected, the Fleet Manager tab, and VPN Information showing Not Connected](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/private-network.webp)

*Virtual Private Network with Tailscale selected on a drone that is not paired or logged in yet.*

## Which one should I use?

|  | Fleet Manager VPN | Tailscale | ZeroTier |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Account | Your Fleet Manager organization (included with your license) | Your own Tailscale account | Your own ZeroTier network (self-managed) |
| Set up on the drone | One click during or after pairing | Log in with a browser link or an auth key | Paste a network ID |
| Ground stations | Joined from Fleet Manager's **Network** page, streams set with stream bindings | Join your tailnet | Join your network |
| Best for | Most operators, and every fleet | Teams already on Tailscale | Teams already on ZeroTier |

The drone can be on one VPN at a time through this page.

> **UAVnet is being retired**
>
> UAVnet, UAVmatrix's hosted ZeroTier controller at uavnet.uavmatrix.com, is being discontinued in favour of Fleet Manager. If your drones use a UAVnet network, move them to the Fleet Manager VPN. The **Open UAVNet Controller** button on this page opens UAVnet.

## Fleet Manager VPN

The Fleet Manager VPN is your organization's private network, run by Fleet Manager on the Tailscale client. You don't need a Tailscale account.

1. In Fleet Manager, open **Network** and select **Enable VPN Network** if it isn't on yet. See [Network and VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/).
2. [Pair the drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/fleet-pairing/) and keep **Enable VPN for this UAV** ticked in the pairing wizard. A drone that is already paired joins from the **Fleet Manager** tab on this page (see below), or with **Push to Drone** on Fleet Manager's **Network** page.
3. Put each ground station on the network from Fleet Manager's **Network** page: [Connect a ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/connect-gcs/).
4. Send streams to it with a [stream binding](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/stream-bindings/). Fleet Manager adds the destination on the drone's [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/) page for you.

A step-by-step flight setup over 4G is in [Fly beyond visual range over 4G](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/bvlos-4g/).

## Tailscale

Use this for your own tailnet, or for the Fleet Manager VPN on a drone that is already paired. UAVcast-Pro installs Tailscale. Choose how the drone logs in on one of the three tabs.

**Web Login**

1. Set **Enable VPN** to **Yes** and choose **Tailscale** in **Services**.
2. On **Web Login**, select **Generate Login URL**, then **Authenticate this device**.
3. Log in to Tailscale in the new tab and approve the device.
4. Back in UAVcast-Pro the status changes to **Connected** and shows the **IPv4 Address**, **Host Name** and **Tailnet**.

**Auth Key**

1. In the [Tailscale admin console](https://login.tailscale.com/admin/settings/keys), generate an auth key. Make it pre-approved; make it reusable if you set up several drones.
2. In UAVcast-Pro, choose **Tailscale**, open **Auth Key**, paste the key (`tskey-auth-…`) and optionally set **Hostname (Optional)**.
3. Select **Connect with Auth Key**.

Use this for drones without a browser at hand, or for setting up many drones the same way.

**Fleet Manager**

If the drone is [paired with Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/fleet-pairing/) and your organization has the VPN enabled, select **Connect to Fleet Manager VPN**. Connecting can take up to 30 seconds. The status then shows **Connected to Fleet Manager**.

Not paired yet? The tab says **Not Paired with Fleet Manager** and links to **Go to Fleet Manager Pairing**.

Install Tailscale on the ground station, log in to the same tailnet, and use its Tailscale IP (`100.x.y.z`) as the destination on Ground Control Stations.

When connected, **Interface Down** takes the Tailscale interface down without logging out, **Interface Up** brings it back, and **Logout** removes the device from the tailnet.

> **The Fleet Manager VPN replaces your own Tailscale login**
>
> The Fleet Manager VPN runs on Tailscale with Fleet Manager's own login server. Connecting to it logs the drone out of your own tailnet. If your SSH session runs over that tailnet, it drops. Do this from the local network.

## ZeroTier

Use this if you run your own ZeroTier network, for example in ZeroTier Central or on your own controller.

### Join the drone

1. In UAVcast-Pro, go to **Virtual Private Network**.
2. Set **Enable VPN** to **Yes**.
3. In **Services**, choose **ZeroTier**.
4. Paste your 16-character network ID into **Network ID** and select **Join Network**.
5. Authorize the drone in your ZeroTier controller if the network is private. The **ZeroTier Network** panel then shows **Connected** and the **Device IP**.

**ACCESS_DENIED** means the member isn't authorized yet.

### Join the ground station

1. Install [ZeroTier One](https://www.zerotier.com/download/) on the ground station computer.
2. Join the same network ID: on Windows and macOS from the ZeroTier tray or menu-bar icon (**Join New Network**); on Linux with `sudo zerotier-cli join <network-id>`.
3. Authorize it in your controller and note the IP address it gets.

On [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/), set **Destination IP or Host** to the ground station's **ZeroTier** IP. Telemetry and video now go through the VPN.

> **Switching between Wi-Fi and 4G**
>
> ZeroTier and Tailscale follow the best available network. You can start on Wi-Fi at the field and the link moves to the modem when Wi-Fi goes out of range, without changing any address.

## Settings reference

| Setting | Default | Values | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Enable VPN** | **No** | **Yes**, **No** |  |
| **Services** | **ZeroTier** | **ZeroTier**, **Tailscale** | Disabled until VPN is enabled. |
| **Network ID** (ZeroTier) | empty | 16-character ZeroTier network ID | From your own ZeroTier controller. |
| **Auth Key** (Tailscale) | empty | `tskey-auth-…` |  |
| **Hostname (Optional)** (Tailscale) | system hostname | text | Name shown in the Tailscale admin console. |

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| ZeroTier shows **ACCESS_DENIED** | Authorize the member in your ZeroTier controller. |
| Connected, but no telemetry at the ground station | The destination still uses the LAN IP. Use the ground station's VPN IP, and allow UDP 14550 and 5600 in its firewall. |
| *No VPN Information Available* | VPN is disabled or the service isn't running. Check **Enable VPN** and the **Action Logs**. |
| Tailscale web login shows *No Authentication URL* | Use the **Auth Key** tab instead. |

The interfaces appear on the [Networks](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/networks/) page as `zt…` (ZeroTier) or `tailscale0`, marked **VPN**.

Still stuck? See [VPN connected but the drone can't be reached](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/vpn-cant-reach-drone/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/vpn/


---

# Dynamic DNS

> Keep a hostname pointed at your drone's changing public IP with UAVcast-Pro Dynamic DNS (No-IP, DynDNS, DuckDNS or a generic URL), and when a VPN is the better choice.

Dynamic DNS keeps a hostname, such as `mydrone.ddns.net`, pointed at the drone's current public IP address. UAVcast-Pro checks the public IP every 5 minutes and updates your DNS provider when it changes. Open **Dynamic DNS** in the sidebar.

> **Most cellular links need a VPN instead**
>
> Dynamic DNS only helps if the drone's public IP can receive incoming connections. Most mobile operators put SIM cards behind carrier-grade NAT, so the public IP belongs to the operator, not to your drone. Use a [VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/vpn/) unless your SIM has a public (often "static" or "M2M") IP address.

Dynamic DNS doesn't change where UAVcast-Pro sends telemetry and video: those always go to the IP addresses on [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/). It's for reaching the drone's web interface or SSH from outside.

## Set it up

1. Create a hostname with your DNS provider (No-IP, DynDNS or DuckDNS).
2. In UAVcast-Pro, go to **Dynamic DNS**. Set **Enable Dynamic DNS?** to **Yes**.
3. Choose your **DNS System**.
4. Enter your account username (the field is labelled **Dynamic DNS configuration**), your **Password** and the hostname in **Alias**. For DuckDNS, put your token in the username field and anything in **Password** (the form requires it, DuckDNS ignores it). Fields save as you leave them.
5. Select **Connect** to start the updater. It sends the current IP straight away and then checks every 5 minutes. **Disconnect** stops it.

![Dynamic DNS Manager with Enable Dynamic DNS set to No, empty username, password and alias fields, and DNS System noip](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/dynamic-dns.webp)

*Dynamic DNS Manager before it is enabled.*

## Settings reference

| Setting | Default | Values | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Enable Dynamic DNS?** | **No** | **Yes**, **No** |  |
| **DNS System** | **No-IP** | **No-IP**, **DynDNS**, **DuckDNS**, **Generic** |  |
| **DNS URL** | empty | update URL | Only for **Generic**. The provider's DynDNS-compatible update URL. |
| **Dynamic DNS configuration** (username) | empty |  | Your DNS account username, or your token for DuckDNS. The UI labels this field oddly; it is the username. |
| **Password** | empty |  | Your DNS account password. Required by the form; ignored for DuckDNS. |
| **Alias** | empty | hostname | The hostname to update, for example `mydrone.ddns.net`. |
| Update interval | 5 minutes | fixed |  |

The **Dynamic DNS** row on the [Dashboard](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/dashboard/) shows whether the updater is running. The **Action Logs** show each update and the provider's reply.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/dynamic-dns/


---

# Networks

> See every network interface on the drone and choose whether Wi-Fi or the 4G/LTE modem carries the traffic, so the link stays on cellular when you fly out of Wi-Fi range.

The Networks page shows every network interface on the drone (Ethernet, Wi-Fi, modem, VPN) and which one is the default route. It's also where you choose whether Wi-Fi or the cellular modem is preferred when both are connected. Open **Networks** in the sidebar.

![Networks page with summary cards, Network Priority set to Auto, and the interfaces table listing eth0 and wlan0](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/networks.webp)

*Networks with Auto (System Default) active and Wi-Fi as the default route.*

## Choose the network priority

When Wi-Fi and the modem are both connected, Linux sends traffic through the one with the lowest route metric. **Network Priority** sets those metrics for you:

| Option | Use it when | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **WiFi Priority (Indoor Mode)** | On the bench or at home, to save mobile data. | Wi-Fi metric 100, modem metric 600. |
| **Modem Priority (Outdoor Mode)** | Before every flight over cellular. | Modem metric 100, Wi-Fi metric 600. |
| **Auto (System Default)** | You don't want UAVcast-Pro to change anything. | NetworkManager's own metrics. |

> **Switch to Modem Priority before take-off**
>
> If the drone takes off on Wi-Fi priority, the link stays on Wi-Fi until Wi-Fi is lost, then has to fail over to the modem in the air. That causes a gap in telemetry and video. Select **Modem Priority (Outdoor Mode)** on the ground.

The change applies to the active connections without restarting them (*Applying changes...*).

> **Which connections are changed**
>
> The Wi-Fi metric is set on the NetworkManager connection named `preconfigured`, which is the name Raspberry Pi Imager gives the Wi-Fi you enter while flashing. Wi-Fi set up any other way keeps its own metric, and Ethernet is never changed.

## Interface information

The summary cards show **Active Interfaces**, **Default Gateway** (and the interface it goes through) and **Total Interfaces**. **Network Interfaces** lists each interface with **Name**, **IP Address**, **Gateway**, **Status** (**Active**, **Inactive**, **VPN**), **Speed**, **Type** and which one is **Default**.

Common interface names:

| Name | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `eth0`, `end0` | Wired Ethernet |
| `wlan0` | Wi-Fi |
| `ppp0`, `wwan0` | Traditional modem |
| `usb0`, `eth1` | HiLink modem |
| `zt…` | ZeroTier |
| `tailscale0` | Tailscale |

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/networks/


---

# Camera settings

> Set up a Raspberry Pi camera or USB webcam in UAVcast-Pro and stream low-latency H.264 video over UDP to QGroundControl or Mission Planner. Resolution, FPS and bitrate.

UAVcast-Pro captures video from a Raspberry Pi CSI camera or a USB webcam, encodes it as H.264 and sends it as RTP over UDP to every ground station that has **Enable Video** turned on. Mission Planner and QGroundControl play it directly on port 5600. A copy of the stream feeds the live preview in the web interface and the on-drone recorder. Open **Camera → Camera settings**.

![Camera Control Panel with CAM 1 set to a Raspberry Pi camera, camera settings for resolution, FPS, bitrate and stream recovery, and the Live Preview panel](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/camera.webp)

*Camera → Camera settings with a Raspberry Pi camera as CAM 1 at 1536×864 and 30 FPS, bitrate Auto. Live Preview is off here.*

## Set up the camera

1. Connect the camera and go to **Camera → Camera settings**.
2. Set **Enable Camera?** to **Yes**.
3. Click the **CAM 1** slot and pick the camera. CSI cameras show as *Raspberry Pi Camera - imx708 (CSI)* or similar; USB cameras by their name.
4. Under **Camera Settings**, pick a **Resolution** your camera supports. Unsupported sizes are marked.
5. Leave **Select FPS** on **Auto** and **Bitrate** at `0` (auto) to start with.
6. Under **Stream Settings**, tick **Enable Live Preview?** and select **Start**.
7. On [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/), turn on **Enable Video** for each ground station that should get video.

If no camera appears in the list, see the **Action Logs** at the bottom of the page: they show every device the camera detector checked and why it was skipped.

## Settings reference

| Setting | Default | Values | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Enable Camera?** | **Yes** | **Yes**, **No** | **No** stops video entirely. |
| **CAM 1** | Raspberry Pi camera | Detected cameras, **Enter Custom Pipeline** | Pick **Enter Custom Pipeline** to write your own GStreamer pipeline. See [Custom pipeline](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/custom-pipeline/). |
| **Resolution** | `640x480` | Sizes the camera reports | If the camera can't deliver the size, UAVcast-Pro falls back to the largest supported size and logs which one it used. |
| **Select FPS** | **Auto** | **Auto** or the rates the camera supports at this resolution | **Auto** lets the camera choose. |
| **Bitrate** | `0` (**Auto**) | 0–10000 kbps, in steps of 100 | Set a fixed value for cellular links. |
| **Stream Recovery Rate** | **Auto** | **Auto** (0), 1, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 90, 120 frames | Keyframe interval. Lower values recover faster after packet loss and fix grey smearing over VPN, at the cost of bandwidth. |
| **Flip Settings** | Off | **Vertical Flip**, **Horizontal Flip** | CSI cameras. |
| **Rotation** | `0°` | 0°, 90°, 180°, 270° | USB and other non-CSI cameras. |
| **Enable Live Preview?** | On | On, off | Preview on this page and on the Flight Map. Recording also uses this copy of the stream. |

Settings save as you change them. If a running stream doesn't pick up a change, select **Restart** under **Stream Settings**.

## Pick settings for your link

There's no single right setting: the bitrate must fit inside the slowest part of the link with room left for telemetry. Starting points for one camera:

| Link | Resolution | FPS | Bitrate | Stream Recovery Rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local Wi-Fi or Ethernet | 1920x1080 | 30 | 4000–6000 kbps | Auto |
| Good 4G/LTE | 1280x720 | 30 | 1500–2500 kbps | 30 frames |
| Weak 4G or long range | 1280x720 or 854x480 | 15–20 | 800–1200 kbps | 15 frames |

If the picture freezes or smears grey after packet loss, lower the bitrate first, then lower **Stream Recovery Rate** so keyframes come more often.

### CPU load

The **System load** indicator shows how hard the encoder works. On a Raspberry Pi 5 every stream is encoded in software (the Pi 5 has no H.264 encoder), so high resolutions or two streams can max out the CPU. When it warns *CPU is near its limit. Lower the resolution or bitrate.*, do that before you fly.

## Live preview

**Live Preview** plays the stream in the browser through the built-in media server (WebRTC on port **8889**). It's a few hundred milliseconds behind the UDP stream your ground station gets, depending on the network. Use the open-in-new-tab button to watch it full screen. Browsers start the preview muted; unmute it in the player if you use [audio](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/audio/).

The preview needs the browser to reach port 8889 on the drone directly. It works on the LAN and over a VPN, but not through Fleet Manager's **Open via Proxy**, which only carries the web interface. Use **Open via VPN** for the preview.

## How the stream is sent

| Stream | Transport | Port on the ground station |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Camera 1 video | H.264, RTP over UDP | **Video Port** (default `5600`) |
| Camera 2 video (dual stream) | H.264, RTP over UDP | **Video Port (Camera 2)**, default Video Port + 1 (`5601`) |
| Audio (optional) | Opus, RTP over UDP | Video Port + 2 (`5602`) |
| Preview | WebRTC | Browser to drone, port 8889 |

The drone pushes the stream to the ground station. The ground station doesn't need to request it, and nothing on the drone listens for incoming video connections.

## Related

- [Two cameras: RC switching and dual stream](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/multi-camera/)
- [Audio](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/audio/)
- [Recordings and flight review](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/recordings/)
- [Custom GStreamer pipeline](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/custom-pipeline/)
- [Troubleshooting: camera not detected](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/camera-not-detected/)
- [Troubleshooting: choppy or delayed video](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/choppy-or-delayed-video/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/

# Two cameras: RC switching and dual stream

> Connect two cameras to UAVcast-Pro and switch between them from your RC transmitter, or stream both at once to QGroundControl or Mission Planner on separate UDP ports.

UAVcast-Pro handles two cameras, for example a forward FPV camera and a downward or gimbal camera. You can use them in two ways:

- **Switching**: one stream, and you choose which camera feeds it, from the web interface or from an RC channel on your transmitter. Uses the bandwidth and CPU of one stream.
- **Dual stream**: both cameras stream at the same time, each to its own UDP port, each with its own resolution, FPS and bitrate. Uses twice the bandwidth and CPU.

Supported combinations: CSI + USB, two USB cameras, or two CSI cameras on boards with two camera connectors (Raspberry Pi 5, Compute Module carrier boards).

## Add the second camera

1. Go to **Camera → Camera settings**. Make sure **CAM 1** has a camera.
2. Select **Add Camera** next to CAM 1 and pick the second camera. It appears in the **CAM 2** slot.
3. Click a slot to make that camera the active one (*Click to switch to Camera 2*).

In switching mode both cameras share Camera 1's resolution and frame rate (*Resolution and FPS from Camera 1 will be used*). If Camera 2 doesn't support that size, it uses its native resolution and is scaled, unless you turn on **Match Camera 1 Resolution** for a camera that supports it.

## Switch cameras from your RC transmitter

**RC Channel Switching** appears when two cameras are set and dual stream is off.

1. On your transmitter, assign a two-position switch to a free channel, for example channel 7. Check in Mission Planner or on **Flight Map → Radio** that the channel moves between about 1000 and 2000 µs.
2. Under **RC Channel Switching**, turn on **Enable RC channel camera switching**.
3. Pick the **RC Channel**.
4. Flip the switch and watch **Current PWM**. Below 1500 selects Camera 1, above 1500 selects Camera 2.

![Camera Control Panel with CAM 1 filled and an empty Add Camera slot](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/camera--control-panel.webp)

*The camera slots: CAM 1 in use and Add Camera for the second camera. RC Channel Switching shows up once both slots are filled and dual stream is off.*

While RC switching is on, clicking a camera slot does nothing: the transmitter is in control. Turn RC switching off to choose cameras by hand.

| Setting | Default | Values | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Enable RC channel camera switching** | Off | On, off |  |
| **RC Channel** | Channel 7 | Channel 1–18 | Read from the flight controller's RC input. |
| Switch point | 1500 µs | fixed | PWM < 1500 = Camera 1, PWM > 1500 = Camera 2. |

## Stream both cameras at once (dual stream)

1. With two cameras set, turn on **Dual stream** on the Camera page. The badge shows **Both live**.
2. Under **Per-camera settings**, set resolution, FPS and bitrate for each camera.
3. On [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/), each destination now has **Video Port (Camera 2)**. Leave it empty to use **Video Port** + 1 (`5601`), or enter another port. With several destinations on one computer, space their video ports 3 apart (`5600`, `5603` …) so camera 2 and audio don't land on another destination's port.
4. Set up a second video receiver on the ground station for that port.

Camera 1 goes to each ground station's **Video Port** (default `5600`), Camera 2 to **Video Port (Camera 2)** (default `5601`).

QGroundControl shows one video stream at a time. To watch Camera 2, run a second receiver, for example a second QGroundControl instance on port 5601, Mission Planner with a GStreamer source on 5601, or GStreamer directly:

```bash
gst-launch-1.0 udpsrc port=5601 caps="application/x-rtp, media=(string)video, clock-rate=(int)90000, encoding-name=(string)H264" ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! autovideosink sync=false
```

> **Watch the CPU and the link**
>
> Two streams double the encoding load and the bandwidth. Keep an eye on **System load** (*CPU is near its limit. Lower a stream's resolution/bitrate, or turn off the second stream.*) and keep the combined bitrate well inside your cellular uplink. A common split is 1280x720 at 1500 kbps for the main camera and 854x480 at 600 kbps for the second.

The Flight Map shows one video window per active stream. Recordings can include both cameras: see **Record camera 2** in [Recordings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/recordings/).

## Troubleshooting

- **Second camera missing from the list**: two CSI cameras need a board with two camera ports. On a Raspberry Pi, reboot after installing UAVcast-Pro: the installer enlarges the camera memory pool (CMA) so two cameras can run together.
- **Camera 2 picture stretched**: Camera 2 is scaled to Camera 1's resolution in switching mode. Use cameras with the same aspect ratio, or turn on **Match Camera 1 Resolution**.
- **Switch does nothing**: check **Current PWM**. *No signal* means the flight controller isn't reporting RC input on that channel.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/multi-camera/


---

# Audio

> Add sound from a USB microphone or a webcam's built-in mic to the UAVcast-Pro live preview, and send it to ground stations as an RTP/Opus stream on Video Port + 2.

UAVcast-Pro can add sound from a USB microphone or a USB camera's built-in mic. Audio is encoded as Opus, which costs little CPU and bandwidth. It always plays in the live preview, and you can also send it to your ground stations as a separate RTP stream. Find it in the **Audio** card on **Camera → Camera settings**.

## Turn on audio

1. Plug in a USB microphone, or use a webcam with a built-in mic.
2. On **Camera → Camera settings**, turn on **Audio**.
3. Leave **Audio device** on **Auto (camera microphone if present)**, or pick a device. Use **Test tone (no microphone needed)** to test the path without a mic.
4. Watch the indicator. **Audio live** with a moving level meter means sound is captured.
5. In **Live Preview**, unmute the player. Browsers start the preview muted.

![Audio card on the Camera page with the Audio switch off and the status Audio off](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/camera--audio.webp)

*Camera → Audio, switched off. Turn it on to choose the microphone and bitrate.*

A microphone that fails never interrupts the video. The indicator shows **Audio error** with the reason instead.

## Send audio to ground stations

Turn on **Send audio to ground stations**. UAVcast-Pro then sends a separate RTP/Opus stream to every ground station that receives video, on that destination's **Video Port + 2**. With the default video port that's `5602`. Two destinations on the same computer therefore need video ports at least 3 apart, for example `5600` and `5603`.

QGroundControl and Mission Planner ignore audio. Play it with GStreamer:

```bash
gst-launch-1.0 udpsrc port=5602 caps="application/x-rtp, media=(string)audio, clock-rate=(int)48000, encoding-name=(string)OPUS, payload=(int)97" ! rtpopusdepay ! opusdec ! audioconvert ! autoaudiosink
```

The stream is Opus at 48 kHz, RTP payload type 97. VLC can play it with an SDP file that describes those values.

## Settings reference

| Setting | Default | Values | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
