| **Audio** | Off | On, off | Changing any audio setting restarts the camera service. |
| **Audio device** | **Auto (camera microphone if present)** | Auto, detected capture devices, **Test tone (no microphone needed)** | A saved device that is unplugged shows as *(not connected)*. |
| **Bitrate** | `64 kbps` | 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128 kbps | 32–64 kbps is plenty for speech and engine noise. |
| **Send audio to ground stations** | Off | On, off | RTP/Opus to Video Port + 2 on every destination with video enabled. |

## Troubleshooting

- *No audio capture device found*: plug in a USB microphone or a camera with a built-in mic. On the drone, `arecord -l` lists capture devices.
- **No signal**: the device is open but silent. Check the mic's mute switch, or try **Test tone**.
- Audio in the preview but not on the ground station: make sure **Send audio to ground stations** is on, that the destination has **Enable Video** on, and that your receiver listens on Video Port + 2.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/audio/


---

# Custom GStreamer pipeline

> Use a custom GStreamer pipeline in UAVcast-Pro to stream an RTSP IP camera, a thermal camera, H.265 or a test pattern, with examples and how preview and destinations behave.

When the built-in camera support doesn't cover your camera, give UAVcast-Pro your own GStreamer pipeline. Typical cases are an RTSP IP or gimbal camera, a thermal camera, H.265, or sending to a fixed address. UAVcast-Pro runs the pipeline as the camera service, restarts it if it fails, and can still feed the live preview and the recorder.

## Set up a custom pipeline

1. Go to **Camera → Camera settings**.
2. Click the **CAM 1** slot and choose **Enter Custom Pipeline**.
3. Type the pipeline in **Custom Pipeline**, without the `gst-launch-1.0` prefix. (If you paste it with the prefix, UAVcast-Pro strips it.)
4. Select **Start** (or **Restart**) and check the **Action Logs** for errors.

> **A custom pipeline ignores your ground station list**
>
> The pipeline decides where video goes. **Video Port** and **Enable Video** on [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/) have no effect: put the ground station's address and port in the pipeline's `udpsink`.

Test the pipeline over SSH with `gst-launch-1.0 -v <pipeline>` before you paste it. The error messages are clearer there.

## Examples

```text
videotestsrc ! x264enc ! video/x-h264, stream-format=byte-stream ! rtph264pay ! udpsink host=192.168.0.100 port=5600
```

```text
rtspsrc location=rtsp://192.168.144.25:8554/main.264 latency=0 ! rtph264depay ! h264parse ! rtph264pay config-interval=1 pt=96 ! udpsink host=10.147.17.20 port=5600 sync=false
```

```text
v4l2src device=/dev/video0 ! video/x-raw,width=1280,height=720,framerate=30/1 ! videoconvert ! x264enc tune=zerolatency speed-preset=superfast bitrate=1500 key-int-max=30 ! h264parse config-interval=1 ! rtph264pay pt=96 ! udpsink host=10.147.17.20 port=5600 sync=false
```

```text
videotestsrc ! x264enc tune=zerolatency ! rtph264pay pt=96 ! multiudpsink clients=10.147.17.20:5600,10.147.17.21:5600
```

Replace the IP addresses with your ground stations' addresses (VPN addresses over 4G).

## Live preview and recording

With **Enable Live Preview?** ticked, UAVcast-Pro adds a branch to your pipeline that sends the encoded video to the built-in media server, so the preview, the Flight Map video window and recording keep working. It finds the right place automatically:

- If your pipeline has `tee name=t`, it adds a branch from that tee.
- Otherwise it splits the stream just before `rtph264pay` or `rtph265pay`.
- For an RTSP source without a recognised parser, it leaves the pipeline as it is, and there's no preview.

For the most predictable result, end your encoded stream with `h264parse` and a `tee name=t`, and put your own `udpsink` on a branch of that tee.

## Limits

- Dual stream, RC switching and per-camera settings don't apply to a custom pipeline. The pipeline is the whole video setup.
- Resolution, FPS, bitrate and flip settings are hidden, because the pipeline sets them.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/custom-pipeline/


---

# Recordings and flight review

> Record camera video and MAVLink telemetry on the drone with UAVcast-Pro, automatically when armed, to the SD card or a USB SSD, and review flights with video, map and data.

UAVcast-Pro records each flight on the drone itself: the camera video and a MAVLink telemetry log (`.tlog`). Recording uses the stream that is already encoded, so it costs no extra CPU and never interrupts the live video to your ground station. Because the files are written on the drone, you get full-quality video even when the cellular link drops. Recordings start automatically when you arm, or by hand from the Flight Map. Requires v6.5.1 or later.

Open **Camera → Recordings**. It has two tabs: **Library** and **Settings**.

![Recordings library with a storage bar and two recorded flights with durations, CAM 1 and Telemetry badges](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/camera--recordings.webp)

*Camera → Recordings → Library with two recorded flights.*

## Record automatically when armed

This is on by default. Recording starts when the motors arm and stops when they disarm. If the link drops in flight, recording carries on.

Before you rely on it:

- Check the free space in **Recording storage** on the Flight Map or in **Settings**.
- Recording doesn't need **Enable Live Preview?**. With recording on, the camera keeps a copy of the stream in the built-in media server even when the preview is off.

## Record by hand

The Flight Map's top bar has a **Recording** group: **CAM 1** (and **CAM 2** with dual stream) to start and stop video, and **Telemetry** to start and stop a telemetry log. A red dot shows what is recording. Read-only users can't start recordings.

## Storage settings

Open **Camera → Recordings → Settings**.

| Setting | Default | Values | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Storage location** | **Internal storage** | Internal storage, a detected USB drive or SSD, **Or another folder** | Plug in a disk and select **Look for disks again** to see it. Internal storage is `/opt/uavcast-pro/recordings/video`. |
| **Keep free** | `2` GB | 0.5–1000 GB | Recording never fills the disk past this. The system needs room too. |
| **Delete oldest recordings when space runs low** | On | On, off | Like a dashcam: recording never stops for lack of space. Off: recording stops instead. |
| **Delete recordings older than** | `0` days | 0–3650 days | `0` keeps recordings until the space is needed. |
| **Record automatically when armed** | On | On, off |  |
| **Record camera 1** | On | On, off | Applies to automatic recording. |
| **Record camera 2** | On | On, off | Only when dual stream is on. |
| **File length** | `1` min | 1–30 min | Video is saved in pieces of this length. Shorter pieces lose less after a power cut. |
| **Record telemetry** | **While armed** | **While armed**, **Always while connected**, **Off** | The `.tlog` shown next to the video. **Always** also logs on the ground and starts a new file at every arm, disarm and hour. |

![Recordings settings with Internal storage selected, 2 GB keep free, delete oldest recordings on and record automatically when armed on](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/camera--recordings-settings.webp)

*Internal storage selected, with automatic recording on arm.*

> **Record to a USB SSD**
>
> A USB 3 SSD is faster and far more durable than a microSD card for continuous video. Plug it in, select **Look for disks again**, then pick it under **Storage location**.

## Files and formats

- Video is written as fragmented MP4 segments, which stay playable if power is cut mid-flight. Downloads are MP4.
- Telemetry is a standard MAVLink `.tlog`, readable in Mission Planner, MAVExplorer, UAV Log Viewer and [Flight Analytics](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-map/flight-analytics/).
- A recording in the library is one clip as long as its files follow each other without a gap of more than 15 seconds.

## Review a flight

Select **Play** on a recording to open **Flight review**: the video, the map track, the cockpit view and the flight data on one timeline.

- The timeline marks **Armed**, **Disarmed** and flight-mode changes.
- **Back 10 seconds**, **Play**/**Pause**, **Forward 10 seconds** and **Playback speed** (0.5× to 4×).
- With two cameras, **Change video layout** switches between **Picture in picture** and **Side by side**; **Show this camera large** swaps them.
- The data panel shows **Altitude**, **Speed**, **Battery**, **Satellites** and **Mode** at the current moment.
- **Download** saves the clip as MP4.

![Flight review player with the video area, map track, cockpit view and a timeline with playback controls](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/camera--flight-review.webp)

*Flight review: video, map, cockpit and telemetry on one timeline.*

If the player says *No telemetry log for this recording*, telemetry wasn't recording at the time (by default it only logs while armed).

## Delete recordings

Select **Delete** on a recording. If it has a telemetry log you choose **Delete video only** or **Delete video and telemetry**. Deleting is permanent. A recording that is still running must be stopped first.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/recordings/


---

# Pair with Fleet Manager

> Connect a drone running UAVcast-Pro to UAVmatrix Fleet Manager: get the pairing code on the drone, enter it in Fleet Manager, check the connection, rename or unpair.

Pairing connects a drone running UAVcast-Pro to your organization in [UAVmatrix Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/), the cloud dashboard for your fleet. Once paired, the drone keeps a certificate-authenticated, encrypted connection to Fleet Manager and reconnects by itself after a reboot or a network change. You start pairing on the drone and finish it in Fleet Manager. It takes about two minutes.

## Before you begin

- UAVcast-Pro with an **activated license** on the drone. Pairing is refused without one (*No valid license found. Please activate your license first.*).
- An **admin** user in UAVcast-Pro. **Fleet Management** is hidden for read-only users.
- A Fleet Manager account with the **Owner** or **Admin** role in the organization. The drone's license must belong to a member of that organization.
- Internet on the drone, with outbound TCP **8883** (MQTT over TLS) and HTTPS (443) allowed.

## Pair the drone

1. On the drone's web interface, go to **Management → Fleet Management**.
2. Select **Connect to Fleet Manager**. The drone asks Fleet Manager for a code and shows a **Pairing Code** with an **Expires in** countdown, then *Waiting for Manager to confirm pairing...*.
3. In another tab, sign in at [fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com](https://fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/) and go to **Fleet → Pair Device**.
4. Enter the code from the drone and confirm the device details (hostname, architecture, UAVcast-Pro version) match the drone in front of you.
5. Finish the steps in Fleet Manager (VPN choice and name).
6. Back on the drone, the page switches to **Fleet Connection** with status **Connected**.

![Connect to Fleet Manager card with the Connect to Fleet Manager button](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/fleet--connect.webp)

*Management → Fleet Management on a drone that isn't paired yet. Selecting Connect to Fleet Manager replaces this card with the 8-digit Pairing Code and its Expires in countdown.*

> **The code is valid for 5 minutes**
>
> If it runs out before you enter it, select **Connect to Fleet Manager** again for a new code.

The Fleet Manager side, including organizations, VPN and what to do with the drone once it's in the fleet, is covered in [Add your first drone to Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/).

## After pairing

The **Fleet Connection** card shows:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Connected** / **Disconnected** | Whether the drone is talking to Fleet Manager right now. |
| **Device Name** | The name shown in Fleet Manager. Edit it here or in Fleet Manager. *Managed by Fleet Manager* means the name is set there. |
| **Hostname**, **Device ID** | How Fleet Manager identifies this drone. |
| **Manager URL** | The Fleet Manager instance the drone is paired with. |
| **Last Connected** | When the drone last reached Fleet Manager. |

What Fleet Manager gets from the drone: live telemetry (position, battery, GPS, flight state), UAVcast-Pro system status, and remote service control. Ground station destinations that Fleet Manager creates through stream bindings show up on [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/) with a cloud icon.

To join the drone to your organization's VPN later, use the **Fleet Manager** tab on [Virtual Private Network](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/vpn/).

## Unpair

1. Go to **Management → Fleet Management**.
2. Select **Disconnect from Fleet** and confirm.

This removes the pairing and the drone's certificates. To use the drone in Fleet Manager again, pair it again with a new code. Remove the drone from your fleet in Fleet Manager too, so it doesn't stay listed as offline.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| *No valid license found. Please activate your license first.* | Activate the license on **Application**. See [Licensing & activation](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/). |
| Fleet Manager says the license isn't owned by a member of the organization | The license was bought with an email that isn't a member. Add that email in Fleet Manager (see [Licenses](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/)), or invite that account to the organization. |
| Code expired | Select **Connect to Fleet Manager** again. |
| Paired, but status stays **Disconnected** | The drone can't reach Fleet Manager on TCP 8883. Some networks block it. Check the drone's internet connection and firewall. |

More help: [Pairing code invalid](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/) and [Drone offline in Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/drone-offline-fleet-manager/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/fleet-pairing/


---

# Users & access

> Secure the UAVcast-Pro web interface with an admin login, add read-only users who can watch telemetry and video but not control the drone, and change or reset passwords.

A fresh UAVcast-Pro install has no users and no login: anyone who can open the web interface has full admin rights. Add an admin user to turn on the login. After that, you can add **Read Only** users for observers, customers or payload operators who should see everything but change nothing. Open **Management → Users**.

![Users page with the Add New User dialog open, with username, password, confirm password and role fields](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/users.webp)

*Management → Users with the Add New User dialog open.*

## Turn on the login

1. Go to **Users** and select **Add User**.
2. Enter a **Username** (at least 3 characters), a **Password** (at least 6 characters) and **Confirm Password**.
3. Select **Create User**. The first user is always an **Admin** (*First user must be an admin*).

From now on every visitor gets a login page. A login lasts 7 days on that browser, or until you select **Logout** in the user menu at the bottom of the sidebar.

> **The web interface uses plain HTTP**
>
> Logins and settings travel unencrypted. That's fine on your own LAN or inside a [VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/vpn/), but never forward the web interface's port to the internet.

## Roles

| Can… | **Admin** | **Read Only** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| See the Dashboard, Data Streams, Flight Controller, Flight Map, Ground Control Stations and Camera pages | Yes | Yes |
| Watch live video and telemetry, view dashboards and recordings | Yes | Yes |
| Change any setting | Yes | No |
| Arm, disarm, change mode, start or clear missions | Yes | No |
| Start or stop recordings | Yes | No |
| Open Modem, Virtual Private Network, Dynamic DNS, Networks, Fleet Management, Users and Application | Yes | No (hidden) |

You can't create a **Read Only** user before an admin exists (*Create an admin user first before adding read-only users*).

Read-only web users are different from the **Read Only** switch on a ground station destination, which blocks commands from a ground station program. See [Ground control stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/).

## Change a password

Select **Change Password**, enter the **Current Password** and the **New Password** twice, and select **Update Password**. Passwords are stored as bcrypt hashes.

## Delete a user

Select **Delete** on the user's row and confirm.

- You can't delete your own account while other users exist.
- Deleting the **last** user turns the login off again: *After deletion, the application will be open without authentication until a new user is created.*

## Forgot the admin password

There's no reset link, because the drone has no email, and password recovery isn't self-service.

- If another admin can still log in, they can delete your user under **Users** and create it again.
- If nobody with the admin role can log in, contact support at **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)**. Include your license key (or the email you bought it with), the device's hostname or name as shown under **Application → License Manager → Activated Devices**, the UAVcast-Pro version, and whether you can reach the device over SSH.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/users/


---

# Application settings, logs and backups

> Change the UAVcast-Pro web port and language, download logs for support with debug mode, and back up, restore or reset the settings database from the Application page.

The **Application** page holds everything about UAVcast-Pro itself: the license, updates, interface settings, log downloads and the settings database. It's only visible to admins, and it's the one page that works before the device is licensed. Open **Management → Application**.

![Application page with License Manager and Update Application on the left, and Settings, Logging and Database cards on the right](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/application.webp)

*Management → Application.*

| Card | Covered in |
| --- | --- |
| **License Manager** | [Licensing & activation](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/) |
| **Update Application** | [Update UAVcast-Pro](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/updating/) |
| **Settings**, **Logging**, **Database** | This page |

## Settings

| Setting | Default | Values | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Take a Tour** |  |  | Restarts the guided tour of the interface. |
| **Dark Theme** | On | On, off | Saved per browser. Also in the theme toggle in the top bar. |
| **Server Port** | `80` | 1–65535 | Port of the web interface. See below. |
| **Language** | Browser language, else English | English, Español, 简体中文, 繁體中文, Italiano, Nederlands, Polski, Português, Русский, Türkçe | Also in the user menu at the bottom of the sidebar. |

### Change the web interface port

1. Enter the new port in **Server Port**.
2. Select **Submit and restart server**. A dialog shows the **New URL**, for example `http://192.168.1.50:8080`.
3. Wait a few seconds and open the new URL.

Bookmarks and links to the old address stop working. A changed port shows the warning *The server port has been changed from the default port 80.* From UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3 the port is kept when you update; earlier versions reset it to 80.

## Logging

UAVcast-Pro logs every service separately. Download them when something goes wrong and send them to support.

1. Turn on **Debug Mode** for more detail. Reproduce the problem.
2. In **Select logs to download**, keep **All Logs** or pick one service.
3. In **Select time range**, choose a window that covers the problem (**Last 10 minutes** to **All Time**).
4. Select **Download**. You get a zip file.
5. Email it to [support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com) with a short description of what happened. Turn **Debug Mode** off again afterwards.

The download includes a `diagnostics.txt` snapshot (settings, serial ports, power and USB events) that speeds up support.

| Log | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| **Mavlink Manager**, **Mavlink Publisher** | Flight controller link, routing to ground stations |
| **Camera Server**, **Camera Detector** | Video pipeline, camera detection |
| **Modem Manager**, **Modem Detector** | Modem connection, APN attempts |
| **VPN Manager** | ZeroTier and Tailscale |
| **NTRIP Client** | RTK corrections |
| **DNS Manager** | Dynamic DNS updates |
| **License Manager** | Activation and the 4-hourly license check |
| **Application Updater**, **Application Installer** | Updates and installs |
| **Backend API Server** | The internal API |

**Prune All Logs** deletes all log files. It can't be undone; do it before reproducing a problem if you want a clean log. On the drone, logs are in `/opt/uavcast-pro/logs`.

Every page also has an **Action Logs** console that shows the live log of that page's service.

## Database

All settings (ground stations, flight controller, camera, modem, VPN, NTRIP, users, dashboards, injectors, license data) live in one SQLite database, `/opt/uavcast-pro/uavcast.db`.

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Backup Database** | Downloads the database as `uavcast_backup.db`. |
| **Restore Database** | Uploads a `.db` backup and replaces the current settings, users included. |
| **Reset Database** | Resets ground stations, flight controller, camera, VPN and Dynamic DNS settings to their defaults. Users, license, modem, NTRIP, recording settings, dashboards, injectors and Fleet Manager pairing are kept. Can't be undone. |

Use backups to keep a known-good configuration before changes, or to set up a second drone the same way. Reboot after a restore so every service starts with the restored settings.

> **Restoring on different hardware**
>
> The license data in the database is tied to the device it came from. After restoring a backup on another Pi or SD card, activate the license on the new device. Restore also brings over the users and passwords from the backup.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/application-settings/


---

# Fleet Manager

> UAVmatrix Fleet Manager tracks every UAVcast-Pro drone on one live map, with remote control, missions, VPN streaming to ground stations and team roles.

UAVmatrix Fleet Manager is a web app at [fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com](https://fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/) for running many drones from one place. Every drone that runs UAVcast-Pro can be paired to your organization. After that you see it on a live map, open its terminal, send commands, upload missions and route its video and telemetry to the ground stations your pilots use.

![Fleet Manager dashboard with stats cards, UAV status list and recent activity](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/dashboard.webp)

*Dashboard: stats cards, the UAV Status list and Recent Activity from several team members.*

## What you can do with it

[Add your first dronePair a UAVcast-Pro drone with an 8-digit code in about two minutes.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/)[Track the fleet liveEvery drone on one map, with status rings, a 5-minute trail and follow mode.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/map/)[Control drones remotelyFlight modes, arm and disarm, missions and preflight calibration from the browser.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remote-control/)[Stream to ground stationsSend video and MAVLink from many drones to QGroundControl or Mission Planner over VPN.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/stream-bindings/)[Invite your teamOwner, Admin and Viewer roles per organization.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/)[Plan missionsDraw waypoints, save missions for the organization and upload them to any drone.](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/missions/)

## How it fits together

Fleet Manager never talks to the flight controller directly. UAVcast-Pro on the drone's companion computer does that, and keeps one encrypted connection to Fleet Manager:

1. **Pairing.** UAVcast-Pro asks Fleet Manager for a pairing code. You type the code into Fleet Manager. Fleet Manager then hands the drone its own client certificate.
2. **Control channel.** The drone connects to Fleet Manager's MQTT broker over TLS on port **8883**, authenticated with that certificate. Telemetry, heartbeats, commands, terminal sessions and remote access to the UAVcast-Pro web interface all travel over this connection. It works through NAT and cellular networks because the drone always connects outward.
3. **Data channel (optional).** Video and MAVLink to a ground station go peer to peer over your organization's private VPN, a WireGuard network run by Fleet Manager. Without VPN, Fleet Manager still shows and controls the drone, but it doesn't route streams.

## Concepts

| Term | What it means in Fleet Manager |
| --- | --- |
| **Organization** | Your company or team. Drones, missions, the VPN network and members belong to one organization. Each user can own one organization and be a member of any number of others. |
| **UAV** | A drone (or rover, boat or other vehicle) running UAVcast-Pro, paired to one organization at a time. Fleet Manager identifies it by a device ID that UAVcast-Pro derives from the companion computer's CPU serial and boot disk, so it keeps its identity across reboots and network changes. |
| **Pairing** | Linking a UAV to an organization with an 8-digit code that UAVcast-Pro shows. The code is valid for 5 minutes. |
| **Ground station (GCS)** | A laptop or PC running QGroundControl, Mission Planner or similar, joined to your organization's VPN so it can receive streams. |
| **Stream binding** | A rule that says "send this UAV's video and telemetry to that ground station". Each binding gets its own UDP ports, so one ground station can receive many drones at once. |
| **Roles** | **Owner**, **Admin** or **Viewer**, set per organization. Viewers can watch; Admins and the Owner can pair, control and configure. See [Roles and permissions](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/roles-and-permissions/). |
| **Licenses and seats** | Every paired UAV needs an active UAVcast-Pro license owned by a member of the organization. Team members don't use up seats. See [Licenses](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/). |
| **Status and alerts** | Online, offline, no-MAVLink and GPS warnings on the map and fleet list, plus system announcements. See [Status indicators and notifications](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/alerts-and-status/). |

## What you need

Fleet Manager is included with your UAVcast-Pro license: no separate subscription, no extra seats.

> Fleet Manager is included with a UAVcast-Pro license. Each drone you pair needs one.
>
> [Buy UAVcast-Pro](https://uavmatrix.com/checkout) · [See plans and pricing](https://uavmatrix.com/products)

- A UAVmatrix account (the same one you use at [uavmatrix.com](https://uavmatrix.com/) to buy licenses).
- At least one companion computer with UAVcast-Pro installed and its license activated. See [Installation](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/installation/) and [Activate your license](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/).
- Internet on the drone with outbound HTTPS (443) and TCP **8883** open.

## Start here

1. [Set up your organization](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/set-up-organization/)
2. [Add your first drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/)
3. [Connect a ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/connect-gcs/)
4. [Invite your team](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/


---

# Set up your organization

> Sign in to Fleet Manager with your UAVmatrix account, create the organization your drones and team belong to, and switch, rename or delete it.

Everything in Fleet Manager belongs to an organization: drones, missions, the VPN network, stream bindings and team members. Create one before you pair your first drone.

## Sign in

Fleet Manager has no separate password. It signs you in with your UAVmatrix account, the same account you use at [uavmatrix.com](https://uavmatrix.com/) to buy and manage UAVcast-Pro licenses.

1. Go to [fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com](https://fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/) and select **Sign In** (or **Get Started**).
2. Sign in on the UAVmatrix page you are sent to. If you don't have an account yet, create one there.
3. You come back to the Fleet Manager **Dashboard**.

> **Sign in with the email that owns your licenses**
>
> Fleet Manager only accepts a drone when its UAVcast-Pro license is owned by a member of the organization, matched by email. Signing in with the account you bought the licenses with saves you a support request later. See [Licenses](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/).

Profile details (name, email, password) are managed in your UAVmatrix account, not in Fleet Manager. **Settings → Profile** links there.

## Create the organization

1. Open the organization switcher at the top of the sidebar and select **Create organization**. If you have no organization yet, pages such as **Fleet** and **Network** also show **No Organization Yet** with a **Create Organization** button.
2. Enter an **Organization Name** (2 to 50 characters), for example your company name or "Survey Operations North". Add a **Description (optional)** if you like.
3. Select **Create**.

![Create Organization dialog with Organization Name and Description fields](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/onboarding--create-organization.webp)

*Create Organization dialog, filled in with a company name such as Nordic Aerial Survey AS.*

You become the organization's **Owner**. Fleet Manager also creates a private VPN network for the organization in the background. It stays off until you [enable VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/).

> **One organization per owner**
>
> Each user can create (own) one organization. If you try to create a second one, Fleet Manager answers **You already own an organization**. You can still be an Admin or Viewer in any number of other organizations, for example a customer's or a partner's.

## Switch between organizations

If you belong to more than one organization, the switcher at the top of the sidebar lists them under **Organizations**. The organization you pick decides what **Fleet**, **Fleet Map**, **Missions**, **Network** and the dashboard show. Fleet Manager remembers your choice in this browser.

![Sidebar organization switcher open, listing two organizations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/dashboard--organization-switcher.webp)

*Organization switcher open, listing Nordwind Aerial Services and Nordwind R&D Sandbox.*

## Rename or delete the organization

Go to **Settings → Organizations**. The tab lists the organizations where you are Owner or Admin.

- **Rename or change the description:** Owner or Admin. Edit **Name** or **Description** and select **Save Changes**.
- **Delete:** Owner only. Select **Delete Organization** and confirm. This removes all drones, their telemetry history, missions, stream bindings and team memberships, and it can't be undone.

![Settings Organizations tab with name, description and Delete Organization button](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/settings--organizations.webp)

*Settings → Organizations for the Owner, with Save Changes and Delete Organization.*

> **Unpair drones before you delete an organization**
>
> Deleting the organization doesn't tell the drones. They keep trying to reconnect until you select **Disconnect from Fleet** in UAVcast-Pro on each one. Remove the drones first from their UAV page (see [Remove or transfer a drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/)) so Fleet Manager unpairs them for you.

To hand the organization to someone else instead, [transfer ownership](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/#transfer-ownership).

## Next steps

- [Add your first drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/)
- [Invite your team](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/set-up-organization/


---

# Add your first drone

> Pair a UAVcast-Pro drone with your Fleet Manager organization using the 8-digit pairing code, choose VPN access and see it live on the fleet map.

Pairing links one drone running UAVcast-Pro to your organization. After pairing, the drone keeps a certificate-authenticated connection to Fleet Manager and reconnects by itself after a reboot or a change of network. You pair each drone once, and it takes about two minutes.

You work in two browser tabs: the drone's UAVcast-Pro web interface, and Fleet Manager. Keep both open.

## Before you begin

- **UAVcast-Pro installed with an activated license.** UAVcast-Pro refuses to start pairing without one and shows **No valid license found. Please activate your license first.** See [Activate your license](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/).
- **The license is owned by a member of your organization.** Fleet Manager compares the email of the license owner in the UAVmatrix store with the emails of your members. See [Licenses](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/).
- **Owner or Admin role** in the organization. Viewers don't see **Pair Device**. See [Roles and permissions](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/roles-and-permissions/).
- **Internet on the drone** over Ethernet, Wi-Fi or a cellular modem, with outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) and TCP **8883** open. Port 8883 carries the encrypted MQTT connection to Fleet Manager.
- **A current UAVcast-Pro 6 release.** Pairing starts from **Management → Fleet Management** in UAVcast-Pro. Arm and disarm and pre-flight calibration from Fleet Manager need UAVcast-Pro 6.3.0_rc13 or newer; Fleet Manager marks them with a version badge on older drones.

## Pair the drone

1. **Get a pairing code in UAVcast-Pro.** Open the drone's web interface. In the sidebar under **Management**, select **Fleet Management**, then **Connect to Fleet Manager**. UAVcast-Pro shows an 8-digit **Pairing Code**, an **Expires in** countdown and **Waiting for Manager to confirm pairing...**

   ![UAVcast-Pro Connect to Fleet Manager card with the Connect to Fleet Manager button](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/fleet--connect.webp)

   *UAVcast-Pro → Fleet Management before pairing. Selecting Connect to Fleet Manager shows the 8-digit code, the Expires in countdown and Waiting for Manager to confirm pairing...*

   > **The code is valid for 5 minutes**
   >
   > If the countdown runs out before you enter it, select **Connect to Fleet Manager** again. Always type the code that is on screen now: UAVcast-Pro only waits for its newest code.

2. **Open Pair Device in Fleet Manager.** Go to **Fleet** and select **Pair Device**. The **Pair UAV** wizard opens.

3. **Choose the organization.** On the **Organization** step, pick the organization this drone should belong to and select **Continue**. The list only shows organizations where you are Owner or Admin. If you have just one, Fleet Manager selects it and skips this step.

4. **Enter the code.** On the **Pairing Code** step, type the 8 digits and select **Continue**. Fleet Manager looks the code up and moves on to **Confirm Device**.

   ![Pair UAV wizard on the Pairing Code step with an 8-digit code entered](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/pair-device--code.webp)

   *Fleet → Pair Device, Pairing Code step, with the progress bar showing Organization completed.*

5. **Confirm the device.** Check the details UAVcast-Pro sent: **Name**, **Hostname**, **OS**, **Architecture** and **UAVcast Version**. Make sure they match the drone in front of you, then select **Complete Pairing**. If your organization has VPN enabled, the button says **Continue** and the next step is VPN.

   ![Confirm Device step listing name, hostname, OS, architecture and UAVcast version](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/pair-device--confirm.webp)

   *Confirm Device step: check that the name, hostname, OS, architecture and UAVcast Version match the drone in front of you.*

6. **Choose VPN access (only if VPN is enabled).** The **VPN Connection** step appears when the organization has [VPN enabled](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/). With VPN on, ground stations on your organization's network receive this drone's video and telemetry directly, over 4G, Wi-Fi or satellite, without port forwarding.

   - **Enable VPN for this UAV** is ticked by default. UAVcast-Pro joins your organization's VPN right after pairing.
   - If the drone is already on a Tailscale network, Fleet Manager shows **Existing VPN Connection Detected** with that network's server and IP. The box changes to **Replace existing VPN with Fleet Manager network** and is not ticked. Tick it only if you want the drone to leave its current network.

   Select **Complete Pairing**.

   ![VPN Connection step with the Enable VPN for this UAV checkbox ticked](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/pair-device--vpn.webp)

   *VPN Connection step, with the three benefits listed and Enable VPN for this UAV ticked.*

   > **Replacing a VPN can drop your SSH session**
   >
   > If you replace an existing Tailscale connection and your current SSH or browser session to the drone runs over it, that session drops. Connect to the drone over the local network before you continue, or use its new VPN address afterwards.

7. **Name the drone.** **Pairing Complete!** appears with a **UAV Name** field. Type a name your team will recognize on the map, such as the airframe's tail number or "Survey-14", and select **Save**. The name syncs to UAVcast-Pro when the drone is online. Select **View UAV** to open its page.

   ![Pairing Complete screen with UAV Name field and View UAV button](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/pair-device--complete.webp)

   *Pairing Complete! with the UAV Name field edited to a tail number.*

Meanwhile UAVcast-Pro, which checks back every 5 seconds, receives the drone's certificate and connection settings (and the VPN key, if you chose VPN). Its Fleet Management page switches to **Connected**.

## Check the connection

The drone appears on **Fleet** and on **Fleet Map** within a few seconds. Its badge shows:

| Badge | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **PAIRING** | Fleet Manager has issued the certificate and is waiting for the drone's first heartbeat. |
| **ONLINE** | The drone is connected. UAVcast-Pro sends a heartbeat every 5 seconds. |
| **OFFLINE** | Nothing received for 20 seconds. The card shows when the drone was last seen. |

If the badge stays on **PAIRING** or turns **OFFLINE**, check from the drone that it can reach Fleet Manager on port 8883:

```bash
nc -vz fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com 8883
```

A line ending in `succeeded!` means the port is open. Anything else points to a firewall or a carrier that blocks the port. See [Drone offline in Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/drone-offline-fleet-manager/).

## Send video and telemetry to a ground station

Pairing doesn't start any streams. To fly from QGroundControl or Mission Planner, [connect a ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/connect-gcs/) to the VPN and add a [stream binding](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/stream-bindings/). Fleet Manager gives each binding its own block of ports (video, room for camera 2 and audio, and telemetry), so several drones can stream to one ground station at once. The first drone uses the defaults, 5600 and 14550; read the others from the binding's **Ports** column.

## If pairing fails

| Message | Cause and fix |
| --- | --- |
| **Invalid pairing code** | No such code. Check the digits, or get a new code in UAVcast-Pro. |
| **This pairing code has expired** | More than 5 minutes passed. Select **Connect to Fleet Manager** again in UAVcast-Pro. |
| **This pairing code has already been used** | The code was claimed already, by you or a colleague. Check **Fleet** for the drone before you pair again. |
| **License is not owned by any member of this organization** | The license on the drone belongs to an email that isn't a member. Invite that person, or ask support to add the email to your account. See [Licenses](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/#licenses-bought-with-another-email). |
| **License has expired** / **License has been refunded** | The license on the drone is no longer active. Renew it or activate another license in UAVcast-Pro. |
| **This UAV is already paired to an organization** | The drone belongs to a different organization. It must be removed there first. See [Remove or transfer a drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/). |
| **Too many attempts. Please wait a minute and try again.** | More than 10 code checks or 5 pairing attempts in a minute. Wait a minute. |

More causes and checks: [Pairing code invalid or expired](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/).

## Pairing the same drone again

Pairing a drone again into the **same** organization keeps its name, telemetry history and stream bindings and only renews its certificate. You need this after you select **Disconnect from Fleet** in UAVcast-Pro, or when Fleet Manager shows **Re-pair required**. See [Re-pair a drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/#re-pair-a-drone).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/


---

# Connect a ground station

> Join a QGroundControl or Mission Planner laptop to your organization's VPN with one Tailscale command and start receiving drone video and telemetry.

A ground station (GCS) is the laptop or PC where a pilot runs QGroundControl, Mission Planner or similar. To receive a drone's video and telemetry through Fleet Manager, the ground station joins your organization's private VPN. After that you decide which drones stream to it with [stream bindings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/stream-bindings/).

This takes about five minutes per ground station.

## Before you begin

- **Owner or Admin role.** Viewers can see the **Network** page but not the auth key or the connection command, and can't enable VPN or configure devices. They see *Ask an Owner or Admin of this organization to connect a new device to the VPN.*
- **VPN enabled** for the organization. If **Network** shows **Enable VPN Network**, select it first. See [Network and VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/).
- **Admin rights on the ground station** computer, to install Tailscale and run one command.
- At least one drone [paired](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/) and joined to the VPN.

> **Fleet Manager runs its own VPN server**
>
> The organization's network uses the Tailscale client but Fleet Manager's own control server, not a tailscale.com account. You don't need to sign up for Tailscale. If the computer is already on another Tailscale network, the command below moves it to your organization's network.

## Join the ground station to the VPN

1. **Install Tailscale** on the ground station from [tailscale.com/download](https://tailscale.com/download) (Windows, macOS or Linux).

2. **Copy the connection command.** In Fleet Manager, open **Network**, stay on the **Devices** tab and find **Connect a Device**. Under **GCS Connection Command**, copy the command. It looks like this:

   ```bash
   tailscale up --authkey=<your-org-key> --login-server=https://vpn-connect.uavmatrix.com
   ```

   ![Connect a Device card with the GCS Computer Only warning and the tailscale up command](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/network--connect-device.webp)

   *Network → Devices → Connect a Device, with the GCS Computer Only warning and the copy button next to the command (auth key blurred).*

   > **For the ground station only**
   >
   > Don't paste this command into UAVcast-Pro or run it on the drone. Drones join the VPN during pairing, or with **Push to Drone** on the same page.

3. **Run the command as administrator.**

   - Windows: open **Terminal** or **PowerShell** with **Run as administrator** and paste the command.
   - macOS and Linux: paste it in a terminal, prefixed with `sudo`.

   When the command returns without an error, the computer is on the network. `tailscale status` lists the drones and other devices it can see.

4. **Find the computer in Connected Devices.** Back in Fleet Manager, the computer appears in **Connected Devices** with its hostname and a `100.x.y.z` address. Select **Sync** if it doesn't show up within a few seconds. A new device has the type **Unknown**, and a banner says how many devices need configuration.

5. **Mark it as a ground station.** In the **Type** column, select **Configure**. Choose **Ground Control Station (GCS)**, select **Continue**, then **Complete Setup**.

   ![Device setup wizard asking What type of device is this, with Ground Control Station selected](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/network--setup-wizard.webp)

   *Configure dialog: What type of device is this? with Ground Control Station (GCS) selected for a laptop named ops-laptop-03.*

The computer now has the **GCS** badge and appears in the **Ground Station** list when you add a stream binding.

> **Name ground stations after the person or position**
>
> Use **Rename** in the device's actions menu (the **⋯** button) to give it a name like "Field laptop – Team North". Binding lists are much easier to read in a large fleet.

## Start receiving a drone

1. Go to **Network → Stream Bindings** and select **Add Binding**.

2. Choose the **Drone** and the **Ground Station**, then select **Create Binding**. The drone must be online.

3. Read the ports in the **Ports** column, for example `5600 / 14550`.

4. In your ground control software, listen on those ports:

   - **QGroundControl:** telemetry on UDP 14550 connects automatically. For video, open **Application Settings → Video** (under **General** in older versions), set **Source** to **UDP h.264 Video Stream** and the UDP port to the binding's video port (**UDP URL** `0.0.0.0:<port>` in current versions). For further drones, add a UDP link on each binding's telemetry port under **Application Settings → Comm Links**.
   - **Mission Planner:** choose **UDP** in the connection drop-down, select **Connect** and enter the telemetry port.

More detail, including many drones on one ground station: [Stream bindings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/stream-bindings/) and [Stream to multiple ground stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/multiple-ground-stations/).

## The auth key

The command contains a reusable key for your organization's network. It is valid for 90 days and can be used on any number of ground stations. Owners and Admins can select the refresh button in **Connect a Device** to create a new key. Ground stations that have already joined stay connected. If the card says **No valid auth key available. Generate a new key to connect devices.**, the key has expired. Create a new one.

## Remove a ground station

On **Network → Devices**, open the device's actions menu and select **Remove Device**. This removes it from the VPN and deletes its stream bindings. To connect it again later, run the connection command again.

## Troubleshooting

- **Command fails or times out:** check that the computer can reach `https://vpn-connect.uavmatrix.com` and that the key isn't expired.
- **Ground station connected but no telemetry or video:** check that there is a binding, that **Video** and **Telemetry** are switched on, and that the ground station software listens on the binding's ports. The Windows firewall often blocks inbound UDP for a new app. See [No telemetry in the ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/) and [No video in the ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/).
- **Can't reach the drone over VPN:** see [VPN connected but can't reach the drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/vpn-cant-reach-drone/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/connect-gcs/


---

# Invite your team

> Invite pilots, operators and customers to your Fleet Manager organization by email, change roles, revoke invitations and transfer ownership.

Each person signs in with their own UAVmatrix account and gets a role in your organization: **Admin** or **Viewer** (there is exactly one **Owner**). Fleet Manager doesn't limit the number of members, and members don't use up licenses. See [Roles and permissions](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/roles-and-permissions/) for exactly what each role can do.

All of this happens on **Team** (page title **Team Management**). Owners and Admins can manage members. Viewers see the member list only.

![Team Management page listing an organization's members with roles and pending invitations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/team.webp)

*Team Management for an operator with 13 members: one Owner, four Admins and eight Viewers.*

## Invite a member

1. On **Team**, select **Invite Member**.
2. In **Invite Team Member**, enter the person's **Email Address**, choose the **Organization** (if you manage more than one) and the **Role**: **Admin** or **Viewer**.
3. Select **Send Invitation**.

![Invite Team Member dialog with email, organization and role fields](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/team--invite.webp)

*Invite Team Member dialog with Role set to Viewer for a customer contact.*

Fleet Manager emails an invitation link. The invitation is listed under **Pending Invitations** until it is accepted, and it expires after **7 days**. You can't send a second invitation to an email that already has a pending one: revoke the old one first.

> **Invite with the email they bought licenses with**
>
> If this person owns UAVcast-Pro licenses for drones you want to pair, invite the same email they used in the UAVmatrix store. Fleet Manager matches license owners to members by email. See [Licenses](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/).

## Accept an invitation

The invited person opens the link from the email. The invitation page shows the organization, **Invitation sent to**, and **Your role** with a short description of it.

- Signed in already: select **Accept Invitation**.
- Not signed in: select **Sign In** under **Sign in to accept this invitation**. New users select **Create Account**, which opens the UAVmatrix sign-up with the email filled in, and come back to the invitation afterwards.

![Invitation page with organization name, invited email, role description and Accept Invitation button](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/invite.webp)

*Invitation page as the invitee sees it: Your role Viewer, View-only access to drones and fleet data, and Accept Invitation.*

If the page says **Invitation Expired**, **Invitation Already Used** or **Already a Member**, ask an Owner or Admin for a new invitation, or just sign in.

## Change a member's role

Open the menu next to a member and select **Change Role → Admin** or **Viewer**. The change takes effect right away; they may need to reload the page to see it. Admins can change the role of other Admins. Nobody can change the Owner's role: [transfer ownership](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/#transfer-ownership) instead.

![Member actions menu with Change Role, Transfer Ownership and Remove Member](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/team--member-menu.webp)

*Member menu opened by the Owner, showing Change Role, Transfer Ownership and Remove Member.*

## Remove a member or revoke an invitation

- **Remove a member:** open the member's menu and select **Remove Member**. They lose access right away. The Owner can't be removed.
- **Revoke an invitation:** under **Pending Invitations**, select **Revoke**. The link stops working.

> **No confirmation step**
>
> **Remove Member** and **Transfer Ownership** act as soon as you select them. Check the name before you click.

Removing a member doesn't touch the drones. But if that person owns the licenses of drones you want to pair later, pairing those drones will fail until they are a member again.

## Transfer ownership

Only the Owner can do this. Open the menu of the member who should take over and select **Transfer Ownership**. That member becomes the **Owner**, and you become an **Admin**.

Use this when the person who set up the organization leaves, or before you delete your UAVmatrix account: Fleet Manager won't delete an account that still owns an organization.

## Working with customers and partners

A user can be a member of any number of organizations, with a different role in each. Typical setups:

- **Service provider:** your staff are Admins in your organization. Each customer gets a Viewer role so they can follow their flights live on the map.
- **Subcontractor:** a partner invites your pilot as Admin in their organization. Your pilot switches between both with the organization switcher.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/


---

# Roles and permissions

> The exact permission matrix for Fleet Manager's Owner, Admin and Viewer roles: pairing, flight commands, terminal, missions, VPN and team.

Fleet Manager has three roles, set per organization. A person can be an Admin in one organization and a Viewer in another.

| Role | In short |
| --- | --- |
| **Owner** | Everything an Admin can do, plus deleting the organization and transferring ownership. Exactly one per organization: the person who created it, or whoever ownership was transferred to. |
| **Admin** | Runs the fleet: pairs and removes drones, sends commands, opens the terminal, plans and uploads missions, manages the VPN and stream bindings, and manages the team. |
| **Viewer** | Read-only. Sees the dashboard, fleet, live map, flight history, missions, network and team, but can't change or command anything. |

New members are invited as Admin or Viewer. The Owner role only changes hands through [Transfer Ownership](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/#transfer-ownership).

## Permission matrix

The matrix comes from the permission rules Fleet Manager enforces on the server, so a hidden button is never the only thing standing in the way.

| Action | Owner | Admin | Viewer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Fleet and drones** |  |  |  |
| See dashboard, fleet list, UAV pages and live map | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Watch flight history playback | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Save, rename and delete named flights | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Pair a drone (**Pair Device**) | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Rename a drone, change its map color | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Remove a drone | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| **Commands** |  |  |  |
| Change flight mode, RTL, Loiter, Circle | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Arm, disarm, force arm | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Preflight calibration | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Start, stop and read missions on a drone | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Reboot or shut down the companion computer | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| SSH **Terminal** on the UAV page | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| **Open via Proxy** (UAVcast-Pro web interface through Fleet Manager) | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| **Missions** |  |  |  |
| View saved missions | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Create, edit and delete missions | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| **Upload to Drone** | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| **Network and VPN** |  |  |  |
| See the Network page, devices and stream bindings | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| See the VPN auth key and the **GCS Connection Command** | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Enable VPN, generate auth keys, **Push to Drone** | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Rename, change type of, or remove VPN devices | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Add, pause or remove stream bindings | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Delete the VPN network | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| **Team** |  |  |  |
| See members and roles | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Invite members (as Admin or Viewer) | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Change a member's role (except the Owner's) | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Remove members (except the Owner), revoke invitations | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Transfer ownership | ✓ | – | – |
| **Organization and settings** |  |  |  |
| Rename the organization, edit its description | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Change telemetry retention, prune or delete history | ✓ | ✓ | – |
| Delete the organization | ✓ | – | – |
| **Everyone** |  |  |  |
| Use FleetBot, create and close own support tickets | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Edit own profile (in the UAVmatrix account) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |

> **Admins can manage other Admins**
>
> An Admin can invite new Admins, demote another Admin to Viewer and remove other Admins. Give the Admin role only to people you'd trust with the whole fleet. The Owner is the only member an Admin can't change.

> **What Viewers see**
>
> Viewers get the same pages, without the controls. The UAV control panel shows a Viewer the live status and logs, but no flight mode, mission or arm buttons and no Terminal tab. On **Network**, Viewers don't see the VPN auth key: *Only Owners and Admins can see the VPN auth key.* Fleet Manager also checks every command on the server, so a Viewer can't send one by other means.

## Choosing roles for a business fleet

| Person | Suggested role |
| --- | --- |
| Fleet or operations manager | Owner (one person) |
| Pilots, technicians, the person who pairs new airframes | Admin |
| Customers following their job live, management, auditors | Viewer |
| Contractors who need to fly your drones | Admin, removed when the job ends |

## Not a role: super admin

UAVmatrix staff have a separate support role across all organizations. It is used for support tasks such as [adding extra license emails](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/#licenses-bought-with-another-email) to an account. It isn't part of your organization and can't be assigned.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/roles-and-permissions/


---

# Dashboard

> Read the Fleet Manager dashboard at a glance - total and online UAVs, team size, the UAV status list, the Getting Started checklist and the recent activity log.

**Dashboard** is the first page after you sign in. It answers three questions: how many drones are up right now, which ones, and what your team changed recently.

![Fleet Manager dashboard with four stats cards, the UAV Status list and Recent Activity](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/dashboard.webp)

*Dashboard: the four stats cards, UAV Status with battery and GPS per drone, and Recent Activity from the team.*

## Stats cards

| Card | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Total UAVs** | Drones paired to the organization you have open (*In this organization*). |
| **Online** | Drones in this organization connected right now, heard from within the last 20 seconds (*Currently connected*). |
| **Organizations** | Organizations you are a member of. |
| **Team Members** | Members of the organization you have open. |

Switch organization in the sidebar to see another organization's numbers.

## UAV Status

A list of your most recently seen drones with their status, battery and last check-in. Select a drone to open its [UAV page](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/uav-details/), or **View All** to go to [Fleet](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/).

## Getting Started

New organizations see a two-step checklist until both steps are done:

1. **Create or Join an Organization** (**Go to Team**)
2. **Pair a UAV (UAVcast)** (**Pair Device**), completed when the organization has at least one drone

Follow [Add your first drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/) for the second step.

## Recent Activity

The last 10 events in your organization, with who did them. Fleet Manager logs, among others:

- drones paired, re-paired and removed
- stream bindings created and removed, ground stations assigned
- members invited, removed and role changes, ownership transfers
- VPN enabled or disabled

The activity log is kept when a drone or member is removed, so you can still see who did what.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/dashboard/


---

# Fleet

> The Fleet page lists every UAV in your organization with live status, battery and last check-in, and is where you pair drones and open controls.

**Fleet** (sidebar **Fleet Management → Fleet**) lists every UAV in the selected organization. It updates live, so you can leave it open on a wall screen next to the [map](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/map/).

![Fleet page with a grid of UAV cards showing online and offline status, battery and last seen](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/fleet.webp)

*Fleet page with UAVs (46): ONLINE cards with battery levels, and dimmed OFFLINE cards with Last seen times.*

## UAV cards

The header shows **UAVs (n)**. Each card shows:

- **Name** and a status badge: **ONLINE**, **OFFLINE** or **PAIRING**.
- **Battery** in percent. It turns yellow below 50 % and red below 20 %.
- **Last seen**, as relative time. Offline cards are dimmed.
- **Re-pair required**, when the drone must be paired once more (see [Re-pair a drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/#re-pair-a-drone)).

A drone counts as offline after **20 seconds** without a message from UAVcast-Pro, which sends a heartbeat every 5 seconds.

Two buttons on each card:

- **Operations** opens the [control panel](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remote-control/): flight modes, arm and disarm, missions.
- **Details** opens the [UAV page](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/uav-details/): live telemetry, terminal, logs, system actions, rename and remove.

## Buttons on the page

- **Pair Device** starts the [pairing wizard](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/). Owners and Admins only.
- **Refresh** reloads the list.
- **Need more devices?** → **View Plans** opens the UAVmatrix store, where you buy more UAVcast-Pro licenses. See [Licenses](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/).

## Re-pair banner

When one or more drones use an older connection certificate, a banner at the top says **n UAV(s) must be re-paired**. Re-pair each listed drone once; it keeps its name and history. See [Re-pair a drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/#re-pair-a-drone).

![Fleet page with a re-pair banner and Re-pair required badges on two cards](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/fleet--repair-required.webp)

*Fleet page with the banner 2 UAVs must be re-paired and the Re-pair required badge on the two affected cards.*

## Tips for large fleets

- **Name drones for the map.** Names appear on map labels and in binding lists. A tail number or role ("Inspection-07") beats the default hostname. Rename from the UAV page.
- **Give each drone its own color.** Fleet Manager assigns colors from a 24-color palette automatically. Set a fixed color in the control panel (**Change map color**) for drones your team should recognize at a glance.
- **Use organizations to separate customers.** Drones belong to exactly one organization. If you operate for several customers who should each see only their drones, give each one an organization.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/


---

# UAV details

> A drone's page in Fleet Manager shows live telemetry and companion computer health, an SSH terminal and MAVLink log, and reboot or remove.

Each drone has its own page. Open it with **Details** on the [Fleet](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/) card, from the dashboard, or with **View UAV** at the end of pairing.

The header shows the name, a live status badge, **Re-pair required** if needed, the organization, the device **ID** and **Last seen**. Owners and Admins also get **Rename** and **Remove**.

The page has four tabs: **Overview**, **Terminal**, **Logs** and **Actions**.

## Overview

Live data, pushed to the browser as it arrives.

![UAV details Overview tab with UAVcast Application card and MAVLink / Flight Controller card](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/drone-detail.webp)

*Overview tab of an armed VTOL in AUTO: UAVcast Application card with CPU Temp, CPU, Memory and Disk, and the MAVLink / Flight Controller card with battery, GPS, altitude and heading.*

**UAVcast Application** describes the companion computer: connection state (**Connected**, **Waiting for data...** or **Connecting...**), **Hostname**, **Uptime**, **CPU Temp**, **CPU**, **Memory** and **Disk** usage, the UAVcast-Pro services and their state, and the drone's network addresses (LAN and VPN). It also has the buttons to [open UAVcast-Pro remotely](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remote-uavcast/): **Open via Proxy** and, when the drone is on the VPN, **Open via VPN**.

**MAVLink / Flight Controller** shows what the flight controller reports: **ARMED** or **DISARMED**, **FAILSAFE** and **GCS FAILSAFE** flags, **Battery**, **GPS** (satellites and fix), **Altitude** and **Heading**.

> **Watch CPU Temp on hot days**
>
> A Raspberry Pi that runs hot slows down, and video is the first thing to suffer. If **CPU Temp** climbs during a flight, see [Undervoltage and throttling](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/undervoltage-and-throttling/).

### Connected Ground Stations

Below the cards, **Connected Ground Stations** lists the ground stations that receive this drone's streams, with **Video** and **Telemetry** switches and **Pause** / **Resume**. **Add GCS** (Owners and Admins) binds another ground station to this drone. It creates the same stream binding as **Network → Stream Bindings**, with the next free ports on that ground station, and sends the new destination to the drone. See [Stream bindings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/stream-bindings/).

## Terminal

A browser SSH session to the companion computer, over Fleet Manager's encrypted connection. No port forwarding and no VPN needed. Owners and Admins only. The drone must be online.

Select **Connect** to open a shell. Quick-command buttons run common checks for you: `df -h`, `free -h`, `top -bn1`, `ip a`, `ip r`, `uptime`, `dmesg` and `ps aux`. **Disconnect** closes the session.

![Terminal tab with an SSH session showing df -h output and quick command buttons](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/drone-detail--terminal.webp)

*Terminal tab connected to a field drone, after running the df -h quick command.*

> **This is a live shell on the aircraft**
>
> The terminal is a real shell on the companion computer. Restarting services or the network while the drone is in the air can cut telemetry and video. Use it on the ground unless you know what a command does.

## Logs

A live view of the telemetry and heartbeat messages the drone sends to Fleet Manager, with **Telemetry** and **Heartbeat** filters, **Auto-scroll**, **Pause** and clear. **Download logs** saves what is on screen to a text file (`mavlink-log-<id>-<time>.txt`), which is useful to email to support with your ticket number (tickets only take an image).

This is a live log, not a flight log archive. Fleet Manager stores telemetry for [flight history](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/map/flight-history/), but doesn't store or export DataFlash or `.tlog` files. Those stay on the flight controller and in your ground station software.

![Logs tab with a scrolling list of telemetry and heartbeat entries and the Telemetry, Heartbeat and Auto-scroll switches](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/drone-detail--logs.webp)

*Logs tab streaming TELEMETRY and HEARTBEAT entries, with Telemetry, Heartbeat and Auto-scroll on.*

## Actions

**System Actions** has **Reboot** (Restart the companion computer) and **Shutdown** (Power off the companion computer). Both need the drone to be online. To confirm, you type the action's name.

These act on the companion computer only, not on the flight controller. A shutdown can't be undone remotely: someone has to power-cycle the drone.

![Actions tab with System Actions card and Reboot and Shutdown buttons](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/drone-detail--actions.webp)

*Actions tab with the Confirm Reboot dialog open, asking to type reboot to confirm.*

## Rename

Select **Rename**, enter the new name in **Edit UAV** and save. The name syncs to UAVcast-Pro when the drone is online.

## Remove

**Remove** deletes the drone from the organization and unpairs it. See [Remove or transfer a drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/uav-details/


---

# Remote control

> Change flight modes, arm or disarm, run missions and start a preflight calibration from Fleet Manager's UAV control panel, with safety checks.

The **UAV Control Panel** sends commands to the flight controller through UAVcast-Pro over Fleet Manager's encrypted connection. It works over any internet link the drone has, including 4G, and doesn't need the VPN.

Open it with **Operations** on a [Fleet](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/) card, or **Controls** in a drone's popup on the [Fleet Map](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/map/). On the map, the panel also has **Terminal** and **Logs** tabs.

![UAV Control Panel with Flight Mode, Mission and Actions columns for an armed quadcopter](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/control-panel.webp)

*UAV Control Panel for an armed quadcopter in LOITER: Flight Mode with the RTL, Circle and Loiter buttons, Mission with an 18-waypoint survey selected, and Actions with Arm and Disarm.*

Only **Owners** and **Admins** can send commands. See [Roles and permissions](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/roles-and-permissions/).

> **Remote commands move real aircraft**
>
> A command from Fleet Manager acts on the aircraft as if a ground station sent it. Keep a pilot with a ground station or RC transmitter in control of every flight, follow your local rules for remote and BVLOS operations, and treat Fleet Manager as a supervision and dispatch tool, not your only link.

## Header

The header shows the drone's status, **ARMED** and **FAILSAFE** flags, a **GCS Failsafe** badge, the map color picker (**Change map color**, with **Reset to auto**) and a **Details** link to the [UAV page](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/uav-details/).

If the flight controller's GCS failsafe is off, the panel warns: **GCS Failsafe not enabled. Without GCS failsafe, the vehicle will not return to launch if it loses connection to the ground station.** Set up the failsafe in your ground station software (ArduPilot parameter `FS_GCS_ENABLE`) before flying beyond visual line of sight.

## Flight Mode

Pick a mode from the drop-down, or use the quick buttons **RTL**, **Circle** and **Loiter** (**Hold** on rovers). Every mode change asks for confirmation, and the more dangerous the mode, the stronger the check:

| Confirmation | Modes |
| --- | --- |
| Simple **Change to *MODE*?** | STABILIZE, ALT_HOLD, LOITER, POSHOLD, BRAKE, FLOWHOLD, HOLD, FBWA, FBWB, CRUISE, QHOVER, QLOITER, QSTABILIZE |
| Confirmation with a description of what the mode does | AUTO, GUIDED, RTL, SMART_RTL, CIRCLE, FOLLOW, ZIGZAG, QRTL, TAKEOFF, AVOID_ADSB, ACRO, MANUAL |
| Type the mode name to confirm | LAND, SPORT, AUTOTUNE, FLIP, DRIFT, THROW, QLAND, QACRO, AUTOROTATE |

![Mode change confirmation dialog asking to type LAND to confirm](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/control-panel--mode-confirm.webp)

*Confirmation for LAND, a mode that must be typed to confirm.*

The mode lists are ArduPilot's (Copter, Plane, Rover and Sub). On a PX4 flight controller, use your ground station to change modes.

## Mission

Runs [missions](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/missions/) saved in your organization:

- **Select mission** picks a saved mission. The counter shows the current and total waypoint, for example `3/18`, or **None**.
- **Start** first reads the mission on the drone and compares it with the one you selected. If they differ, **Mission Not Loaded on Drone** offers **Upload & Start**.
- **Stop**, **Read** (fetch the mission from the drone) and **Clear**.

Each action asks you to confirm.

## Actions

- **Arm** and **Disarm**. The arm dialog says **This will arm the UAV. Ensure all personnel are clear of the propellers before arming.** Tick **Force arm (bypass pre-arm checks)** only on the bench: it skips the checks that stop an unsafe takeoff.
- **Select action... → Preflight Calibration** calibrates the gyroscope and levels the accelerometer. Keep the vehicle completely still on a level surface, then select **Start Calibration**.

![Arm confirmation dialog with propeller warning and Force arm checkbox](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/control-panel--arm-confirm.webp)

*Arm dialog with the propeller warning and the Force arm (bypass pre-arm checks) box unticked.*

Arm, disarm and preflight calibration need UAVcast-Pro **6.3.0_rc13** or later on the drone. On older versions the panel shows **UAVcast Upgrade Required**. See [Updating](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/updating/).

## When a command doesn't go through

- The drone must be online. Commands to an offline drone fail.
- Fleet Manager waits for the drone to acknowledge each command. If the flight controller refuses, for example arming with failed pre-arm checks, the error appears in the panel and on the drone's status messages.
- Messages from the flight controller (pre-arm failures, mode changes) show in the drone's popup on the map and in the [Logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/uav-details/#logs) tab.

For phone-sized screens, see [Lite view](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/lite-view/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remote-control/


---

# Open UAVcast-Pro remotely

> Reach a drone's UAVcast-Pro settings from anywhere through Fleet Manager, either via the built-in proxy without VPN or directly over your organization's VPN.

You can change a drone's UAVcast-Pro settings (camera, modem, ground stations and so on) without being on the same network as the drone. On the [UAV page](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/uav-details/), the **UAVcast Application** card has two buttons:

| Button | How it connects | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Open via Proxy** | Through Fleet Manager's encrypted connection to the drone. Works for any online drone, no VPN needed. | Configuration changes and basic management. |
| **Open via VPN** | Opens `http://<drone VPN address>` directly. Shown only when the drone is on your organization's VPN, and your computer must be on that VPN too. | Everything, including the live flight map and telemetry. |

The proxy is for Owners and Admins. Fleet Manager refuses it for Viewers with **Access denied. Only administrators can access UAVcast remotely.**

## Open via Proxy

1. On the UAV page, select **Open via Proxy**.
2. Read the **Remote UAVcast Access via Proxy** dialog and select **Continue**.
3. UAVcast-Pro opens in a new tab on its **Application** page. Sign in with the drone's UAVcast-Pro user: the proxy doesn't pass on your Fleet Manager login. (A drone that has no UAVcast-Pro users yet opens without a login.)

![Remote UAVcast Access via Proxy dialog listing features that are unavailable](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/drone-detail--proxy-warning.webp)

*Remote UAVcast Access via Proxy dialog, listing WebSocket features unavailable: live telemetry, MAVLink connection status and the flight map.*

The proxy carries ordinary page requests, not live connections. **WebSocket features unavailable** means these don't work through it:

- live telemetry and real-time updates
- MAVLink connection status
- the flight map

Each request has 30 seconds to complete. On a slow link, large pages can time out with **Request timed out. UAVcast may be unreachable.** If the drone is offline you get **Drone is offline. UAVcast interface is not available.**

> **Be careful with network settings through the proxy**
>
> The proxy runs over the drone's own internet connection. If you change the modem, network priority or VPN settings and the drone loses internet, the proxy goes with it, and you'll need local access to fix it.

## Open via VPN

Join your computer to the organization's VPN the same way as a ground station (see [Connect a ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/connect-gcs/)). Then **Open via VPN** opens the drone's interface directly, with all live features. It is the better choice for anything beyond changing a setting.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remote-uavcast/


---

# Re-pair, remove or transfer a drone

> Re-pair a drone when Fleet Manager asks, remove it from your organization, move it to another one or replace its companion computer.

A drone belongs to one organization at a time. This page covers the three things you do to an existing drone: pair it again, remove it, and move it somewhere else.

## Re-pair a drone

Re-pairing renews the drone's connection certificate. The drone keeps its record in Fleet Manager: name, telemetry history, saved flights and stream bindings stay as they are.

You need it when:

- Fleet Manager shows **Re-pair required** on the drone, or the banner **This UAV must be re-paired** on its page. Fleet Manager has moved to a newer, stricter certificate and this drone still has an old one.
- Someone selected **Disconnect from Fleet** in UAVcast-Pro.

![UAV page with the banner This UAV must be re-paired](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/drone-detail--repair-required.webp)

*UAV page with the This UAV must be re-paired banner explaining the Disconnect and Connect to Fleet Manager steps.*

1. In the drone's UAVcast-Pro interface, open **Fleet Management** and select **Disconnect from Fleet**. Confirm **Disconnect from Fleet?** If the page already shows **Connect to Fleet Manager**, skip this.
2. Select **Connect to Fleet Manager** to get a new 8-digit code.
3. In Fleet Manager, go to **Fleet → Pair Device**, choose the **same organization** and enter the code. Follow the wizard as in [Add your first drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/).

Don't remove the drone in Fleet Manager first. Removing it deletes its history; re-pairing keeps it.

## Remove a drone

Use this when a drone is retired, sold or moving to another organization. Owners and Admins only.

1. Open the drone's [UAV page](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/uav-details/) and select **Remove**.
2. Confirm **Delete UAV**.

If the drone is online, Fleet Manager first tells UAVcast-Pro to unpair and waits up to 5 seconds for an answer. UAVcast-Pro then shows **Connect to Fleet Manager** again and leaves the organization's VPN.
