If the drone is offline or doesn't answer, **UAVcast Not Responding** asks whether to continue. **Delete Anyway** removes it from Fleet Manager only. Then, next time you can reach the drone, select **Disconnect from Fleet** in UAVcast-Pro yourself. Until then it still thinks it is paired.

![Delete UAV confirmation dialog warning that telemetry and command history will be removed](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/drone-detail--delete.webp)

*Delete UAV dialog for a retired airframe, warning that all telemetry data and command history will be permanently removed.*

### What removing deletes

| Deleted | Kept |
| --- | --- |
| The drone record and its name | Entries in **Recent Activity** |
| All stored telemetry and flight history, including saved flights | Saved missions (they belong to the organization) |
| Command history and stream bindings | The UAVcast-Pro license, which stays activated on the drone |
| The drone's VPN device |  |

> **This can't be undone**
>
> There is no export of flight history before you remove a drone. If you need the data, replay or record what you need from [Flight history](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/map/flight-history/) first.

## Move a drone to another organization

Fleet Manager has no "transfer" button for a single drone, because history stays with the organization that recorded it. To move a drone:

1. In the current organization, [remove the drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/#remove-a-drone). Its history there is deleted.
2. Make sure the drone's UAVcast-Pro license is owned by a member of the new organization. See [Licenses](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/).
3. In the new organization, [pair the drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/).

If you try to pair a drone that still belongs to another organization, Fleet Manager stops with **This UAV is already paired to an organization**. Only an Owner or Admin of that organization can release it.

To hand over a **whole fleet** with its history (for example when a company is sold), keep the organization and [transfer ownership](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/#transfer-ownership) to the new owner instead.

## Replace the companion computer

Fleet Manager identifies a drone by a device ID that UAVcast-Pro computes from the companion computer's CPU serial number and its boot disk (SD card or SSD). A new companion computer, or a new SD card or SSD in the same one, shows up as a **new** drone. Reinstalling UAVcast-Pro on the same board and disk keeps the same device ID.

1. Remove the old drone in Fleet Manager (or keep it until you no longer need its history).
2. Install UAVcast-Pro on the new computer and activate the license. See [Activate your license](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/).
3. Pair it as a new drone and recreate its stream bindings.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/


---

# Live map

> Track every drone in your fleet on one live map with status rings, heading lines, 5-minute trails, follow mode and OpenAIP airspace layers.

**Fleet Map** (sidebar **Overview → Fleet Map**) shows every drone in the selected organization on one map, updated live as telemetry arrives. It is built for a control room: leave it open and you see at a glance which aircraft are up, where they are heading and which ones need attention.

![Fleet map with many colored drone markers, heading lines and flight trails over a region](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/map.webp)

*Fleet Map on the Dark style over the Port of Rotterdam: each drone in its own color with heading line and trail, and grey offline markers labelled with how long ago they were seen.*

## Reading a marker

Each drone is drawn in its own color, with an icon for its vehicle type: quadcopter, hexacopter, plane, VTOL, rover, boat or submarine. Rings and badges around the marker flag problems:

| On the marker | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Drone's own color, no ring | Online and healthy. |
| Grey marker, grey dashed ring and clock badge | **Offline**: nothing received for 20 seconds. |
| Orange ring with **!** badge | **NO MAVLINK**: UAVcast-Pro is online but has had no telemetry from the flight controller for 10 seconds. Check the flight controller connection. |
| Red dashed ring | **GPS lost**: no satellites or no fix. |
| Yellow dashed ring | **GPS weak**: fewer than 6 satellites or only a 2D fix. |
| **H** marker | The drone's home position, set when it arms. Hover to see its altitude (AMSL). |

Armed or disarmed isn't shown by the marker itself. Open the popup, or use the [control panel](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remote-control/), to see **Armed**.

The label next to the marker reads `Name • FLIGHTMODE`, with **NO MAVLINK**, **NO GPS** or **WEAK GPS** added when they apply, or `Name • OFFLINE • 5 mins ago` for an offline drone.

### Heading line and trail

- The **heading line** is a dashed line in the drone's color pointing where the nose points. It is hidden when the drone is offline.
- The **flight trail** shows the last **5 minutes** of the path, as a dashed line in the drone's color (grey when offline). A new point is added about every 11 m of movement.

## Drone popup

Select a marker to open its popup: name, organization and status, then **Battery**, **Altitude**, **Mode**, **Armed**, **GPS** (satellites and fix type: No Fix, 2D, 3D, DGPS or RTK), **Signal** and, when offline, **Last seen**. The latest status message from the flight controller appears too, which is often the fastest way to read a pre-arm failure.

**Signal** is the round-trip time between Fleet Manager and the drone, measured every 10 seconds: excellent under 100 ms, good under 300 ms, fair under 600 ms, poor above that or after three missed pings.

![Drone popup on the map with battery, altitude, mode, armed, GPS and signal rows and Follow, History and Controls buttons](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/map--popup.webp)

*Popup for an armed survey drone in AUTO: Battery 71%, Altitude 85.5 m, GPS 20 sats (3D), Signal 61 ms (Excellent), with Follow, History and Controls.*

Three buttons:

- **Follow** keeps the drone in view. See below.
- **History** opens [flight history](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/map/flight-history/) for this drone.
- **Controls** opens the [UAV Control Panel](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remote-control/).

## Follow a drone

Select **Follow** in the popup. The map zooms in (to at least zoom level 14) and centers on the drone, then pans only when the drone gets close to the edge of the screen, so the map doesn't jitter. A **Following *name*** banner appears; select its **X**, or **Unfollow**, to stop. Opening **History** also stops following.

![Map following one drone with the Following banner at the top](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/map--follow.webp)

*Follow mode on a fixed-wing mapping a corridor, with the Following banner and the trail behind it.*

## Drones without GPS

Drones that are online but have no position yet are listed in a **drones without GPS** box on the map. Select one to open its control panel. The counter **n drones on map** tells you how many are plotted.

## Map Settings

Select the gear button at the top right to open **Map Settings**. Your choices are saved in this browser.

| Section | Option | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Overlays** | **Airspace Layers**: restricted airspace, airports, heliports | Off |
| **Drone Filter** | **All Drones**, **Online Only** or **Offline Only** | All Drones |
| **Marker Options** | **Heading Line** | On |
|  | **Marker Tooltip**: name label on markers | On |
|  | **Always Visible**: show the label permanently instead of on hover | On |
|  | **Flight Trail**: recent flight path (last 5 min) | On |
| **Map Style** | **Satellite**, **Light** or **Dark** | Dark |

![Map Settings panel with overlays, drone filter, marker options and map style](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/map--settings.webp)

*Map Settings panel with Airspace Layers on, Drone Filter set to Online Only and Map Style Satellite.*

> **For a busy map**
>
> With 20+ drones in one area, switch **Always Visible** off so labels only appear on hover, and use **Online Only** to hide parked aircraft.

## Airspace layers

**Airspace Layers** draws restricted airspace, airports and heliports from OpenAIP on top of the map. The layer appears from zoom level 7 and closer. It is one combined layer; you can't toggle categories separately.

> **Not a substitute for official airspace checks**
>
> The airspace layer is for situational awareness. Check NOTAMs and your national drone map or UTM service before each flight.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/map/


---

# Flight history

> Replay a drone's recorded flight on the Fleet Manager map, read duration, max altitude and speed, save named flights and set telemetry retention.

Fleet Manager records each drone's telemetry once per second while it is connected: position, altitude, speed, heading, battery, flight mode, armed state and GPS. **Flight history** replays that recording on the map.

## Open a drone's history

On **Fleet Map**, select the drone's marker and then **History** in the popup. The drawer ***name* - Flight History** opens at the bottom of the map.

![Flight history drawer under the map with a session picker, playback controls, stats and a replayed flight path](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/map--history.webp)

*Flight history for an inspection drone: the saved flight Turbine blade inspection selected, playback at 4x, and Duration, Max Alt, Max Speed and Avg Battery.*

## Pick a session

**Select flight session** lists:

1. **Saved flights** first (with a bookmark icon), the ones your team has named.
2. Then one entry per **day** with recorded telemetry, for the last 30 days.

A day groups all telemetry from that date, so several flights on one day appear as one session. Save the stretch you care about as a named flight to find it again quickly.

## Play it back

- Play and pause, step back or forward by 5 % of the session, or jump to the start or end. Drag the timeline to scrub.
- Speeds: **0.5x**, **1x** (real time), **2x**, **4x**, **8x**, **10x** and **20x**.
- Keyboard: **Space** play/pause, **←** / **→** step, **Esc** close.

On the map, a green **Start** and a red **End** marker frame the flight. The part already played is drawn in cyan, the rest dashed in grey, and a drone icon labelled with its altitude moves along the path.

The stats panel shows **Duration**, **Max Alt**, **Max Speed** and **Avg Battery**, and **Current Position** shows **Alt**, **Speed**, **Heading** and **Mode** at the playback point.

## Save, rename and delete flights

Owners and Admins can save, rename and delete named flights. Viewers can play them back.

- **Save and name this flight** saves the current time range under a name (up to 100 characters), for example "Survey over Field A". Two saved flights can't overlap: **A saved session already exists for this time range**.
- **Rename flight** changes the name.
- **Delete saved flight** removes the name only. **Delete Saved Flight?** explains that the telemetry itself is not deleted.

## How long history is kept

Owners and Admins set retention per organization in **Settings → History** (**Telemetry History**):

- **Retention:** 7, 14, 30, 60 or 90 days, **6 months** or **1 year**. The default and the maximum is 1 year.
- **Prune Now** deletes data older than 7, 14, 30, 60 or 90 days right away (default 30), after the **Prune Old History** confirmation.
- **Delete Drone History** (trash icon per drone) or **Select All** → **Delete Selected (n)** clears history for chosen drones.
- Cards show **Storage Used**, **Total Records** and **Retention**.

Fleet Manager removes data past the retention period once a day. Older data is compressed after 7 days, so a year of history for a large fleet stays practical.

![Settings History tab with retention selector, prune options and per-drone history list](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/settings--history.webp)

*Settings → History for an organization with 46 drones: Storage Used, Total Records, Retention 90 days, and the per-drone list with Delete buttons.*

> **No log export**
>
> Fleet Manager doesn't export flight history as a file, and it doesn't store video or flight controller logs (`.tlog`, DataFlash). Keep those from your ground station software or the flight controller's SD card. For video recordings on the drone, see [Recordings and flight review](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/recording-flight-review/).

Removing a drone deletes its whole history, saved flights included. See [Remove or transfer a drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/map/flight-history/


---

# Missions

> Draw waypoint missions on the map, choose MAVLink commands and altitude frames, save missions for the whole organization and upload them to any online drone.

**Missions** (sidebar **Fleet Management → Missions**) is a waypoint planner in the browser. Missions are saved for the organization, so anyone on the team can load one, and an Owner or Admin can upload it to any online drone.

![Mission Planner with a waypoint survey pattern drawn on a satellite map](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/missions.webp)

*Mission Planner on the Satellite style with an 18-waypoint survey grid, Takeoff and Return to Launch, and the header showing 18 waypoints and total distance.*

Viewers can open and look at saved missions. Saving, uploading and deleting need Owner or Admin.

## Plan a mission

1. Select **Create New** (or **Missions → New Mission**).
2. Click on the map to add waypoints. Drag a waypoint to move it. While placing, **Next WP** shows the distance from the previous waypoint (**Prev:**) and from home (**Home:**).
3. Open the waypoint drawer (**n Waypoints**) to edit each row: **Command**, **Params**, **Alt**, **Frame** and **Radius**. Drag rows to reorder. Row **H** is home.
4. Set **Defaults:** for new waypoints at the top of the drawer: **Alt** (default 50 m) and **WP Radius** (default 30 m).

![Waypoint drawer with columns for command, params, coordinates, altitude, frame, radius and distance](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/missions--waypoint-drawer.webp)

*Waypoint drawer with a Takeoff, several Waypoint rows, a Change Speed and a Return to Launch, Frame set to Relative.*

### Altitude frames

| Frame | Altitude is measured from |
| --- | --- |
| **Relative** (default) | The home position |
| **Absolute** | Mean sea level |
| **Terrain** | The ground below the waypoint (needs terrain data on the flight controller) |

### Commands

The **Command** picker is searchable and lists the MAVLink mission commands ArduPilot understands, grouped as:

- **Navigation:** Waypoint, Takeoff, Land, Return to Launch, Loiter Unlim, Loiter Turns, Loiter Time, Loiter to Alt, Spline Waypoint, Vtol Takeoff, Vtol Land, Payload Place, Delay and more.
- **Conditions:** Delay, Change Alt, Distance, Yaw.
- **Do commands:** Change Speed, Set ROI Location, Set Servo, Set Relay, Jump, Digicam Control, Set Cam Trigg Dist, Mount Control, Gripper, Parachute, VTOL Transition and others.

Commands that take parameters (for example delay time, loiter turns, speed or servo PWM) get editable fields in **Params**.

Limits: altitude 0 to 10,000 m, radius 1 to 1,000 m, at least one waypoint.

## Save

Select **Save**, enter a **Name** (up to 100 characters) and an optional **Description**, and confirm **Save Mission**. The header shows **Unsaved** while there are changes; **Update Mission** saves them. Open saved missions from **Missions → Saved Missions**.

## Upload to a drone

1. Save the mission. An unsaved mission can't be uploaded (**Mission not saved**).
2. Select **Upload to Drone**, choose the UAV under **Select UAV** and confirm.
3. Wait for the confirmation. The upload times out after 30 seconds if the drone doesn't answer.

![Upload Mission to Drone dialog with a list of online UAVs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/missions--upload.webp)

*Upload Mission to Drone dialog with the online UAVs to choose from.*

To fly it, select the mission in the drone's [control panel](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remote-control/#mission) and select **Start**. If the mission on the drone differs from the one you selected, the panel offers **Upload & Start**.

## Read a mission from a drone

Under **Missions → Read from Drone**, choose an online drone. Its current mission loads into the planner as **Mission from *name***. Save it to keep a copy, for example before you overwrite it.

> **Check the mission in your ground station before flight**
>
> Fleet Manager uploads exactly what you planned. Before an automatic flight, check the mission and the vehicle's failsafes in QGroundControl or Mission Planner, as you would with any other planning tool.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/missions/


---

# Network and VPN

> Enable your organization's private WireGuard VPN in Fleet Manager, connect drones and ground station laptops, and manage the devices table.

Every organization can have its own private VPN: a WireGuard mesh network between your drones and your ground stations, run by Fleet Manager. On it, each device gets a fixed `100.x.y.z` address and can reach the others directly, whether it is on 4G, Wi-Fi or satellite, without port forwarding or public IP addresses.

Fleet Manager uses this network to route [stream bindings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/stream-bindings/): video and MAVLink from a drone to the laptops where pilots run QGroundControl or Mission Planner.

All of this is on **Network** (sidebar **Fleet Management → Network**).

## When do I need VPN?

VPN is **optional**: Fleet Manager shows, maps and controls drones without it, over the drone's own encrypted connection. Turn it on when you want streams to reach ground stations.

| VPN recommended | VPN not required |
| --- | --- |
| Drone and ground station on different networks (4G, remote sites) | Drone and ground station on the same local Wi-Fi |
| You want direct video and telemetry streaming | You use a direct USB or serial telemetry link |
| You need encrypted links between sites | You are testing in a controlled environment |
| You operate across several locations |  |

## Enable VPN

Owners and Admins only.

1. Open **Network**. If VPN is off, the page shows **Enable VPN Network** with what it gives you: secure WireGuard-based connections, low-latency video and telemetry streaming, and working across any network.
2. Select **Enable VPN Network**.

![Network page with the Enable VPN Network card for an organization without VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/network--enable.webp)

*Network page before VPN is enabled, with the three benefits and the Enable VPN Network button.*

Once VPN is on, the page shows four counters (**Total Devices**, **Online**, **UAVs**, **Ground Stations**) and three tabs: **Devices**, **Stream Bindings** and **Settings**.

![Network page Devices tab with status counters and a connected devices table](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/network.webp)

*Network → Devices for a large operator: Total Devices 51, Online 39, UAVs 44, Ground Stations 7, and the Connected Devices table.*

## Put drones on the VPN

Drones never need a manual command. There are two ways:

- **When pairing.** If VPN is enabled before you pair, the wizard's **VPN Connection** step joins the drone. See [Add your first drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/).
- **Push to Drone.** For drones paired before VPN was enabled, the **Push to Drone** card on the **Devices** tab lists every drone that isn't on your network. Select **Connect** next to a drone to send it the VPN settings. The drone must be online.

If a drone is already on another Tailscale network, it has an **Existing VPN** badge. **Connect** then asks for confirmation (**Existing VPN Connection Detected**) and **Replace & Connect** moves it to your organization's network.

The drone appears in **Connected Devices** with the **UAV** type and its VPN address, and the UAV page gets an **Open via VPN** button.

## Put ground stations on the VPN

Ground stations join with one Tailscale command from **Connect a Device**. Follow [Connect a ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/connect-gcs/).

## Connected Devices

The table lists every device on the network:

| Column | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Status** | Online or offline on the VPN |
| **Device** | Name and hostname |
| **Type** | **UAV**, **GCS** or **Unknown**. Unknown devices have a **Configure** button. |
| **IP Address** | The device's VPN address (`100.x.y.z`) |
| **Last Check-in** | When the device was last seen on the network |

Select **Sync** to refresh the list from the VPN server. Each row's actions menu has:

- **Rename**: a readable name, for example "Field laptop – Team North".
- **Change Type**: switch between **UAV**, **GCS** and **Unknown**. For a UAV, choose which paired drone it is.
- **Remove Device**: takes the device off the network. For a drone, Fleet Manager tells it to leave the VPN, and its stream bindings are removed.

### Configure an unknown device

New ground stations show up as **Unknown**, and a banner counts the devices that need configuration. Select **Configure** and answer **What type of device is this?**

- **Ground Control Station (GCS):** a computer running QGroundControl, Mission Planner or similar. It will **receive** video and telemetry and becomes available for stream bindings.
- **Drone / UAV:** a drone with UAVcast-Pro. Choose which paired drone it is, so you can manage its streaming.

Select **Continue**, then **Complete Setup**.

## Settings tab

**Danger Zone → Delete Network** permanently deletes the VPN network, all connected devices, all authentication keys and all stream bindings. Devices drop off the network, and you'd have to connect every ground station and drone again.

Deleting the network also switches VPN off for the organization, and online UAVs are told to leave the VPN. The Network page then shows **Enable VPN Network** again, which creates a new, empty network. There is no separate switch to turn VPN off: **Delete Network** is the way to do it.

## Network requirements

| Device | Needs outbound |
| --- | --- |
| Drone (Fleet Manager connection) | HTTPS (TCP 443) to `fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com`, TCP 8883 for MQTT over TLS |
| Drone and ground station (VPN) | HTTPS (TCP 443) to `vpn-connect.uavmatrix.com`, plus UDP for WireGuard. Tailscale uses UDP 41641 by default. |

Most cellular and office networks allow this. If devices join the VPN but can't reach each other, see [VPN connected but can't reach the drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/vpn-cant-reach-drone/).

When two devices can't reach each other directly over UDP, their traffic is relayed through Tailscale's public DERP relay servers over HTTPS (TCP 443). It stays end-to-end encrypted, but the relay adds delay, so allow outbound UDP where you can.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/


---

# Stream bindings

> Route video and MAVLink from any drone to any ground station over VPN, how Fleet Manager assigns UDP ports, and QGC and Mission Planner setup.

A stream binding tells a drone to send its video and telemetry to one ground station over your organization's VPN. One drone can stream to several ground stations, and one ground station can receive several drones. Fleet Manager picks the ports so that streams never collide.

## Before you begin

- [VPN enabled](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/#enable-vpn) and the drone on the VPN (type **UAV** in **Connected Devices**).
- The ground station [connected and configured as **GCS**](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/connect-gcs/).
- **Owner or Admin** role.
- The drone **online**. Fleet Manager sends the new destinations to UAVcast-Pro right away and waits for it to confirm.

## Add a binding

1. Go to **Network → Stream Bindings** and select **Add Binding**.
2. In **Add Stream Binding**, choose the **Drone** and the **Ground Station**.
3. Select **Create Binding**.

![Add Stream Binding dialog with drone and ground station selectors and a note on automatic ports](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/network--add-binding.webp)

*Add Stream Binding dialog with a drone and a ground station selected, and the note that ports are assigned automatically.*

The binding appears in the table with **Video** and **Telemetry** switched on and its **Ports** (video / telemetry). UAVcast-Pro starts sending within seconds.

If the drone doesn't confirm within 15 seconds, Fleet Manager cancels the binding with **Failed to send configuration to drone - it may be offline**. Check that the drone is online and try again.

## How ports are assigned

Ports are counted **per ground station**. Each binding gets its own block of UDP ports on that ground station, so drones never overlap:

- a **video** port for camera 1, followed by room for **camera 2** (dual stream) and **audio**, which UAVcast-Pro sends to the next ports after the video port;
- a **telemetry** port for MAVLink.

The first binding on a ground station uses the defaults, video **5600** and telemetry **14550**. Later bindings get the next free block.

A few consequences worth knowing:

- **Every ground station starts at the defaults.** The same drone can have different ports on two laptops, depending on what else each laptop receives.
- **Freed ports are reused.** Removing a binding frees its block for the next new binding to that laptop.
- **Ports don't follow the drone.** Removing and re-adding a binding can give it different ports. Always read the **Ports** column before setting up the ground station software.
- Ports are assigned by Fleet Manager and can't be edited in the app.
- A **Video Port (Camera 2)** set by hand on the drone is kept when Fleet Manager updates its destinations only from UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3. On earlier versions the next update clears it.

## Set up the ground station software

Use the ports from the binding's **Ports** column. The stream arrives from the drone's VPN address.

**QGroundControl**

- **Telemetry:** QGroundControl listens on UDP 14550 by default, so the first drone connects by itself. For more drones, open **Application Settings → Comm Links**, add a link of type **UDP** with the binding's telemetry port, and connect it.
- **Video:** in **Application Settings → Video** (under **General** in older versions), set **Source** to **UDP h.264 Video Stream** and the UDP port to the binding's video port (**UDP URL** `0.0.0.0:<port>` in current versions). QGroundControl shows one video at a time; to watch several drones, run a second instance or use a video player for the others.

**Mission Planner**

- **Telemetry:** in the connection drop-down at the top right, choose **UDP**, select **Connect** and enter the binding's telemetry port. For several drones, connect once per port; Mission Planner lists each vehicle by system ID.
- **Video:** right-click the HUD, choose **Video → Set GStreamer Source** and enter a pipeline that listens on the binding's video port. See [Mission Planner](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/mission-planner/) for the exact pipeline.

> **Give each drone its own MAVLink system ID**
>
> When one ground station receives several drones, each flight controller needs a unique `SYSID_THISMAV` (ArduPilot) or `MAV_SYS_ID` (PX4). Otherwise the ground station mixes them up.

More on running many vehicles from one station: [Stream to multiple ground stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/multiple-ground-stations/).

## Pause or remove a binding

- Switch **Video** or **Telemetry** off in the table to stop that stream without losing the binding or its ports. Do this while the drone is online, so it gets the change.
- Select the trash icon to remove the binding. The ports become free for the next binding to that ground station.

Use the search box and the **Video Status** filter (**All Video**, **Video On**, **Video Off**) to find bindings in a large fleet.

![Stream Bindings table listing drones, ground stations, video and telemetry switches and ports](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/network--stream-bindings.webp)

*Stream Bindings tab: each binding lists its drone, ground station, Video and Telemetry switches and its ports.*

## Bindings on the UAV page

Each drone's [UAV page](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/uav-details/#connected-ground-stations) lists its ground stations under **Connected Ground Stations**, with the same switches and **Pause** / **Resume**. **Add GCS** there creates a binding the same way as **Add Binding** here, with the next free ports on that ground station.

## No stream arriving?

See [No telemetry in the ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/) and [No video in the ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/). The usual causes are a firewall on the laptop blocking inbound UDP, the ground station software listening on the wrong port, or the stream switched off in the binding.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/stream-bindings/


---

# Status indicators and notifications

> What Fleet Manager's offline, no-MAVLink, GPS, failsafe and battery indicators mean, plus system announcements, the status page and alerts.

Fleet Manager shows problems where you are already looking: on the map, on the fleet list and on each drone's page. This page lists every indicator and what to do about it.

## Drone indicators

| Indicator | Where | Meaning | First thing to check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **OFFLINE**, grey marker with clock badge | Fleet, map, UAV page | Nothing received from UAVcast-Pro for 20 seconds | The drone's internet link and port 8883. See [Drone offline in Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/drone-offline-fleet-manager/). |
| **NO MAVLINK**, orange ring with **!** | Map | UAVcast-Pro is online but has had no flight controller data for 10 seconds | Flight controller power and cable. See [No MAVLink heartbeat](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/). |
| Red dashed ring, **NO GPS** | Map | No satellites or no fix | Antenna view of the sky, GPS cable. |
| Yellow dashed ring, **WEAK GPS** | Map | Fewer than 6 satellites or only a 2D fix | Wait for more satellites before flight. |
| Battery in yellow / red | Fleet cards | Below 50 % / below 20 % | Plan the landing. |
| **ARMED** | UAV page, control panel, map popup | Motors armed | Treat the aircraft as live. |
| **FAILSAFE** | UAV page, control panel | The flight controller is in failsafe | The flight controller's messages, shown in the map popup and **Logs**. |
| **GCS FAILSAFE** / **GCS Failsafe not enabled** | UAV page, control panel | Ground-station failsafe triggered, or not configured | Set `FS_GCS_ENABLE` before BVLOS flights. |
| **Re-pair required** | Fleet, UAV page | The drone uses an old connection certificate | [Re-pair the drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/#re-pair-a-drone). |
| **Signal** poor | Map popup | Round trip to the drone above 600 ms, or three missed pings | Cellular coverage, or a congested link. |

Indicators update live while the page is open. Fleet Manager checks for offline drones every 5 seconds.

![Map close-up with markers showing offline, no MAVLink and weak GPS rings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/map--indicators.webp)

*Close-up of four markers: a healthy drone, one OFFLINE with clock badge, one NO MAVLINK with orange ring, and one WEAK GPS with yellow dashed ring.*

## Activity log

Changes your team makes (pairing, removing drones, stream bindings, invitations, role changes, VPN) are logged under **Recent Activity** on the [Dashboard](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/dashboard/), with who made them.

## System announcements

When UAVmatrix has planned maintenance or an incident, a banner appears at the top of every page: blue for information, amber for a warning, red for critical. Dismissing it hides it until you open Fleet Manager in a new browser session.

## Status page

**System → Status** (page **System Status**) shows whether Fleet Manager is working normally: **All systems operational**, or **We're experiencing some issues** with the **Active Incidents**. **Past Incidents** lists the last resolved ones with their **Resolution**. Check it first when many drones go offline at once.

![System Status page with All systems operational and a list of past incidents](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/status.webp)

*System Status showing All systems operational and two Past Incidents marked Resolved.*

## Email and webhook alerts

Fleet Manager doesn't send email, SMS or webhook alerts for drone events yet (for example low battery or a drone going offline). Keep the map or fleet list open in the control room, and rely on the flight controller's own failsafes for battery and link loss.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/alerts-and-status/

# Licenses and seats

> How UAVcast-Pro licenses and device slots decide which drones you can pair in Fleet Manager, and how to use licenses bought with another email.

Fleet Manager is included with your UAVcast-Pro license. It doesn't have its own subscription, seats or plans. What you can pair is decided by your UAVcast-Pro licenses from the [UAVmatrix store](https://uavmatrix.com/):

- **Drones:** every paired drone runs UAVcast-Pro with an activated license. Each activation uses one of the license's **Device Slots** in the store ("2 of 5 device slots used"). Need more drones? Buy more licenses or slots. **Fleet → Need more devices? → View Plans** takes you to the store.
- **Team members:** free. Fleet Manager doesn't limit how many people you invite, and members don't need a license of their own.

> Fleet Manager is included with a UAVcast-Pro license. Each drone you pair needs one.
>
> [Buy UAVcast-Pro](https://uavmatrix.com/checkout) · [See plans and pricing](https://uavmatrix.com/products)

## What Fleet Manager checks when you pair

When you enter a pairing code, Fleet Manager looks up the license that is activated on that drone and checks that:

1. the license exists and is active, not expired and not refunded, and
2. its **owner's email** (the store account that bought it) belongs to a **member of the organization** you are pairing into, in any role.

If both are true, the drone is paired. Fleet Manager checks again whenever the drone is re-paired.

| Message in the pairing wizard | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **License is not owned by any member of this organization** | The license belongs to a store account whose email isn't a member here. |
| **License has expired** | The license's expiry date has passed. |
| **License has been refunded** | The license was returned. |
| **Invalid license key** | The store doesn't know the license on the drone. Check the activation in UAVcast-Pro. |

The license is also checked one step earlier, when UAVcast-Pro asks for a pairing code. If UAVcast-Pro shows **Invalid or inactive license** instead of a code, the license is expired, refunded or not linked to a store account.

For activation problems on the drone itself, see [Activate your license](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/) and [License won't activate](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/license-activation-failed/).

## Who should own the licenses

Fleet Manager matches by email, so plan who buys:

- **Simplest:** the organization's Owner buys all licenses with the email they sign in to Fleet Manager with.
- **Several buyers:** any member's licenses count, Viewers included. A purchasing colleague can be a Viewer.
- **Customer-owned drones:** if a customer bought the licenses, invite the customer's store email to your organization (Viewer is enough).

## Licenses bought with another email

A common case: licenses were bought with `purchasing@company.com`, but the pilot signs in to Fleet Manager as `anna@company.com`. Pairing fails with **License is not owned by any member of this organization**.

You have two ways to fix it:

1. **Invite the buying email** to the organization. That account must sign in once to accept the invitation.
2. **Ask UAVmatrix support to add a license email** to your account. Support can add one or more extra emails to a Fleet Manager user. Licenses owned by any of those emails then count as that user's when pairing, in every organization the user belongs to.

To request it, open a ticket from the support bubble (category **General Inquiry**) or email [support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com) from the address you sign in with, and list the other email(s) the licenses were bought with. See [Support](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/support/).

Good to know:

- Emails are matched without regard to upper or lower case.
- Each extra email can belong to one Fleet Manager user only.
- Only UAVmatrix support can add or remove these emails. They don't appear in your own settings.
- The licenses stay in the original store account. This only changes who Fleet Manager counts as the owner when you pair.

## Moving licenses between drones

A license is activated per device in UAVcast-Pro, not in Fleet Manager. To move one, free the device slot in UAVcast-Pro or the store, activate it on the new drone, then [pair the new drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/). See [Replace the companion computer](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/#replace-the-companion-computer).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/


---

# Lite view

> Lite view is Fleet Manager's phone-sized control screen: fleet list, live battery, GPS and altitude, flight modes and mission start, pause and RTL.

**Lite Control** is a phone-friendly version of Fleet Manager for use in the field: big buttons, the essentials only, and live updates over your phone's mobile data.

## Open Lite view

On your phone, sign in to Fleet Manager, open the menu and select **Fleet → Lite View**. You can also go straight to `https://fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/lite`. Add it to your home screen for one-tap access.

## Fleet list

The list shows every drone with its status and battery (orange below 40 %, red below 20 %), a **Live updates active** indicator and the count **n online / n total**. Tap a drone to open its control screen.

![Lite view fleet list on a phone with several drones, status and battery](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/lite.webp)

*Lite view on a 390 × 844 phone: Fleet list with 33 online / 46 total, flight mode and battery per drone.*

## Drone screen

- Banners for **Vehicle Armed** and **Failsafe Active**.
- Cards for **Battery**, **GPS**, **Altitude** and **Speed**.
- **Device ID**, **Organization**, **Position** and **View Full Details** (opens the full UAV page).

![Lite view drone screen with armed banner, status cards and control buttons](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/lite--drone.webp)

*Lite view for an armed drone in AUTO: Vehicle Armed banner, Battery, GPS, Altitude and Speed cards, and the mode and mission controls.*

### Safety status

Lite view shows **ARMED** (*Motors active - exercise caution*) or **DISARMED** (*Safe to approach*), but has no arm or disarm button: **For safety, arm/disarm should be performed via your Ground Control Station (QGC, Mission Planner).**

### Flight Mode (Owner and Admin)

**Quick Access** shows the modes you use most for the vehicle type, **All Modes** the full list. Safe modes switch after a simple confirmation; navigation and dangerous modes ask **Change to *MODE*?** with a stronger check, as in the [control panel](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remote-control/#flight-mode).

### Mission Control (Owner and Admin)

For a mission already on the drone:

- **Start** / **Resume**, **Pause**, **RTL** and **Stop**, each with a confirmation. Rovers use HOLD instead of LOITER to pause and stop.
- **Jump to Waypoint**: pick the number with − and +, then **Jump to WP n**. **Currently at waypoint n** shows progress.
- **Refresh Mission Data** reloads the mission from the drone.

If the drone has no mission, you see **No Mission Loaded**. Upload one from [Missions](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/missions/) on a computer first.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/lite-view/

# Settings, account and billing

> The Fleet Manager Settings tabs for profile, organizations, support and history, where billing and invoices live, and how to delete your account.

Open **Settings** from the sidebar (**Organization → Settings**) or the user menu. It has four tabs: **Profile**, **Organizations**, **Support** and **History**.

## Profile

Your name, email, picture and password belong to your UAVmatrix account. **Profile changes are managed through the UAVMatrix Store**: under **Password & Security**, select **UAVMatrix Store** to change them there. Fleet Manager picks up the changes automatically.

![Settings Profile tab with account details, link to the UAVMatrix Store and Danger Zone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/settings--profile.webp)

*Settings → Profile with the Password & Security row and the Danger Zone.*

## Organizations

Rename the organization, edit its description or (Owner only) delete it. See [Set up your organization](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/set-up-organization/#rename-or-delete-the-organization).

## Support

Your support tickets with their status, and the **Support Chat Bubble** switch that shows or hides the floating support button. See [Support and FleetBot](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/support/).

## History

Telemetry retention, pruning and per-drone history deletion, for Owners and Admins. See [Flight history](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/map/flight-history/#how-long-history-is-kept).

## Billing

Fleet Manager has no billing page. Licenses, device slots, orders and invoices are all in your account at [uavmatrix.com](https://uavmatrix.com/). See [Licenses and seats](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/).

## Delete your account

**Profile → Danger Zone → Delete Account** deletes your Fleet Manager account. Type `DELETE` to confirm.

What it removes:

- your profile and account information in Fleet Manager
- all your organization memberships
- all your active sessions
- missions you created and invitations you sent

Entries you made in **Recent Activity** stay, without your name.

> **Owners must hand over first**
>
> You can't delete your account while you own an organization. Fleet Manager lists the organizations and asks you to [transfer ownership](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/#transfer-ownership) or delete them first.

Deleting your Fleet Manager account doesn't delete your UAVmatrix store account or your licenses. Manage those at [uavmatrix.com](https://uavmatrix.com/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/settings/

# Support and FleetBot

> Get help inside Fleet Manager: ask the FleetBot assistant, open a support ticket with a screenshot, follow its status and check system status.

Help is one click away on every Fleet Manager page: the round support button at the bottom right opens a panel with two tabs, **FleetBot** and **Ticket**.

## Ask FleetBot

**FleetBot** is an AI assistant that knows Fleet Manager's pages and features. Ask it things like "How do I connect a second ground station?" and it answers with links to the right page.

![Support panel on the FleetBot tab with a question and an answer linking to the Network page](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/support-bubble--fleetbot.webp)

*Support panel, FleetBot tab, answering how to add a stream binding with a link to Network → Stream Bindings.*

- Type your question in **Ask FleetBot...** and send it.
- A conversation holds up to 20 messages, each up to 2,000 characters. If you reach the limit, start a new conversation.
- FleetBot can be wrong, especially on numbers. Where it disagrees with these docs, the docs win.

> **What FleetBot sees**
>
> FleetBot receives only what you type in the chat, not your drones' data. Messages are sent to Anthropic's Claude AI model to generate the answer. Don't paste auth keys, passwords or license keys.

## Open a support ticket

1. Open the support panel and choose the **Ticket** tab.
2. Choose a **Category**: **Bug Report**, **Feature Request**, **General Inquiry** or **Question**.
3. Enter a **Subject** (5 to 200 characters) and a **Message** (20 to 5,000 characters). Say which drone, what you did and what you expected.
4. Optional: add a screenshot. **Capture** grabs the screen through your browser (you pick the window), **Upload** attaches an image file up to 5 MB.
5. Select **Submit Ticket**.

![Support panel on the Ticket tab with category, subject, message and screenshot fields](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/support-bubble--ticket.webp)

*Ticket tab filled in as a Bug Report about a drone stuck on PAIRING, with Capture and Upload for an optional screenshot.*

You get a ticket number such as `SUP-7KQ2XA`. Fleet Manager also records the page you were on and your browser, so support can reproduce the problem.

> **Include logs for drone problems**
>
> For problems on the drone side, logs help most. A ticket only accepts an image, so email the UAVcast-Pro log bundle (a ZIP file, see [Collect logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/)) or the **Download logs** file from the drone's **Logs** tab to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)**, with your ticket number (for example `SUP-7KQ2XA`) in the subject.

## Follow your tickets

**Settings → Support** lists your tickets with their status: **Open**, **In Progress**, **Resolved** or **Closed**. Open one to see the details and the attached screenshot. Select **Close Ticket** when your issue is solved. You can also create a ticket there with **Create Support Ticket**.

## Hide the support button

Select the hide icon (**Hide support bubble**) in the panel header, or switch **Support Chat Bubble** off in **Settings → Support**. Turn it back on in the same place. You can always open tickets from **Settings → Support**.

## Other ways to get help

- **System status:** **System → Status** shows active and past incidents. If many drones go offline at once, check it first. See [Status indicators and notifications](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/alerts-and-status/#status-page).
- **Email:** [support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com).
- **Community:** the [UAVmatrix Discord](https://discord.gg/xwqMTXh).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/support/

# Security and privacy

> How Fleet Manager secures drones with per-drone TLS certificates, isolates organizations on private WireGuard VPNs, enforces roles and stores data.

This page is for the people who have to sign off on Fleet Manager: security officers, IT and operations managers.

## Drone connection

- **Per-drone client certificates.** At pairing, Fleet Manager issues each drone its own TLS client certificate. The drone uses it to connect to Fleet Manager's MQTT broker on port **8883**, the broker's only public listener. There is no shared password.
- **Each drone can only use its own topics.** The certificate's identity is the drone's device ID, and the broker only lets a drone publish and subscribe under its own topics. One compromised drone can't read or command another.
- **Outbound only.** Drones connect out to Fleet Manager. You don't open inbound ports on the drone or its network.
- **Short pairing window.** Pairing codes are 8 random digits, valid 5 minutes and usable once. Code checks are rate-limited (10 checks and 5 pairing attempts per user per minute). The drone's certificate and VPN key are only handed out until the drone first connects, and never later than 15 minutes after the code expires.
- **Certificate upgrades.** When Fleet Manager tightens the certificate scheme, older drones are flagged **Re-pair required** instead of being silently trusted.

## Private VPN per organization

- Each organization gets its own network on Fleet Manager's VPN server (`vpn-connect.uavmatrix.com`), a self-hosted Tailscale-compatible control server. Traffic between devices is end-to-end encrypted with WireGuard. Devices of one organization can't see another organization's devices: the VPN server enforces a separate access rule for each organization. If Fleet Manager can't confirm that isolation, it hides the auth key (*VPN isolation could not be verified, so the auth key is hidden.*) instead of handing out a key.
- Joining needs an auth key that only Owners and Admins can create. Keys expire after 90 days. Drones receive the key automatically during pairing or **Push to Drone**, and only with an Owner's or Admin's consent.
- Removing a device in **Network** removes it from the VPN server.

## Access control

- Sign-in goes through your UAVmatrix account. Fleet Manager stores no passwords.
- Three roles per organization (Owner, Admin, Viewer), enforced on the server for every action. See [Roles and permissions](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/roles-and-permissions/).
- The SSH terminal and remote access to UAVcast-Pro are limited to Owners and Admins.
- Invitation links are encrypted, can be used once and expire after 7 days.
- UAVmatrix can suspend accounts or organizations that break the terms. Suspended users see **Account Suspended** or **Organization Suspended** with the reason and a support contact.

## Data Fleet Manager stores

| Data | Kept |
| --- | --- |
| Telemetry (position, altitude, speed, heading, battery, mode, armed state, GPS, service status), once per second | Per the organization's retention setting: 7 days to 1 year (default 1 year). Compressed after 7 days. Deleted when the drone is removed. |
| Saved flight names and time ranges | Until deleted, or the drone is removed |
| Commands sent to drones, with who sent them | Until the drone is removed |
| Activity log (who paired, removed, invited, changed roles) | Kept when drones or members are removed |
| Missions | Until deleted, or the organization is deleted |
| Support tickets and their screenshots | Kept for support |

Fleet Manager doesn't store video. Video and MAVLink to ground stations travel over the VPN between your devices, and Fleet Manager doesn't record them.

The terminal and the remote UAVcast-Pro proxy pass through Fleet Manager's encrypted connection to the drone; their content isn't stored.

VPN traffic goes directly between your devices when the networks allow it. When they don't (for example behind strict NAT or a mobile carrier), it falls back to Tailscale's public relay (DERP) servers. The traffic stays end-to-end encrypted with WireGuard either way; UAVmatrix doesn't run a relay.

## Third parties

- **Maps:** map tiles come from Esri; the airspace layer from OpenAIP through Fleet Manager.
- **FleetBot:** chat messages are sent to Anthropic to generate answers. Nothing else from your organization is sent. See [Support and FleetBot](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/support/#ask-fleetbot).
- **Product analytics and error reports:** Fleet Manager uses PostHog for usage analytics, such as which pages are opened and which buttons are used, and to report app errors.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/security/


---

# Fleet Manager troubleshooting

> Fix common Fleet Manager problems: pairing errors, drones stuck on PAIRING or offline, re-pair required, missing streams and failed commands.

Start from what you see. Each row links to the fix, either below or on the shared [troubleshooting](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/) pages.

| What you see | Likely cause | Go to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Invalid pairing code**, **This pairing code has expired**, **This pairing code has already been used** | Typo, code older than 5 minutes, or claimed already | [Pairing code invalid or expired](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/) |
| **License is not owned by any member of this organization** | License bought with an email that isn't a member | [Licenses bought with another email](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/#licenses-bought-with-another-email) |
| **This UAV is already paired to an organization** | The drone still belongs to another organization | [Move a drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/#move-a-drone-to-another-organization) |
| UAVcast-Pro shows **No valid license found** or **Invalid or inactive license** | License not activated on the drone, expired or refunded | [License won't activate](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/license-activation-failed/) |
| No **Pair Device** button | You are a Viewer | [Roles and permissions](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/roles-and-permissions/) |
| Drone stuck on **PAIRING** | The drone hasn't connected to the broker yet | [Stuck on PAIRING](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/troubleshooting/#stuck-on-pairing) |
| Drone **OFFLINE** | No internet, port 8883 blocked, or UAVcast-Pro not running | [Drone offline in Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/drone-offline-fleet-manager/) |
| **Re-pair required** | Old connection certificate | [Re-pair a drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/#re-pair-a-drone) |
| **NO MAVLINK** on the map | UAVcast-Pro has no data from the flight controller | [No MAVLink heartbeat](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/) |
| Binding fails: **Failed to send configuration to drone - it may be offline** | Drone offline or didn't confirm within 15 s | [Binding won't save](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/troubleshooting/#binding-wont-save) |
| Binding exists, no telemetry or video in the ground station | Firewall, wrong port, or stream switched off | [No stream at the ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/troubleshooting/#no-stream-at-the-ground-station) |
| Ground station joined the VPN but can't reach the drone | Device type, drone not on VPN, or UDP blocked | [VPN connected but can't reach the drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/vpn-cant-reach-drone/) |
| Commands don't work, **UAVcast Upgrade Required** | Drone offline, Viewer role, or old UAVcast-Pro | [Commands fail](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/troubleshooting/#commands-fail) |
| **Request timed out. UAVcast may be unreachable.** when opening UAVcast-Pro remotely | Slow link through the proxy | [Proxy is slow or incomplete](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/troubleshooting/#proxy-is-slow-or-incomplete) |
| Invitation email never arrived | Spam filter, or wrong address | [Invitation not received](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/troubleshooting/#invitation-not-received) |

## Stuck on PAIRING

**PAIRING** means Fleet Manager has accepted the code and is waiting for the drone's first heartbeat over MQTT.

1. Look at UAVcast-Pro's **Fleet Management** page. If it still says **Waiting for Manager to confirm pairing...**, the drone hasn't fetched its certificate. Check that it has internet.

2. Check outbound TCP 8883 from the drone:

   ```bash
   nc -vz fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com 8883
   ```

3. If you entered an **older** code from the same drone (for example after selecting **Connect to Fleet Manager** twice), UAVcast-Pro isn't waiting for it. Select **Disconnect from Fleet** if shown, get a new code and pair again into the same organization. The drone keeps its record.

The drone has 15 minutes after the code's expiry to fetch its certificate. After that, pair again.

## Binding won't save

Fleet Manager only saves a binding after the drone confirms it. Check that the drone shows **ONLINE**, then try again. If the drone is online but bindings still fail, the drone may not be on the VPN: check **Network → Connected Devices** for it with type **UAV**, or use **Push to Drone**.

## No stream at the ground station

1. On **Network → Stream Bindings**, check that **Video** and **Telemetry** are switched on and note the **Ports**.
2. Check that the ground station software listens on exactly those ports. Only the first drone on a laptop uses 5600 / 14550; every further drone has its own ports.
3. Allow inbound UDP on those ports in the laptop's firewall. On Windows, allow QGroundControl or Mission Planner on **Private** and **Public** networks.
4. Run `tailscale status` on the laptop and check that the drone is listed.

More detail: [No telemetry in the ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/) and [No video in the ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/).

## Commands fail

- The drone must be **ONLINE**.
- Only Owners and Admins can send commands. Viewers don't get the command buttons, and the server rejects commands from them.
- Arm, disarm and preflight calibration need UAVcast-Pro 6.3.0_rc13 or later. [Update UAVcast-Pro](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/updating/).
- The flight controller can refuse a command, for example arming with failed pre-arm checks. Read its message in the map popup or the **Logs** tab.

## Proxy is slow or incomplete

**Open via Proxy** passes each page request over the drone's link, with 30 seconds per request, and doesn't carry live (WebSocket) features. On a weak cellular link, wait for the page to finish loading, or join the VPN and use **Open via VPN**. See [Open UAVcast-Pro remotely](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remote-uavcast/).

## Invitation not received

Ask the person to check spam. On **Team**, check the email under **Pending Invitations**. If it's wrong, **Revoke** it and invite again. Invitations expire after 7 days.

## Still stuck

Open a ticket from the support button with a screenshot, or email [support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com). Include the drone's name and device ID (on its UAV page). Email the UAVcast-Pro log bundle (a ZIP) to [support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com) with your ticket number, since tickets only take an image. See [Support](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/support/) and [Collect logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/troubleshooting/


---

# Fleet Manager FAQ

> Answers to common Fleet Manager questions: drone limits, licenses, VPN, ground stations, ArduPilot and PX4, data retention and moving drones.

### What do I need to use Fleet Manager?

A UAVmatrix account, and drones running UAVcast-Pro with an activated license. Each drone's license must be owned by a member of your organization. See [Licenses and seats](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/).

### Does Fleet Manager cost extra?

No. Fleet Manager is included with your UAVcast-Pro license. There is no separate subscription, and team members are free.

### How many drones can I manage?

Fleet Manager itself sets no limit. Each drone needs its own UAVcast-Pro license activation, so the number of drones follows the licenses and device slots you own.

### Do team members need a license?

No. Invite as many Admins and Viewers as you need. See [Invite your team](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/).

### Which roles are there?

**Owner**, **Admin** and **Viewer**. There is no "Member" role. See [Roles and permissions](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/roles-and-permissions/).

### Where does the pairing code come from?

From the drone. In UAVcast-Pro, open **Fleet Management → Connect to Fleet Manager**. It shows an 8-digit code that is valid for 5 minutes. You type it into Fleet Manager under **Fleet → Pair Device**. See [Add your first drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/).

### Does Fleet Manager work over 4G/LTE?

Yes. The drone connects outward to Fleet Manager on TCP 8883, so it works behind carrier NAT without a public IP. The carrier must not block port 8883.

### Do I need the VPN?

Only to send video and telemetry from drones to ground stations through Fleet Manager. The map, telemetry, commands, missions, terminal and remote access to UAVcast-Pro all work without it. See [Network and VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/).

### Can one ground station receive several drones?

Yes. Each [stream binding](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/stream-bindings/) gets its own block of ports on that ground station, with room for a second camera and audio. The first drone uses 5600 / 14550.

### Can I keep using my own ZeroTier or Tailscale network?

Yes, if you don't need Fleet Manager's stream bindings. You can decline VPN when pairing. If you accept, a drone already on a Tailscale network is moved to your organization's network. A drone on ZeroTier keeps its ZeroTier network and joins the organization's network alongside it; ZeroTier is only left when you unpair the drone.

### Does it work with ArduPilot and PX4?

Fleet Manager works with any MAVLink flight controller that UAVcast-Pro talks to, ArduPilot or PX4: live map, telemetry, status, the terminal and stream bindings are the same. The flight-mode controls use ArduPilot's modes for Copter, Plane, Rover and Sub, and the mission command list follows ArduPilot naming, so on PX4 change modes and plan missions from your ground station.

### Can I fly a drone from Fleet Manager alone?

Fleet Manager can change modes, arm, and start, pause and stop missions. It is not built for manual stick control. Always keep a pilot with a ground station or RC transmitter in control, and follow your local regulations.

### How long is flight history kept?

Up to 1 year by default. Owners and Admins can shorten it to 7, 14, 30, 60 or 90 days or 6 months. See [Flight history](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/map/flight-history/#how-long-history-is-kept).

### Can I export flight logs?

Not today. Fleet Manager replays flights on the map but doesn't export files or store `.tlog`, DataFlash or video.

### Does Fleet Manager send alerts by email?

Not yet. Status is shown live on the map, fleet list and UAV pages. See [Status indicators and notifications](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/alerts-and-status/).

### What happens when a drone loses its connection?

After 20 seconds without data it is shown as **OFFLINE**, and it reconnects by itself when its link comes back. The flight controller's own failsafes decide what the aircraft does; Fleet Manager doesn't command anything on connection loss.

### How do I move a drone to another organization?

Remove it from the current organization (this deletes its history there), then pair it into the new one. See [Remove or transfer a drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/).

### I bought licenses with a different email. What now?

Invite that email to the organization, or ask support to add it as an extra license email on your account. See [Licenses bought with another email](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/#licenses-bought-with-another-email).

### Is there a mobile app?

There is a phone-friendly [Lite view](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/lite-view/) in the browser.

### Is my data safe?

Each drone has its own TLS client certificate, every organization has its own encrypted VPN, and roles are enforced on the server. See [Security and privacy](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/security/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/faq/
