# Fly beyond visual range over 4G

> Fly a drone over 4G/LTE with UAVcast-Pro, a cellular modem and the Fleet Manager VPN, with telemetry and live video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner.

This guide takes a drone from the bench to a flight over the cellular network: telemetry and live video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner, wherever both ends have coverage. It uses the VPN that comes with [Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/), which is included with your UAVcast-Pro license, so neither side needs a public IP or port forwarding.

**Time:** about an hour. **You need:**

- A companion computer (Raspberry Pi 4 or 5, or another [supported board](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/supported-hardware/)) with UAVcast-Pro [installed](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/installation/) and the [license activated](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/).
- A MAVLink flight controller (ArduPilot or PX4), a USB data cable or TELEM wiring.
- A USB 4G/LTE modem and a data SIM. Disable the SIM PIN in a phone first, it saves trouble.
- A camera, if you want video.
- A laptop with QGroundControl or Mission Planner, and the [Tailscale client](https://tailscale.com/download).
- A [Fleet Manager organization](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/set-up-organization/) where you are Owner or Admin.

> **Rules for beyond-visual-line-of-sight flight**
>
> Flying beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) needs an authorization in most countries. UAVcast-Pro gives you the link; the operational approval, the risk assessment and the fail-safes are your responsibility.

## How it fits together

```text
Flight controller ──USB/UART── UAVcast-Pro ──4G──► internet ──► laptop
                                    │                               │
                                    └──── Fleet Manager VPN ────────┘
                  telemetry and video on the ports of the stream binding
```

The drone sends MAVLink and H.264 video to your laptop's VPN address. The VPN makes the laptop reachable over 4G as if both were on the same local network.

> **Prefer to run your own VPN?**
>
> You can use your own ZeroTier network or Tailscale tailnet instead of Fleet Manager: see [VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/vpn/) and [Remote access with Tailscale](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/remote-access-tailscale/). Steps 1, 2 and 7 to 9 below stay the same.

## 1. Connect the flight controller

1. Plug the flight controller into the companion computer over USB, or wire a TELEM port (TX→RX, RX→TX, GND→GND) and enable MAVLink on that port (`SERIALx_PROTOCOL = 2` on ArduPilot, `MAV_x_CONFIG` on PX4).
2. In UAVcast-Pro, open **Flight Controller → Connection**. Choose **USB** or **UART / Serial** under **Link type**, and leave **Port** and **Baud rate** on **Automatic**.
3. Wait for the status **Connected** and a vehicle in **Vehicle**. If it stays at **No heartbeat**, see [No MAVLink heartbeat](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/).

## 2. Set up the modem

1. Plug in the modem and open **Modem**.
2. Set **Enable cellular Modem?** to **Yes** and pick the **Modem type**: **HiLink** for modems that act as a USB network adapter (for example Huawei E3372h), **Traditional (PPP)** for the rest.
3. For a Traditional modem, leave **Access Point Name (Optional)** empty. UAVcast-Pro finds the APN for your SIM and remembers it.
4. Under **Modem Information**, wait for an operator and an IPv4 address.
5. Go to **Networks** and choose **Modem Priority (Outdoor Mode)**, so traffic leaves over the modem even when Wi-Fi is around.

Details: [Cellular modem](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/cellular-modem/). If the modem connects but nothing loads: [Modem connected, no internet](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/modem-no-internet/).

## 3. Turn on the VPN in Fleet Manager

In Fleet Manager, open **Network**. If it shows **Enable VPN Network**, select it. This creates your organization's private network. See [Network and VPN](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/).

## 4. Pair the drone and put it on the VPN

1. In UAVcast-Pro, go to **Management → Fleet Management** and select **Connect to Fleet Manager**. Note the 8-digit code.
2. In Fleet Manager, go to **Fleet → Pair Device**, enter the code and confirm the device.
3. On the **VPN Connection** step, keep **Enable VPN for this UAV** ticked and select **Complete Pairing**.
4. The drone appears under **Network → Connected Devices** with the **UAV** type and a `100.x.y.z` address.

Full walkthrough: [Add your first drone to Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/).

## 5. Put the laptop on the VPN

1. Install Tailscale on the laptop. You don't need a Tailscale account: Fleet Manager runs its own VPN server.
2. In Fleet Manager, on **Network → Devices**, copy the **GCS Connection Command** under **Connect a Device** and run it on the laptop as administrator (`sudo` on macOS and Linux).
3. The laptop appears in **Connected Devices**. In the **Type** column, select **Configure**, choose **Ground Control Station (GCS)** and select **Complete Setup**.
4. Test: `ping <drone VPN IP>` from the laptop. You can now open the drone's web interface at `http://<drone VPN IP>/`.

Details and screenshots: [Connect a ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/connect-gcs/).

## 6. Send telemetry and video to the laptop

1. In Fleet Manager, go to **Network → Stream Bindings** and select **Add Binding**.
2. Choose the drone and the laptop, then select **Create Binding**. Fleet Manager sends the destination to the drone; it appears on the drone's **Ground Control Stations** page with a cloud icon.
3. Read the binding's video and telemetry ports in the **Ports** column. For the first drone on a laptop they are the defaults, `5600` and `14550`.
4. On the laptop, allow incoming UDP on those ports in the firewall (commands in [No video, check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/#check-3)).

## 7. Start the camera

1. Open **Camera → Camera settings**, set **Enable Camera?** to **Yes** and choose the camera in **Select Camera**.
2. For LTE, start with **Resolution** 1280×720, **Select FPS** 15–20 and **Bitrate:** around 1000–1500 kbps.
3. Settings save as you change them. Press **Start** if the camera isn't running yet.

## 8. Open the ground station

- **QGroundControl** connects to UDP 14550 by itself. For video, set **Source** to **UDP h.264 Video Stream** on the binding's video port in the video settings.
- **Mission Planner**: choose **UDP**, press **Connect**, enter the binding's telemetry port. For video, set the GStreamer source as described on the [Mission Planner](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/mission-planner/) page.

## 9. Test on 4G before you fly

1. Turn off the companion computer's Wi-Fi, or take the drone away from it, so the only path is the modem.
2. Check the dashboard: **Cellular** connected, **VPN** connected, **Ground station** *Sending*, **Video** running.
3. Watch the link for 10 minutes on the ground, ideally at the take-off site. Look for video freezes and telemetry gaps.
4. On **Flight Controller → Connection**, check **GCS Failsafe Information**. If it shows **Warning - Failsafe Disabled**, enable the GCS failsafe on the flight controller (ArduPilot: `FS_GCS_ENABL` on Plane, `FS_GCS_ENABLE` on Copter; PX4: `NAV_DLL_ACT`) and choose its action, so the drone acts on its own when the link drops.

> **Record every flight**
>
> Turn on **Record automatically when armed** under **Camera → Recordings → Settings**. You get the video and a telemetry log of every flight for later review: [Record flights and review them](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/recording-flight-review/).

> **UAVnet is being retired**
>
> UAVnet, UAVmatrix's hosted ZeroTier controller, is being discontinued in favour of Fleet Manager. If your drones use a UAVnet network today, move them to the Fleet Manager VPN as described above.

## Next steps

- [Stream to multiple ground stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/multiple-ground-stations/)
- [Add RTK corrections from an NTRIP caster](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/rtk-ntrip-caster/)
- Managing several drones? [Onboard a fleet with Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/fleet-onboarding/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/bvlos-4g/


---

# Remote access with Tailscale

> Reach your drone over LTE with Tailscale and UAVcast-Pro, no port forwarding: log in by URL or auth key, add the laptop as a GCS, stop key expiry.

Tailscale is a WireGuard-based VPN. If your team already uses it, it is the quickest way to reach a drone over 4G: the drone and your laptop join the same tailnet and talk to each other on their `100.x.y.z` addresses.

Don't have a tailnet? The Fleet Manager VPN, included with your license, does the same without a Tailscale account: see [Fly beyond visual range over 4G](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/bvlos-4g/) and [Onboard a fleet](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/fleet-onboarding/).

**You need:** UAVcast-Pro with internet on the drone (Wi-Fi or modem), a Tailscale account, and the Tailscale client on your laptop.

## 1. Log the drone in to Tailscale

1. In UAVcast-Pro, open **Virtual Private Network**.

2. Set **Enable VPN** to **Yes** and **Services** to **Tailscale**.

3. Choose how to log in:

   - **Web Login**: press **Generate Login URL**, then **Authenticate this device** and log in with your Tailscale account in the page that opens.
   - **Auth Key**: create an auth key in the Tailscale admin console, paste it into **Auth Key**, optionally set **Hostname (Optional)**, and press **Connect with Auth Key**. Use this when you set up drones for someone else, or many at once.

4. Wait for **Connected**. Note the **IPv4 Address** (100.x.y.z).

![Virtual Private Network page with Enable VPN Yes, Services Tailscale, the Fleet Manager, Web Login and Auth Key tabs, and VPN Information showing Not Connected](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/private-network.webp)

*Virtual Private Network with Services set to Tailscale, before the drone is logged in (Not Connected). After login, VPN Information shows the connection details.*

> **Turn off key expiry for drones**
>
> Tailscale device keys expire, and a drone with an expired key drops off the tailnet until someone logs it in again. The **Expires** field shows when. In the Tailscale admin console, disable key expiry for drones you deploy.

## 2. Put the laptop on the same tailnet

Install Tailscale on the laptop and log in with the same account or tailnet. Run `tailscale status`: the drone must be in the list. Then:

```bash
ping <drone tailscale ip>
```

Open the drone's web interface at `http://<drone tailscale ip>/`.

## 3. Send telemetry and video to the laptop

1. In UAVcast-Pro, go to **Ground Control Stations** and press **Add Destination**.
2. In **Destination IP or Host**, enter the **laptop's** Tailscale IPv4 address (run `tailscale ip -4` on the laptop).
3. Switch on **Enable Telemetry** and **Enable Video**.
4. Allow incoming UDP 14550 and 5600 on the laptop's firewall. Windows often treats the Tailscale adapter as a public network.

Open QGroundControl or Mission Planner. Telemetry arrives on UDP 14550 and video on UDP 5600.

## 4. Check the connection quality

The **Relay** field on the **Virtual Private Network** page shows whether traffic goes through a Tailscale relay. A relayed path works but adds delay. Some cellular carriers don't allow direct connections, so test on the carrier you fly with.

## Troubleshooting

- Can't ping the drone: [VPN connected but can't reach the drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/vpn-cant-reach-drone/)
- Ping works, no telemetry: [No telemetry in the ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/)
- If the drone is later paired with Fleet Manager and you choose **Replace existing VPN with Fleet Manager network**, it leaves your tailnet and joins the organization's network.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/remote-access-tailscale/


---

# Stream to multiple ground stations

> Send telemetry and live video from one drone to several QGroundControl or Mission Planner stations with UAVcast-Pro, with read-only observers.

One drone, several screens: a pilot on Mission Planner, a payload operator on QGroundControl, a supervisor watching from the office. UAVcast-Pro sends telemetry and video to every destination you add, each with its own switches.

## How it works

Each entry under **Ground Control Stations** is one destination: an IPv4 address plus a telemetry port and a video port. UAVcast-Pro sends:

- MAVLink telemetry over UDP to **Telemetry Port** (default 14550) when **Enable Telemetry** is on,
- H.264 video over RTP/UDP to **Video Port** (default 5600) when **Enable Video** is on,
- nothing at all when **Enable Endpoint** is off.

Commands from every destination reach the flight controller, unless that destination is **Read Only**.

## 1. Add a destination per station

1. Open **Ground Control Stations** and press **Add Destination** once for each station.
2. Give each a **Name** you will recognize in the field, for example *Pilot – Mission Planner* and *Payload – QGC*.
3. Enter each computer's IPv4 address in **Destination IP or Host**. Over 4G, use VPN addresses.
4. Switch on **Enable Telemetry** and **Enable Video** where they are needed. A station that only needs telemetry saves bandwidth with video off.

![Ground Control Station page with two destination cards and the Add Destination button](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/ground-control.webp)

*Ground Control Station with two destination cards. Add Destination adds one card per station.*

## 2. Make observers read-only

For anyone who should watch but never fly, switch on **Read Only** on their destination. The station still receives live telemetry, but it can't change anything on the vehicle: commands, mode changes, arming, parameter writes, mission writes and RC overrides from it are blocked. This applies from UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3; on earlier versions, Read Only does not block parameter writes. Ground station software may show warnings in this mode, because some of its requests (such as downloading parameters or the mission) go unanswered.

> **Two pilots, one drone**
>
> Without Read Only, every station can command the drone. Agree who flies, and make every other station read-only.

## 3. Two stations on one computer

Two programs on one computer can't listen on the same port. Add two destinations with the same IP and different ports, for example:

| Destination | Telemetry Port | Video Port |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mission Planner | 14550 | 5600 |
| QGroundControl | 14551 | 5603 |

Then set the second program to listen on those ports (in QGroundControl, add a UDP comm link on 14551 and set the video UDP port to 5603).

Space video ports **3 apart** (5600, 5603, 5606 …). Each destination uses its video port, plus video port + 1 for the second camera in [dual stream](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/dual-camera-rc-switching/) and video port + 2 for [audio](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/audio/). Ports closer together collide as soon as you turn on dual stream or audio.

## 4. Mind the uplink

Every video destination is a separate copy of the stream. Three video destinations at 1500 kbps need about 4.5 Mbit/s of uplink from the drone. Over 4G, send video only to the stations that need it, or lower the bitrate on **Camera → Camera settings**. **Dashboard → Network Traffic** shows what the modem actually sends.

## 5. Check that every station gets data

On **Dashboard**, the **Ground station** row shows *Sending to n · x packets/s*. The **Connection check** on **Flight Controller → Connection** lists each ground station output, and any destination left out because its address is invalid.

## With Fleet Manager

In Fleet Manager, ground stations join the organization's VPN and you connect them to drones with **Stream Bindings** on the **Network** page. Each additional drone bound to the same ground station gets its own block of ports. See [Stream bindings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/stream-bindings/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/multiple-ground-stations/


---

# RTK GPS over 4G with an NTRIP caster

> Stream RTCM3 corrections from an NTRIP caster over LTE to your flight controller with UAVcast-Pro for RTK Fixed, with no base station on site.

UAVcast-Pro can pull RTCM3 corrections from an NTRIP caster over the drone's own internet link and pass them to the flight controller. You get RTK Float or RTK Fixed positioning without carrying a base station or a separate radio. Any standard NTRIP v1 or v2 caster works.

```text
NTRIP caster ──RTCM3 over TCP/TLS──► UAVcast-Pro ──MAVLink GPS_RTCM_DATA──► flight controller ──► RTK GPS
      ▲                                    │
      └──────── GGA position (VRS) ────────┘
```

**You need:**

- An RTK-capable GPS on the flight controller, such as a u-blox F9P module, Here3+ or Septentrio Mosaic. Standard M8N/M10 navigation modules can't do RTK.
- UAVcast-Pro with the flight controller **Connected** and internet on the drone.
- A caster account: a national CORS network, a commercial service (Trimble, Hexagon, Topcon …) or the free community caster rtk2go.com.

## 1. Enter the caster

1. Open **Flight Controller → NTRIP / RTK**.
2. Enter **Caster host** and **Port** (usually `2101`).
3. Turn on **Use TLS (HTTPS)** only if your provider requires it. Commercial casters often do, public ones rarely.
4. Enter **Username** and **Password**. For rtk2go.com, use your e-mail address as the username and leave the password empty.
5. Press **Test connection**. Wait for **Caster accepted the credentials.**

## 2. Pick a mountpoint

1. Press **Browse mountpoints**. UAVcast-Pro loads the caster's list.
2. Pick the mountpoint closest to where you fly. The list shows **Format**, **GNSS**, **Country**, **Location** and whether it needs a position (**NMEA**: **Required**).
3. Press **Select**. The name lands in **Mountpoint**.

![Caster card with Enable NTRIP client, caster host, port 2101, mountpoint field, Browse mountpoints button and Use TLS](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/flight-controller--ntrip-caster.webp)

*The Caster card. Browse mountpoints, next to the Mountpoint field, opens the list of mountpoints.*

## 3. Send your position (VRS and nearest-mountpoint casters)

VRS and nearest-mountpoint casters build corrections for your location, so they need your position as an NMEA GGA sentence.

1. Leave **Send GGA upstream** on (the default) with **Send interval (seconds)** at 10.
2. Keep **Position source** on **Live position from flight controller**.
3. Enter **Latitude**, **Longitude** and **Altitude (m)** under the manual position as well. UAVcast-Pro uses it until the flight controller has a GPS fix.

For a single fixed base, GGA does no harm, but you can turn it off.

## 4. Start the stream

Turn on **Enable NTRIP client**. Within seconds the status panel should show:

1. **Status**: **Streaming corrections**, with **Caster response** like `ICY 200 OK`.
2. **RTCM messages forwarded** climbing and **Last RTCM frame** at *just now*.
3. **Recent message types** with your constellations, for example 1005, 1077, 1087, 1097.
4. The RTK fix badge moving from **3D fix** to **RTK Float** and then **RTK Fixed** under open sky.

![NTRIP / RTK tab with the status panel showing Disabled and zero counters, and the GPS quality card showing No fix](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/flight-controller--ntrip.webp)

*The status panel and GPS quality card, shown here before a caster is set up (Disabled, no GPS fix). Once corrections flow, these are the fields to watch.*

The **GPS quality** card adds the receiver's reported accuracy and a measured **Position stability (1σ)** that doesn't rely on the receiver's own estimate. The dashboard shows the state under **RTK corrections** and the fix type under **GPS**.

## Presets

```text
Caster host   rtk2go.com
Port          2101
TLS           off
Username      you@example.com
Password      (empty)
Mountpoint    nearest one from Browse mountpoints
```

```text
Caster host   provider host name
Port          2101 (sometimes 2102 or 443)
TLS           as the provider says
Username      provider account
Password      provider password
Mountpoint    the provider's VRS mountpoint
GGA upstream  on, 10 s, live position from flight controller
```

## Good to know

- Corrections travel over the same MAVLink link as telemetry, so the flight controller link must be up.
- After a brief internet drop, corrections resume within seconds. If the caster goes silent, UAVcast-Pro reconnects by itself.
- Accuracy drops with distance from the base station. Pick the nearest mountpoint, or use a VRS service.

## Troubleshooting

Stuck on **Connecting**, a `401` response, no RTCM data or no RTK fix: [RTK corrections not arriving](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/rtk-corrections-not-arriving/). All settings on this page are described in [NTRIP / RTK](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/ntrip-rtk/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/rtk-ntrip-caster/


---

# Two cameras: RC switching or dual stream

> Connect two cameras to UAVcast-Pro and switch between them from your RC transmitter, or stream both at once with dual stream. Setup, ports and CPU.

UAVcast-Pro handles two cameras, for example a forward camera and a downward or zoom camera. You choose between two modes:

|  | **Switching** (default) | **Dual stream** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What the ground station gets | One video stream, showing camera 1 or camera 2 | Two video streams at the same time |
| How you choose | The camera badges in the web interface, or an RC channel | Both always live |
| Ports | **Video Port** | Camera 1 on **Video Port**, camera 2 on **Video Port (Camera 2)** (default: Video Port + 1) |
| CPU and bandwidth | One encode | Two encodes, about double the uplink |

## 1. Add the second camera

1. Connect both cameras. Two CSI cameras on a Pi 5, a CSI and a USB camera, or two USB cameras all work.
2. Open **Camera → Camera settings**. The camera slots show **CAM 1** and **CAM 2**.
3. Click **Add Camera** on the second slot and choose the camera.
4. **Resolution and FPS from Camera 1 will be used** in switching mode. If camera 2 supports camera 1's resolution, turn on **Match Camera 1 Resolution**; otherwise camera 2 uses its own resolution and is scaled to match.

If a camera is missing from the list, see [Camera not detected](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/camera-not-detected/).

## 2a. Switch cameras from your transmitter

1. Under **RC Channel Switching**, turn on **Enable RC channel camera switching**.
2. Choose a free channel in **RC Channel**. The default is channel 7.
3. Map a two-position switch on your transmitter to that channel.
4. Flip the switch and watch **Current PWM**: below 1500 µs selects camera 1, above 1500 µs selects camera 2.

![Camera Control Panel with Enable Camera set to Yes, CAM 1 filled and an empty Add Camera slot](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/camera--control-panel.webp)

*Camera Control Panel with one camera. The RC Channel Switching panel appears below it only once CAM 2 is added and dual stream is off.*

While RC switching is on, the camera badges in the web interface don't switch cameras. Turn RC switching off to select cameras by hand again.

## 2b. Stream both cameras at once

1. Turn on **Dual stream**. The badge shows **Both live**.
2. Each camera now has its own resolution, FPS and bitrate under **Per-camera settings**.
3. Open **Ground Control Stations**. Each destination now shows **Video Port (Camera 2)**. Leave it empty to use **Video Port** + 1 (5601), or enter a port.
4. On the ground station, receive the second stream on that port, for example with a second QGroundControl video source or a GStreamer window: see [Ground stations & video](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/#set-up-the-receiving-side) for QGroundControl, Mission Planner and GStreamer on every OS.

> **Watch the CPU**
>
> UAVcast-Pro encodes video in software. With two streams, keep an eye on **System load**. When it says **CPU is near its limit**, lower one stream's resolution or bitrate, or turn the second stream off. A Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 is recommended for dual stream.

The **Flight Map** shows one video window per active stream. You can hide them as tabs at the bottom of the map.

## Port planning

With dual stream on, each destination uses two video ports, and audio (if **Send audio to ground stations** is on) uses video port + 2. If you add more destinations on the same computer, space their video ports at least three apart, for example 5600 and 5610.

## Recording both cameras

Under **Camera → Recordings → Settings**, **Record camera 2** works only when dual stream is on. See [Record flights and review them](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/recording-flight-review/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/dual-camera-rc-switching/


---

# Record flights and review them

> Record camera video and telemetry on the drone automatically when armed, store it on USB or SSD, and replay video, map and flight data on one timeline.

Since v6.5.1, UAVcast-Pro records on the drone itself: camera video plus a telemetry log, with one click on the flight map or automatically every time you arm. Recording reuses the stream that is already encoded, so it costs no extra CPU and never interrupts the live video to the ground station. Afterwards, the flight review player shows the video, the map track, the cockpit view and the flight data on one timeline.

## 1. Choose where recordings go

1. Plug in a USB drive or SSD if you want to record to it. Recordings fill storage fast, and a USB SSD is more robust than an SD card.
2. Open **Camera → Recordings** and the **Settings** tab.
3. Under **Storage location**, pick the disk, or **Internal storage**. Press **Look for disks again** if the drive was plugged in after the page opened. **Or another folder** lets you enter a path and confirm with **Use this folder**.
4. Set **Keep free** (default 2 GB). Recording never fills the disk beyond this.

![Recordings Settings tab with storage location, keep free, delete oldest recordings, delete recordings older than and record automatically when armed](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/camera--recordings-settings.webp)

*Camera → Recordings → Settings with Internal storage selected and Record automatically when armed on.*

## 2. Decide when to record

| Setting | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Record automatically when armed** | On | Starts when the motors arm and stops when they disarm. If the link drops in flight, recording carries on. |
| **Record camera 1** / **Record camera 2** | On | Camera 2 only records when dual stream is on. |
| **Delete oldest recordings when space runs low** | On | Works like a dashcam: recording never stops for lack of space. When off, recording stops instead. |
| **Delete recordings older than** | 0 days | 0 keeps recordings until the space is needed. |
| **File length** | 1 min | Recordings are saved in pieces of 1–30 minutes. Shorter pieces lose less after a power cut. |
| **Record telemetry** | **While armed** | **Always while connected** also logs on the ground, starting a new file at every arm, disarm and hour. **Off** records video only. |

## 3. Record by hand

On the **Flight Map**, the **Recording** buttons start and stop each camera (**Record camera 1**, **Stop recording camera 1**) and the telemetry log. Read-only users can watch but can't start recordings.

## 4. Find a flight

Open **Camera → Recordings → Library**. Every flight is listed with its video, a thumbnail and its telemetry. A recording in progress shows a **Rec** badge.

![Recordings library with a storage bar and two recorded flights, each with CAM 1 and Telemetry badges and a Play button](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/camera--recordings.webp)

*Camera → Recordings → Library with two recorded flights, each with camera video and telemetry.*

From the library you can:

- **Play** a flight in the flight review player,
- **Download** video clips as MP4,
- **Delete** a recording: **Delete video only**, or **Delete video and telemetry**.

## 5. Review the flight

The flight review player plays the video next to the map track, the cockpit view and the flight data (**Altitude**, **Speed**, **Battery**, **Satellites**, **Mode**) on one timeline.

![Flight review player with the video area, the map, the cockpit view and a timeline with playback controls](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/camera--flight-review.webp)

*Flight review player: video, map and cockpit view above one timeline.*

- The timeline marks arm, disarm and flight-mode changes, so you can jump to the moment that matters.
- Use **Back 10 seconds** and **Forward 10 seconds**, and **Playback speed** from 0.5× to 4×.
- With two cameras, **Change video layout** switches between **Picture in picture** and **Side by side**; **Show this camera large** swaps them.
- If a recording has no telemetry, the player says *No telemetry log for this recording. Telemetry is logged while the drone is armed.*

## Good to know

- Recordings are stored on the drone. Download what you need to keep before **Delete oldest recordings when space runs low** removes it.
- The dashboard's **Storage** card and the **Recording storage** summary show free space.
- Recording continues with **Enable Live Preview?** switched off.
- If the recording service stops responding, the page says *The recording service is not responding.* Restart the camera service from **Camera → Camera settings** and [collect logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/) if it happens again.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/recording-flight-review/


---

# Onboard a fleet of drones with Fleet Manager

> Plan licenses, then name, pair and connect 20+ UAVcast-Pro drones to UAVmatrix Fleet Manager, with team roles, the organization VPN and stream bindings.

This guide walks through bringing a fleet of, say, 20 drones into [UAVmatrix Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/) in one go: licenses, naming, pairing, the organization VPN, and wiring ground stations to drones. It assumes each drone already runs UAVcast-Pro with its flight controller connected and internet access.

## 1. Plan the licenses

Two rules decide whether a drone can be paired:

- **Every drone needs an active UAVcast-Pro license** on the device. One license can cover several drones: its **Allowed Devices** count is the number of slots. For 20 drones you need 20 slots in total, across one or more licenses.
- **The license must be owned by a member of the organization** you pair into. Fleet Manager matches the e-mail address of the store account that bought the license with the members' e-mail addresses. If purchasing bought the licenses under another account, invite that account to the organization, or ask support to add the purchasing e-mail to your user.

Check this before the pairing day: a drone whose license belongs to an outsider is refused with **License is not owned by any member of this organization**.

## 2. Set up the organization and team

1. Sign in to [fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com](https://fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/) with your uavmatrix.com account and create the organization. See [Set up an organization](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/set-up-organization/).
2. Under **Team**, invite your people. Owners and Admins can pair, control and remove drones; Viewers can only watch. See [Roles and permissions](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/team/roles-and-permissions/).
3. Split the pairing work between two or three Admins if you have many drones. Each user can complete 5 pairings per minute; the limit stops brute-force guessing, and also slows down one person pairing 20 drones back to back.

## 3. Name every drone before pairing

The name a drone has in UAVcast-Pro becomes its name in Fleet Manager. Agree on a pattern, for example `SURVEY-01` … `SURVEY-20`, and label the airframes to match.

On each drone, open UAVcast-Pro → **Fleet Management** and fill in **Device Name**. Without a name the drone appears with its hostname. You can rename it in Fleet Manager later.

## 4. Pair each drone

Repeat for every drone. With two browser windows side by side (the drone's UAVcast-Pro and Fleet Manager), each takes about a minute.

1. In UAVcast-Pro, open **Fleet Management** and press **Connect to Fleet Manager**. An 8-digit **Pairing Code** appears. It expires after 5 minutes.
2. In Fleet Manager, go to **Fleet → Pair Device**.
3. **Select Organization**, then **Enter Pairing Code**.
4. **Confirm Device**: check the name, hostname, architecture and UAVcast version, so you pair the drone you think you are pairing.
5. **VPN Connection**: tick **Enable VPN for this UAV** if ground stations should reach the drone over the organization's VPN. If the drone already uses Tailscale, **Replace existing VPN with Fleet Manager network** moves it to the organization's network.
6. **Complete Pairing**. In UAVcast-Pro, **Fleet Connection** changes to **Connected**.

![Fleet Manager pairing wizard on the Confirm Device step showing UAV name, hostname, architecture and UAVcast version](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/pair-device--confirm.webp)

*Fleet → Pair Device, Confirm Device step.*

Errors and what they mean: [Pairing code invalid or expired](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/). The full wizard is described in [Pair your first UAV](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/).

## 5. Check the fleet

Open **Fleet**. Every drone should be listed as online. On **Fleet Map**, each drone appears at its GPS position once its flight controller has a fix. A drone that shows **Offline** has not reported for 20 seconds: see [Drone offline in Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/drone-offline-fleet-manager/).

## 6. Connect the ground stations

1. Go to **Network** and press **Enable VPN Network** if the organization's VPN is not on yet.
2. Press **Connect a Device**, choose **Ground Control Station (GCS)** and copy the **GCS Connection Command**. Run it in a terminal **on the ground station laptop**, with Tailscale installed. Do not paste it into UAVcast-Pro.
3. The laptop appears under **Ground Stations** once it is connected.
4. Under **Stream Bindings**, press **Add Stream Binding** and link each drone to the ground station that should receive it. The drone must be online, because Fleet Manager pushes the destination to it.
5. Each binding gets its own block of ports on that ground station: the first drone uses the defaults, 5600 (video) and 14550 (telemetry), and each further drone gets the next free block. Set up the ground station software with the ports shown on each binding.

![Fleet Manager Network page with stream bindings linking several drones to one ground station with auto-assigned ports](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/network--stream-bindings.webp)

*Network → Stream Bindings: each binding shows its ground station and its video and telemetry ports.*

Details: [Connect a ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/connect-gcs/) and [Stream bindings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/stream-bindings/).

> **Dual stream and audio**
>
> Each binding gets its own block of ports on the ground station, with room for the drone's second camera and audio after its video port, so several drones can share one ground station.

## 7. Day-to-day

- **Re-pair required**: when Fleet Manager shows this badge, re-pair the drone once from UAVcast-Pro. It keeps its name and history. See [Remove or transfer a UAV](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/).
- **Replacing a drone's SD card or board** frees nothing by itself: unregister the old device under **Application → License Manager → Activated Devices** on any drone that uses the same license, then pair the new one.
- **Remote work on a drone**: the UAV details page in Fleet Manager has a terminal, logs and actions such as reboot. See [UAV details](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/uav-details/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/fleet-onboarding/


---

# Troubleshooting

> Fix no video, no MAVLink heartbeat, modem and VPN problems, license errors and Fleet Manager pairing. Start from what you see and follow the checks.

Start from the symptom. Each page below lists the likely causes in the order they happen in the field, with numbered checks that use the exact labels from the UAVcast-Pro and Fleet Manager interfaces.

> **Check the dashboard first**
>
> Open **Dashboard** in UAVcast-Pro. The status card sums up the drone in one line (**All systems normal**, or the number of problems and warnings) and has a row each for **Flight controller**, **Ground station**, **Cellular**, **VPN**, **RTK corrections**, **Video** and **Power supply**. The first red row is usually the place to start.

![UAVcast-Pro dashboard with the status card showing 2 problems: GPS no fix and VPN not connected](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/dashboard.webp)

*Dashboard → status card. Rows with a problem turn red and are counted in the problems badge, here GPS (no fix) and VPN (not connected).*

## Match your symptom

| What you see | Likely cause | Go to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Telemetry works, but the video area in QGroundControl or Mission Planner is black | **Enable Video** is off for that ground station, wrong IP, or a firewall | [No video in the ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/) |
| Video freezes, smears grey or lags seconds behind | Bitrate too high for the link, or keyframes too far apart | [Choppy or delayed video](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/choppy-or-delayed-video/) |
| Flight Controller page says **No heartbeat**, **Waiting for device** or **Detecting baud rate** | Cable, wiring, port or baud rate | [No MAVLink heartbeat](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/) |
| UAVcast-Pro shows the flight controller as **Connected**, the GCS waits for a connection | Telemetry is not sent to the GCS, or the GCS is not listening | [No telemetry in the ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/) |
| **No cameras available** in **Select Camera** | CSI camera stack missing, ribbon cable, or USB camera not seen | [Camera not detected](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/camera-not-detected/) |
| **Invalid license key**, **Maximum activations reached** or **License activation failed** | Wrong key, no free device slot, or no internet | [License won't activate](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/license-activation-failed/) |
| Modem shows a signal and an operator, but nothing loads | APN, network priority or SIM data | [Modem connected, no internet](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/modem-no-internet/) |
| The browser can't reach `http://<device-ip>/` after installing | Wrong address, service not running, or port changed | [Web interface won't open](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/web-interface-wont-open/) |
| The installer stops with an error | 32-bit OS, no internet, or low disk space | [Installation fails](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/installation-fails/) |
| ZeroTier or Tailscale says connected, but you can't ping or open the drone | Member not authorized, wrong network, or GCS not on the VPN | [VPN connected but can't reach the drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/vpn-cant-reach-drone/) |
| NTRIP status is not **Streaming corrections**, or the fix never reaches **RTK Fixed** | Caster settings, GGA, or a receiver that can't do RTK | [RTK corrections not arriving](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/rtk-corrections-not-arriving/) |
| **Voltage too low - use a stronger power supply** or **Slowed down (heat or power)** | Weak power supply or cable, overheating | [Undervoltage and throttling](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/undervoltage-and-throttling/) |
| The drone is **Offline** in Fleet Manager | Drone has no internet, MQTT port blocked, or re-pair required | [Drone offline in Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/drone-offline-fleet-manager/) |
| **Invalid pairing code**, **This pairing code has expired** or **License is not owned by any member of this organization** | Code typed wrong or too old, or license owned by someone outside the org | [Pairing code invalid or expired](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/) |

## Still stuck?

1. [Collect the log files](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/). The download includes a `diagnostics.txt` snapshot of your settings and hardware, so support doesn't need to ask for them.
2. Send them to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)** with your UAVcast-Pro version, the hardware you use and what you have already tried. You can also ask in the [UAVmatrix Discord](https://discord.gg/xwqMTXh).

Short answers to common questions are in the [FAQ](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/faq/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/


---

# No video in QGroundControl or Mission Planner

> Telemetry works but video stays black in QGroundControl or Mission Planner? Check the camera, Enable Video, the destination IP, UDP 5600 and the GCS.

Telemetry arrives and the drone shows on the map, but the video area stays black, or QGroundControl's video window says **WAITING FOR VIDEO**. Work through the checks in order. Most cases are solved by check 2 or 3.

![QGroundControl Fly view connected to an ArduPilot vehicle: toolbar with Not Ready and Stabilize, a five-waypoint mission on the map with No GPS Lock for Vehicle, and the video window in the bottom-left corner showing WAITING FOR VIDEO](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/gcs/qgroundcontrol--fly-view.webp)

*The symptom in QGroundControl: telemetry arrives (Not Ready, Stabilize in the toolbar; No GPS Lock because this bench setup has no GPS), but the video window in the bottom-left corner says WAITING FOR VIDEO.*

| What you see | Likely cause | Start at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Video is black in the GCS and in the UAVcast-Pro live preview | The camera is not running on the drone | [Check 1](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/#check-1) |
| Live preview works, the ground station stays black | Enable Video is off for this ground station, or the IP is wrong | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/#check-2) |
| Worked on Wi-Fi at home, black over 4G | The destination uses a local IP instead of the VPN IP | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/#check-2) |
| Everything looks right, still black on Windows | The firewall blocks incoming UDP on port 5600 | [Check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/#check-3) |
| QGroundControl shows video, Mission Planner does not | Mission Planner has no GStreamer source set | [Check 4](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/#check-4) |

## Check 1: Confirm the camera is streaming on the drone

If the drone isn't producing video, no ground station setting will help.

1. Open the UAVcast-Pro web interface and go to **Camera → Camera settings**.
2. Check that **Enable Camera?** is **Yes** and that a camera is chosen in **Select Camera**.
3. Check that the camera runs: the dashboard's **Video** row should say **Running**. If it is stopped, press **Start** on the Camera page (the button reads **Restart** while the camera runs).
4. Turn on **Enable Live Preview?** and look at **Live Preview**. If you see a picture, the camera works and you can go to check 2.
5. If **Select Camera** says **No cameras available**, go to [Camera not detected](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/camera-not-detected/).

![UAVcast-Pro Camera settings page with CAM 1 enabled and the Live Preview panel showing No Video Available](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/camera.webp)

*Camera → Camera settings with CAM 1 enabled. Live Preview shows No Video Available until Enable Live Preview? is ticked.*

> **The preview is not the ground station stream**
>
> The browser preview goes through the built-in media server (WebRTC on port 8889). The ground station gets a separate H.264 stream over UDP. A working preview proves the camera works, not that the UDP stream reaches your laptop.

If the **Action Logs** on the Camera page say a camera *does not support* a resolution, pick another value in **Resolution**. UAVcast-Pro falls back to the largest supported size and logs which one it used.

## Check 2: Check the ground station destination

UAVcast-Pro only sends video to destinations where video is switched on. Telemetry and video have separate switches, and **both are off on a new destination**.

1. Go to **Ground Control Stations** and find the card for the computer that runs your ground station.
2. Make sure **Enable Endpoint** and **Enable Video** are both on.
3. Check **Destination IP or Host**. It must be the IPv4 address of the ground station computer as seen from the drone. Hostnames are not accepted.
4. Check that **Video Port** is `5600`, or the port your ground station listens on.
5. Fields save when you leave them or press Enter. A green tick confirms the save.

![Video Port 5600 and the Enable Video switch turned on](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/ground-control--video-enabled.webp)

*Ground Control Stations: a destination with Enable Video on and Video Port 5600.*

> **Flying over 4G? Use the VPN IP**
>
> Over a cellular link the drone can't reach your laptop's local address (like `192.168.1.20`). Use the address your laptop has on the VPN (Fleet Manager VPN, Tailscale or ZeroTier). On Windows, run `ipconfig` and look for the Tailscale or ZeroTier adapter.

Using Fleet Manager? Destinations are created for you when you add a stream binding, and each extra drone on the same ground station gets its own ports. Check the video port shown on the binding, not 5600. See [Stream bindings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/stream-bindings/).

## Check 3: Allow UDP 5600 through the firewall

Video arrives as incoming UDP traffic. On Windows this is blocked by default, even when telemetry gets through because the ground station asked for an exception.

**Windows**

Open **PowerShell as Administrator** and run:

```powershell
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "UAV Video" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 5600 -Action Allow
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "MAVLink Telemetry" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 14550 -Action Allow
```

The ZeroTier and Tailscale adapters are often classed as a *Public* network. A rule created this way applies to all profiles.

**Linux**

```bash
sudo ufw allow 5600/udp comment 'UAV Video'
sudo ufw allow 14550/udp comment 'MAVLink Telemetry'
```

**macOS**

The macOS firewall allows incoming UDP for apps you approve. If you clicked *Deny* when QGroundControl first started, allow it again in **System Settings → Network → Firewall → Options**.

## Check 4: Set up video in your ground station

**QGroundControl**

1. Click the **Q** icon, then **Application Settings**.
2. Open the video settings (**Video**, or **General → Video** in older versions).
3. Set **Source** to **UDP h.264 Video Stream**, and check that the UDP address uses port `5600` (**UDP URL** `0.0.0.0:5600` in current versions, **UDP Port** `5600` in older ones).
4. Go back to the Fly view. The video tile should show a picture within a few seconds.

**Mission Planner**

Mission Planner shows video in the HUD. If it stays black, set the source by hand:

1. Right-click the HUD and choose **Video → Set GStreamer Source**.
2. Paste this pipeline and confirm:

```text
udpsrc port=5600 caps="application/x-rtp, media=video, clock-rate=90000, encoding-name=H264, payload=96" ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! video/x-raw,format=BGRA ! appsink name=outsink
```

## Check 5: Test the stream without a ground station

This takes the ground station software out of the picture. If a window with video opens, the drone, network and firewall are fine and the problem is in the GCS settings.

```bash
gst-launch-1.0 -v udpsrc port=5600 caps="application/x-rtp, media=(string)video, clock-rate=(int)90000, encoding-name=(string)H264" ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtph264depay ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! autovideosink sync=false
```

> **Windows: choose the Complete installation**
>
> When you install GStreamer (MSVC 64-bit runtime), pick **Complete**. The Typical installation leaves out the H.264 decoder and the command fails with `no element "avdec_h264"`.

Close the test before you open your ground station again: only one program can listen on port 5600 at a time. Step-by-step receiver setup: [Mission Planner](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/mission-planner/), [QGroundControl](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/qgroundcontrol/), and GStreamer on [Windows](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-windows/), [Linux](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-linux/) or [macOS](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/gstreamer-macos/).

> **Video now, but choppy over 4G?**
>
> See [Choppy or delayed video](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/choppy-or-delayed-video/).

## Still no video?

[Download the logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/) with **Camera Server** selected in the log list, and send them to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)** together with your UAVcast-Pro version, the camera model and the ground station you use.

Related: [Camera settings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/) · [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/


---

# Choppy, laggy or grey video over 4G

> Fix stuttering, grey smears and lag in UAVcast-Pro video over LTE or VPN by matching bitrate, resolution, FPS and Stream Recovery Rate to the link.

The picture arrives, but it stutters, freezes, smears grey blocks across the screen or runs seconds behind. Almost always the stream asks for more than the link can carry, or the encoder sends keyframes too rarely to recover from lost packets.

| What you see | Likely cause | Start at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Grey or green smears that clear up after a second or two | Packets lost and too few keyframes to recover | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/choppy-or-delayed-video/#check-2) |
| Smooth on Wi-Fi, stutters or freezes over LTE | Bitrate above what the cellular uplink carries | [Check 1](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/choppy-or-delayed-video/#check-1) |
| Stutters even on the local network | CPU limit on the drone, or the GCS can not decode fast enough | [Check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/choppy-or-delayed-video/#check-3) |
| Video is seconds behind the drone | You are looking at the browser preview, or the GCS buffers | [Check 4](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/choppy-or-delayed-video/#check-4) |

## Check 1: Lower the bitrate and resolution

A cellular uplink is much slower than its download speed and changes as the drone moves between cells. Start low and step up.

1. Go to **Camera → Camera settings**.
2. Set **Resolution** to 1280×720 or lower.
3. Set **Select FPS** to 15 or 20.
4. Move the **Bitrate:** slider to about 1000–1500 kbps. `0` means auto.
5. Settings save as you change them, and the camera picks them up.
6. Fly, or drive, the route you care about. If it holds up, raise one value at a time.

![Camera Settings card with Resolution, Select FPS, Bitrate and Stream Recovery Rate](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/camera--settings.webp)

*Camera → Camera Settings: Resolution, Select FPS, Bitrate and Stream Recovery Rate are the values to tune for the uplink.*

> **How much does the link carry?**
>
> **Dashboard → Network Traffic** shows the live TX rate per interface. If the modem interface sits at the same ceiling whatever bitrate you set, that ceiling is your uplink.

## Check 2: Set a faster Stream Recovery Rate

Grey overlays come from lost packets. The decoder can only repair the picture at the next keyframe. **Stream Recovery Rate** sets how often keyframes are sent.

1. In **Camera → Camera settings**, find **Stream Recovery Rate**.
2. Move the slider from **Auto** towards **Ultra Fast**: fewer frames between keyframes repair the picture sooner but use more bandwidth. Towards **Bandwidth Saver** saves bandwidth but recovers slowly. The hint under the slider (for example *VPN/WiFi Friendly*) tells you what each position suits.
3. Save, and compare. If the link is very slow, combine a faster recovery rate with a lower bitrate (check 1).

On **Auto**, UAVcast-Pro sends one keyframe per second (one every *FPS* frames, or every 30 frames when FPS is on auto).

## Check 3: Look at the CPU load

UAVcast-Pro encodes H.264 in software. On a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, or with two cameras streaming at once, the CPU can run out.

1. Open **Camera → Camera settings** and look at the **System load** card.
2. If it says **CPU is near its limit. Lower the resolution or bitrate.**, do exactly that.
3. With **Dual stream** on, lower one stream's resolution or bitrate, or turn the second stream off.
4. Check **Dashboard** for **Slowed down (heat or power)** under **Power supply**. A throttled CPU encodes slower. See [Undervoltage and throttling](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/undervoltage-and-throttling/).

## Check 4: Know which stream you are watching

The **Live Preview** in the browser and the video window on the **Flight Map** go through the built-in media server, which adds delay. They are for setup, not for flying. The stream to your ground station goes straight over UDP and has much lower latency.

If the ground station itself lags:

- In QGroundControl, check that low-latency mode is on in the video settings.
- In GStreamer pipelines, use `sync=false` on the video sink, as in the [test command](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/#check-5).
- Over VPN, make sure ZeroTier or Tailscale reaches the drone directly and not through a relay. Tailscale shows the relay in use under **Relay** on the **Virtual Private Network** page.

## Check 5: Check the cellular signal

Go to **Modem** and look at **Signal Quality** and **Technology** under **Modem Information**. A weak signal, or a fall back from LTE to 3G, cuts the uplink. Move the modem away from the flight controller, ESCs and power wires, or use a modem with external antennas.

## Still choppy?

[Download the logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/) (**Camera Server**, last 30 minutes) and send them to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)** with your camera model, resolution, FPS, bitrate and the kind of link you fly on.

Related: [Camera settings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/) · [Cellular modem](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/cellular-modem/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/choppy-or-delayed-video/


---

# No MAVLink heartbeat from the flight controller

> UAVcast-Pro shows No heartbeat or Waiting for device? Check the USB cable, TELEM wiring, SERIAL protocol and baud rate, then use Auto-detect.

The **Flight Controller → Connection** page shows **No heartbeat**, **Waiting for device**, **Detecting baud rate** or **Searching**, and the dashboard's **Flight controller** row never turns green. UAVcast-Pro can't hear the flight controller yet.

The page has a live **Connection check** that tests each step once per second and explains the first problem it finds. Read it first: it is usually faster than this page.

![Connection check card with four rows: flight controller plugged in, readable flight controller data, flight controller responding and sending to ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/flight-controller--connection-check.webp)

*The Connection check on a working link: all four steps pass. When the link fails, the first failing step is marked and explained.*

| What you see | Likely cause | Start at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Waiting for device, or Flight controller plugged in: Not detected | No data cable, or the board is not powered | [Check 1](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/#check-1) |
| Signal on the wire, but no readable data | Wrong baud rate, TX/RX swapped, or the port is not set to MAVLink | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/#check-2) |
| Readable data shows a high % damaged | Loose or long wire, missing ground, or electrical noise | [Check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/#check-3) |
| Port shows in use by another program | Something else holds the serial port | [Check 4](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/#check-4) |
| Status Off or Stopped | The link is switched off | [Check 5](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/#check-5) |

## Check 1: Is the flight controller seen at all?

**Over USB:**

1. Make sure the flight controller is powered and its USB cable goes to the companion computer.
2. Try another cable. Many USB cables only charge and carry no data. If the board lights up but **Flight controller plugged in** says **Not detected**, the cable is the usual cause.
3. Under **Link type**, choose **USB** and leave **Port** on **Automatic**. Automatic finds the flight controller and follows it if the device number changes.

**Over a TELEM port (UART / Serial):**

1. Under **Link type**, choose **UART / Serial**.
2. Check the wiring: flight controller **TX → RX** on the companion computer, **RX → TX**, and **GND → GND**. A missing ground wire is a common cause.
3. Never power the Raspberry Pi from the TELEM port. Power it separately.

> **Raspberry Pi serial port**
>
> The installer enables the Pi's UART and removes the serial console from `cmdline.txt`. On a Pi 3, 4 or Zero 2 W it also disables Bluetooth so the full UART is free. If you installed the OS again after UAVcast-Pro, run the installer again.

## Check 2: Match the port settings on the flight controller

On a TELEM port, the flight controller must speak MAVLink at the speed UAVcast-Pro listens on. USB connections don't use a baud rate.

1. Connect the flight controller to Mission Planner or QGroundControl over USB.
2. Open the full parameter list and find the serial port you wired: `SERIAL1` for TELEM1, `SERIAL2` for TELEM2.
3. Set `SERIALx_PROTOCOL` to `2` (MAVLink2). Write the parameters and reboot the flight controller.
4. Note `SERIALx_BAUD`. In UAVcast-Pro, leave **Baud rate** on **Automatic**, or pick the same value.

With **Automatic**, UAVcast-Pro tries 57600, 115200, 921600, 1500000, 460800, 230400 and 500000 baud and remembers the rate that worked. The status shows *Trying … baud (n of 7)* while it searches.

> **Let UAVcast-Pro search for you**
>
> Press **Auto-detect**. It pauses the link, listens on every port and baud rate, then saves what it finds. This can take up to a minute. If it reports **No flight controller found**, open **Show what was tried** to see each port and speed it tested.

## Check 3: Damaged data

If **Readable flight controller data** shows a percentage *damaged*, bytes are arriving but corrupted. This usually means a loose or long wire, a missing ground wire, or noise from motors and power cables.

- Re-seat the connectors and shorten the cable.
- Route the signal wires away from ESC and battery leads.
- Try a lower `SERIALx_BAUD`, for example 57600 or 115200.

## Check 4: Port in use

The **Port** list marks ports that another program holds (*in use by …*). Stop that program, for example a MAVProxy or a second router you started yourself, or pick another port.

## Check 5: Is the link switched on?

At the top of the page, **Link enabled** must be on. If the status says **Link stopped**, press **Connect**. Settings apply immediately, without a restart.

## Still no heartbeat?

[Download the logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/) with **Mavlink Manager** selected. The included `diagnostics.txt` lists the serial devices, who holds them and the USB and power events from the kernel, which is what support needs for link problems.

Once the flight controller shows **Connected** but your ground station still waits, go to [No telemetry in the ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/).

Related: [Flight controller connection](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/) · [Hardware requirements](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/hardware-requirements/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/


---

# No telemetry in QGroundControl or Mission Planner

> Flight controller connected in UAVcast-Pro but QGroundControl or Mission Planner keeps waiting? Check Enable Telemetry, the IP, UDP 14550 and VPN.

UAVcast-Pro shows the flight controller as **Connected**, but QGroundControl says *Waiting for vehicle connection* or Mission Planner times out with *No heartbeat packets received*. The drone hears the flight controller; the telemetry just doesn't reach your ground station.

If UAVcast-Pro itself shows **No heartbeat**, fix that first: [No MAVLink heartbeat](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/).

| What you see | Likely cause | Start at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dashboard: Ground station None set up, or Not sending | No destination, or Enable Telemetry is off | [Check 1](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/#check-1) |
| Dashboard says Sending, the GCS sees nothing | Wrong IP, firewall, or the GCS listens on another port | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/#check-2) |
| Worked on Wi-Fi, nothing over 4G | Destination is a local IP instead of the VPN IP | [Check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/#check-3) |
| Used to connect over TCP 5760, stopped after an update | TCP 5760 was closed in v6.5.0 | [Check 4](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/#check-4) |
| Telemetry shows, but commands and mode changes do nothing | Read Only is on for this destination | [Check 5](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/#check-5) |

## Check 1: Is telemetry being sent?

1. Open **Dashboard** and read the **Ground station** row in the status card.

   - **None set up**: there is no destination. Add one in step 2.
   - **Not sending**: a destination exists but nothing goes out.
   - **Sending to … · n packets/s**: telemetry leaves the drone. Go to check 2.

2. Go to **Ground Control Stations**. Press **Add Destination** if the list is empty.

3. On the card for your computer, switch on **Enable Endpoint** and **Enable Telemetry**. Both video and telemetry are off on a new destination.

4. Enter the computer's IPv4 address in **Destination IP or Host** and keep **Telemetry Port** at `14550`.

![Telemetry section of a destination with Enable Telemetry on and Read Only off](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/ground-control--telemetry-enabled.webp)

*Ground Control Stations: a destination with Enable Telemetry on.*

> **Invalid addresses are skipped**
>
> UAVcast-Pro only accepts IPv4 addresses such as `192.168.1.10`. If you try to save a hostname, you get *Enter a valid IPv4 address, for example 192.168.1.10.* An address that is missing or invalid is left out of the telemetry router, and the **Connection check** on the Flight Controller page lists it.

## Check 2: Make sure the ground station listens

UAVcast-Pro sends MAVLink over UDP to the address and port you set. The ground station must listen on that port.

- **QGroundControl** listens on UDP 14550 by default. If you changed **Telemetry Port**, add a UDP comm link on the same port in **Application Settings → Comm Links**.
- **Mission Planner**: choose **UDP** in the connection drop-down at the top right, press **Connect** and accept port `14550`.
- Only one program can listen on a port. Close MAVProxy, a second QGroundControl or another tool that may hold 14550.
- Allow incoming UDP 14550 in the firewall. The commands are in [No video, check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/#check-3).

## Check 3: Use the VPN address over cellular

Over 4G the drone can't reach a local address like `192.168.1.20`. Put your computer's VPN address (Fleet Manager VPN, Tailscale or ZeroTier) in **Destination IP or Host**.

From the computer, ping the drone's VPN address. If the ping fails, the VPN is the problem: see [VPN connected but can't reach the drone](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/vpn-cant-reach-drone/).

## Check 4: TCP 5760 no longer works

Since v6.5.0 the telemetry router does not accept TCP connections on port 5760, so only the ground stations you add, and switch on, get data. If you used to connect Mission Planner over TCP 5760, add your computer as a destination and connect over UDP instead.

## Check 5: Commands are ignored

If telemetry shows but arming, mode changes or mission uploads do nothing, check **Read Only** on that destination. Read Only blocks everything that would change the vehicle (commands, mode changes, parameter and mission writes), so the ground station can only watch. This applies from UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3; on earlier versions, Read Only does not block parameter writes. Some ground stations show warnings in this mode because some of their requests go unanswered.

## Still nothing?

[Download the logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/) with **Mavlink Manager** selected and send them to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)**. Mention which ground station you use and its IP address.

Related: [Ground Control Stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/) · [Ports and protocols](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/ports-and-protocols/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/


---

# Camera not detected

> UAVcast-Pro shows No cameras available? Check the CSI ribbon cable, rpicam-hello, camera support on Ubuntu and v4l2-ctl for USB cameras.

**Camera → Camera settings** shows **No cameras available** in **Select Camera**, the camera you want is missing from the list, or the **Action Logs** say *No camera detected*.

| What you see | Likely cause | Start at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A Raspberry Pi CSI camera (ribbon cable) is missing | Cable, connector or the camera stack | [Check 1](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/camera-not-detected/#check-1) |
| CSI camera on Ubuntu | Ubuntu has no Raspberry Pi camera stack by default | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/camera-not-detected/#check-2) |
| A USB camera is missing | Not seen by Linux, or not a video capture device | [Check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/camera-not-detected/#check-3) |
| Camera listed but video never starts | Unsupported resolution or another program holds it | [Check 4](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/camera-not-detected/#check-4) |

## Check 1: Raspberry Pi CSI camera

1. Power off the Pi. Re-seat the ribbon cable at both ends with the contacts facing the right way, and close the connector latches. A Pi 5 and a Pi Zero 2 W need the narrower 22-pin cable.

2. Boot and run this on the Pi:

   ```bash
   rpicam-hello --list-cameras
   ```

   On older Raspberry Pi OS images the command is `libcamera-hello --list-cameras`.

3. If the camera is not listed here, Linux can't see it. Try another cable or camera before changing anything in UAVcast-Pro.

4. If it is listed, restart the camera from the Camera page (**Restart**, or **Stop** then **Start**) and open **Select Camera** again. Each CSI camera appears as its own entry, for example *CSI Camera 0 - imx708 (libcamera)*.

> **Two CSI cameras**
>
> For two cameras the camera driver needs more memory. Since v6.2.2 the installer raises the CMA memory in `config.txt` automatically for multi-camera setups. Reboot after installing if you added the second camera later.

## Check 2: CSI camera on Ubuntu or Debian

UAVcast-Pro uses `rpicam-vid` for CSI cameras. The installer installs `rpicam-apps` (or `rpicam-apps-core`) on Raspberry Pi OS and Debian. On Ubuntu the Raspberry Pi camera stack is not packaged, and the log says *CSI camera not available: Ubuntu requires building libcamera from source. USB cameras are supported.*

Use Raspberry Pi OS 64-bit if you need a CSI camera, or use a USB camera on Ubuntu.

## Check 3: USB camera

1. Plug the camera straight into the companion computer, not through an unpowered hub.

2. Run:

   ```bash
   v4l2-ctl --list-devices
   ```

3. If the camera is missing, Linux does not see it. Check `lsusb` and try another port and cable.

4. If it is listed, restart the camera with **Restart** on the Camera page and open **Select Camera** again.

Most UVC webcams work, for example Logitech C920 and C615. Cameras that only output a format the encoder can't take, or devices that are not video capture devices (some capture cards), are not listed.

## Check 4: Listed, but video doesn't start

- If the log says *Camera … does not support …x… - streaming at …x… instead*, pick a resolution the camera supports in **Resolution**.
- Close any other program that uses the camera. Only one program can open it at a time.
- If **Enable Camera?** shows *Insufficient permissions*, update to v6.5.2 or later, which fixed this.

## Still not detected?

[Download the logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/) with **All Logs** selected, add the output of `rpicam-hello --list-cameras` or `v4l2-ctl --list-devices`, and send everything to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)**.

Related: [Camera settings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/camera/) · [Supported hardware](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/supported-hardware/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/camera-not-detected/

# UAVcast-Pro license won't activate

> Fix Invalid license key, Maximum activations reached and License activation failed in UAVcast-Pro: the key, internet, free slots and replaced hardware.

You enter the key under **Application → License Manager**, press **Validate**, and get an error instead of **License activated successfully**. Until a license is active on this device, every page sends you back to **Application**.

> You need a UAVcast-Pro license to activate the drone. Buy one in the UAVmatrix store.
>
> [Buy UAVcast-Pro](https://uavmatrix.com/checkout) · [See plans and pricing](https://uavmatrix.com/products)

![Application page License Manager with license key field, License Details and the Activated Devices table](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/application--license-activated.webp)

*Application → License Manager on an activated device: License Details and the Activated Devices table, with this device marked Current.*

| What you see | Likely cause | Start at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invalid license key, or Invalid license key format | Typo, extra spaces, or a key for another product | [Check 1](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/license-activation-failed/#check-1) |
| Maximum activations reached | All device slots on the key are in use | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/license-activation-failed/#check-2) |
| Worked before, asks again after a new SD card or new board | The device counts as a new device | [Check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/license-activation-failed/#check-3) |
| License activation failed, or nothing happens | No internet, or the wrong time on the device | [Check 4](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/license-activation-failed/#check-4) |
| Cannot connect to license service | The UAVcast-Pro background service is not running | [Check 5](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/license-activation-failed/#check-5) |
| License Status: Expired | A time-limited license ran out | [Check 6](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/license-activation-failed/#check-6) |

## Check 1: The key itself

1. Copy the key from your order e-mail or your account on [uavmatrix.com](https://uavmatrix.com/), and paste it into the **License Key** field. Typing it by hand is the most common source of errors.
2. Make sure there are no spaces before or after the key.
3. Press **Validate**.

## Check 2: Free a device slot

Each license allows a fixed number of devices (**Allowed Devices**). When **Remaining Devices** is 0, activation fails with **Maximum activations reached. Please deactivate another device first or upgrade your license.**

1. On any device where the license is active, open **Application → License Manager → Activated Devices**.
2. Find the device you no longer use and press **Unregister**. The slot is freed straight away.
3. Activate the new device.

If you can't reach any activated device, contact **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)** with the license key and they can free a slot. To add slots, buy more devices for the license on [uavmatrix.com](https://uavmatrix.com/).

## Check 3: You replaced the SD card or the board

The license is tied to the hardware, including the storage device. A fresh SD card, a new SSD or a new board counts as a new device and takes a new slot. Unregister the old entry in **Activated Devices** before or after you move, as in check 2. **License already activated on this device** is not an error: the key was already active here.

## Check 4: Internet access and time

Activation contacts the UAVmatrix license server over HTTPS (port 443), so the device needs working internet at that moment.

1. On the device, run `curl -I https://uavmatrix.com`. You should get an HTTP response, not a timeout.
2. If you are on a cellular modem, check that it actually has internet: [Modem connected, no internet](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/modem-no-internet/).
3. Check the date with `date`. A device with a wrong clock can't open HTTPS connections. Boards without a real-time clock set the time from the internet after boot, so wait a minute after boot and try again.

## Check 5: Cannot connect to license service

This message means the web interface can't reach UAVcast-Pro's own background service, not the internet. Restart it and try again:

```bash
sudo systemctl restart uavcast-factory
sudo systemctl status uavcast-factory
```

If it doesn't stay **active (running)**, [collect the logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/) with **License Manager** selected.

## Check 6: Expired license

The license details show **License Status:** and **Expiration Date:**. An expired license must be renewed on [uavmatrix.com](https://uavmatrix.com/).

> **64-bit operating system**
>
> UAVcast-Pro v6 only runs on a 64-bit OS. If you got this far, the OS is fine; on a 32-bit OS the installer already stops with *No installation candidate*.

## Still failing?

[Download the logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/) with **License Manager** selected. They contain the response code from the license server, for example `code 550` for no free slots. Send them with the first and last four characters of your key to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)**.

Using Fleet Manager? A license that activates fine can still be refused at pairing. See [Pairing code invalid or expired](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/).

Related: [Activate your license](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/license-activation-failed/
