# 4G modem connected but no internet

> LTE modem shows signal and an operator but the drone has no internet? Check modem type, APN, SIM PIN and data, network priority and the default route.

The **Modem** page shows signal, an operator and maybe an IP address, yet the drone can't reach the internet: the VPN won't connect, the license can't be checked, and video and telemetry never reach the ground station over LTE.

| What you see | Likely cause | Start at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No Modem Connected | Linux does not see the modem, or it lacks power | [Check 1](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/modem-no-internet/#check-1) |
| Error that mentions a HiLink modem, or no Connect button for a USB stick | Wrong Modem type | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/modem-no-internet/#check-2) |
| Registered on the network, but no IPv4 address | Wrong APN, PIN, or no data on the SIM | [Check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/modem-no-internet/#check-3) |
| Modem has an IP address, internet still goes through Wi-Fi | Network priority favours Wi-Fi | [Check 4](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/modem-no-internet/#check-4) |
| Works at home, not in the field (or the reverse) | Roaming, coverage, or a home network on the modem subnet | [Check 5](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/modem-no-internet/#check-5) |

![UAVcast-Pro Modem page with Traditional (PPP) selected and the No Modem Connected panel](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/modem.webp)

*Modem page with Traditional (PPP) selected and no modem plugged in. With a modem connected, the right-hand card shows signal quality, state, operator and IPv4 information.*

## Check 1: Is the modem detected?

If the page says **No Modem Connected**:

1. Check that the modem's power light is on and it sits firmly in a USB port.
2. A modem can draw more current than a Raspberry Pi USB port supplies. Watch the dashboard's **Power supply** row. If it says **Voltage too low - use a stronger power supply**, fix the power first: [Undervoltage and throttling](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/undervoltage-and-throttling/).
3. On the Pi, run `lsusb` to see the modem, and `mmcli -L` to see whether ModemManager found it. A HiLink modem does not show in `mmcli`; it appears as a network interface in `ip addr` instead.

The modem appears on the page by itself once it is detected.

## Check 2: Pick the right modem type

There are two kinds of USB modems, and **Modem type** must match yours.

|  | **HiLink** | **Traditional (PPP)** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| How Linux sees it | A network adapter (the modem is a small router) | A modem managed by ModemManager |
| Who connects | The modem itself, automatically | UAVcast-Pro, with **Connect** and **Disconnect** buttons |
| Huawei example | E3372**h** | E3372**s** |

If you choose **Traditional (PPP)** for a HiLink modem, the log says *HiLink modem detected … Please change your modem type to 'HiLink' in settings.* Change **Modem type** and the error goes away.

## Check 3: APN, PIN and the SIM

For a **Traditional (PPP)** modem:

1. Leave **Access Point Name (Optional)** empty first. UAVcast-Pro then tries your network's default APN and known APNs for the SIM, and remembers the one that works (*Found a working … it will be used from now on* in the log).
2. If that fails, enter the APN your carrier gives for mobile data. Some carriers also need **Username (Optional)** and **Password (Optional)**.
3. If the SIM has a PIN, enter it in **PIN code (Optional)**, or disable the PIN by putting the SIM in a phone. **Unlock Required** under **Modem Information** shows whether the SIM is locked.
4. Put the SIM in a phone and check that mobile data works and the plan has data left.

For a **HiLink** modem, the APN is set in the modem's own web page, usually at `http://192.168.8.1`. Open it from the Pi, or plug the modem into a laptop.

> **UAVcast-Pro keeps trying**
>
> A Traditional modem connects at boot and reconnects after signal loss by itself. If a modem connects without getting an address, UAVcast-Pro switches it to raw-IP mode and tries again. Give it a minute after boot before you change settings.

## Check 4: Make the modem the default route

If the Pi is also on Wi-Fi or Ethernet, traffic goes out the interface with priority, not necessarily the modem.

1. Go to **Networks**.
2. Under **Network Priority**, choose **Modem Priority (Outdoor Mode)** before flight. **WiFi Priority (Indoor Mode)** saves cellular data at home but sends everything over Wi-Fi.
3. In **Network Interfaces**, check that the modem interface is marked **Default** and that **Default Gateway** shows *via* the modem interface.

![Networks page with Network Priority set to Auto and the interfaces table showing wlan0 as default](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/networks.webp)

*Networks page with Auto (System Default) active and Wi-Fi (wlan0) as the default route. Select Modem Priority (Outdoor Mode) here to route over the modem.*

Test from the Pi over the modem alone:

```bash
ping -c 3 -I wwan0 1.1.1.1   # Traditional modem (interface name may differ)
ip route                     # the first "default via" line is the route in use
```

## Check 5: Field-only problems

- **Roaming**: a SIM used abroad may need roaming enabled by the carrier. Check in a phone with the same SIM.
- **Coverage**: look at **Signal Quality** and **Technology**. Some IoT SIMs only work on certain bands or technologies.
- **Subnet clash**: HiLink modems hand out `192.168.8.x`. If your home or office network also uses `192.168.8.0/24`, routing breaks. Change the LAN or the modem's subnet.

## Still no internet?

[Download the logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/) with **Modem Manager** selected, add the output of `mmcli -m 0` and `ip route`, and send them to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)** with the modem model and carrier.

Related: [Cellular modem](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/cellular-modem/) · [Networks](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/networks/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/modem-no-internet/

# Web interface won't open

> Can't open UAVcast-Pro at http://device-ip after installing? Find the right address, check the uavcast-web service, the server port and port 80.

The installer finished, but `http://<device-ip>/` times out, refuses the connection or shows another program's page.

| What you see | Likely cause | Start at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Timeout, or the page never loads | Wrong address, or your computer is on another network | [Check 1](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/web-interface-wont-open/#check-1) |
| Connection refused | The web service is not running | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/web-interface-wont-open/#check-2) |
| Another web page, for example nginx or Apache | Something else uses port 80 | [Check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/web-interface-wont-open/#check-3) |
| Worked before, stopped after a settings change | The server port was changed | [Check 4](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/web-interface-wont-open/#check-4) |
| Loads, but every page jumps to Application | No active license yet | [Check 5](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/web-interface-wont-open/#check-5) |

## Check 1: Use the right address

The web interface runs on **port 80** by default, so the address is just `http://<device-ip>/`.

1. Find the device IP. The installer prints it at the end. On the device you can also run `hostname -I`.
2. On a Raspberry Pi with the default hostname, try `http://raspberrypi.local/`.
3. Use `http://`, not `https://`. The web interface does not serve HTTPS.
4. Make sure your computer is on the same network as the device, or on the same VPN. Over 4G you must use the drone's VPN address.

## Check 2: Is the web service running?

On the device, run:

```bash
sudo systemctl status uavcast-web
```

It should say **active (running)**. If not, start it and read why it stopped:

```bash
sudo systemctl restart uavcast-web
journalctl -u uavcast-web --since "1 hour ago"
```

The web interface needs the background services too. Check them the same way: `uavcast-factory`, `mavlink-manager`, `uavcast-camera` and `redis-server`. The full list is in [Services and files](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/services-and-files/).

## Check 3: Port 80 already in use

If another web server is installed on the device, it may hold port 80. Find out who listens:

```bash
sudo ss -ltnp | grep ':80 '
```

Stop and disable the other server (`sudo systemctl disable --now nginx`, for example), then restart `uavcast-web`.

## Check 4: The server port was changed

**Application → Settings → Server Port** moves the web interface to another port, and the address becomes `http://<device-ip>:<port>/`. If you don't remember the port, read it on the device:

```bash
grep SERVER_PORT /etc/systemd/system/uavcast-web.service
```

## Check 5: Every page goes to Application

That is expected until a license is active on the device. Activate it under **Application → License Manager**. If that fails, see [License won't activate](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/license-activation-failed/).

## Check 6: The installer did not finish

If `uavcast-web` doesn't exist (`Unit uavcast-web.service could not be found`), the installation stopped early. See [Installation fails](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/installation-fails/).

## Still no luck?

Send the output of `systemctl status uavcast-web` and `journalctl -u uavcast-web --since yesterday`, plus `/opt/uavcast-pro/installer.log`, to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)**.

Related: [Install UAVcast-Pro](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/installation/) · [Application settings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/application-settings/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/web-interface-wont-open/

# Installation fails

> Fix UAVcast-Pro installer errors like No installation candidate found or failed dependencies: check the 64-bit OS, internet, disk and installer log.

You ran `curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | sudo bash` and it stopped with an error, hung, or finished without a working web interface.

| What you see | Likely cause | Start at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No installation candidate for … found! | 32-bit OS or an unsupported architecture | [Check 1](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/installation-fails/#check-1) |
| Failed to update package lists, or Failed to install dependencies | No internet, or a broken apt setup | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/installation-fails/#check-2) |
| Hangs for a long time on a Pi Zero 2 W | Low memory and slow storage | [Check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/installation-fails/#check-3) |
| Service failed to start | A component could not start after install | [Check 4](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/installation-fails/#check-4) |

## Check 1: 64-bit operating system

UAVcast-Pro v6 needs a 64-bit OS: arm64 or amd64 (x86 PCs). On arm64, boards other than a Raspberry Pi (Jetson and other ARM boards) need UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3 or later; older installers stop with *Device is not a Raspberry Pi*.

```bash
dpkg --print-architecture   # must print arm64 or amd64
uname -m                    # aarch64 or x86_64
```

If you see `armhf`, `armv7l` or `i686`, you are on a 32-bit OS. Flash **Raspberry Pi OS (64-bit)** with Raspberry Pi Imager and install again. Supported systems are Raspberry Pi OS, Debian and Ubuntu; see [Supported hardware](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/supported-hardware/).

## Check 2: Internet and apt

The installer downloads UAVcast-Pro and system packages, and installs ZeroTier and Tailscale.

1. Check internet access: `curl -I https://install.uavmatrix.com`.
2. Run `sudo apt update` by hand and fix any errors it shows, for example a third-party repository with an expired key.
3. Run the installer again. It is safe to run it more than once.

## Check 3: Low-power boards

On a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W the installation takes much longer than on a Pi 4 or 5, and the installer shows a time estimate. Let it finish. Use a fast SD card and a stable power supply: an undervoltage reset during install leaves a half-finished installation.

## Check 4: Read the installer log

The installer writes everything to `/opt/uavcast-pro/installer.log`.

```bash
sudo tail -n 100 /opt/uavcast-pro/installer.log
```

Look at the last error lines. If the installer fails before it can create `/opt/uavcast-pro`, the log is in `/tmp/uavcast-installer.log`.

## Install a specific version

To list the versions available for your architecture, or to install one of them:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | bash -s -- -l          # list versions
curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | sudo bash -s -- -b 6.5.2  # install 6.5.2
```

## Still failing?

Send `/opt/uavcast-pro/installer.log`, the output of `cat /etc/os-release` and `dpkg --print-architecture`, and your board model to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)**.

Related: [Install UAVcast-Pro](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/installation/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/installation-fails/


---

# VPN connected but can't reach the drone

> Fleet Manager VPN, Tailscale or ZeroTier says connected but you can't ping the drone? Check authorization, the network or tailnet, internet and the GCS IP.

Both the drone and your laptop say they are on the VPN, but `ping` to the drone's VPN address times out, the web interface won't open over the VPN, or telemetry and video don't arrive.

| What you see | Likely cause | Start at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ZeroTier network shows ACCESS_DENIED, or no IP address | The drone is not authorized on the network | [Check 1](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/vpn-cant-reach-drone/#check-1) |
| Drone is fine, the laptop gets no address or the wrong one | The laptop joined another network or tailnet | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/vpn-cant-reach-drone/#check-2) |
| Tailscale worked for weeks, then stopped | The device key expired | [Check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/vpn-cant-reach-drone/#check-3) |
| VPN on the drone never connects in the field | The drone has no internet over the modem | [Check 4](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/vpn-cant-reach-drone/#check-4) |
| Ping works, but no telemetry or video | The ground station destination uses the wrong IP | [Check 5](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/vpn-cant-reach-drone/#check-5) |

## Check 1: Authorize the drone on the network

**ZeroTier:**

1. In UAVcast-Pro, open **Virtual Private Network**. Check that **Enable VPN** is **Yes**, **Services** is **ZeroTier**, and the **Network ID** is the one from your ZeroTier controller.
2. Look at your network under **Connected Networks**. If its status badge says **ACCESS_DENIED**, the drone joined but is not authorized.
3. In your ZeroTier controller, open the network and authorize the member with the drone's node ID.
4. Back in UAVcast-Pro, wait until the network shows status `OK` and an IP address. That is the address you use from the laptop.

On a private ZeroTier network, every device that joins (drone, laptop, tablet) must be authorized once in the controller before it gets an address. (UAVnet networks are private too; UAVnet is being retired, so move to the Fleet Manager VPN.)

**Tailscale:** the drone shows **Connected** with an **IPv4 Address** (100.x.y.z) when it is in. If it says **Not Connected**, use **Web Login → Generate Login URL**, or the **Auth Key** tab with a key from your Tailscale admin console.

## Check 2: Put the laptop on the same network

Both ends must be on the same ZeroTier network or the same tailnet.

- **ZeroTier**: on the laptop, join the same Network ID and authorize the laptop in your controller too. On Windows, check the ZeroTier tray icon; on Linux run `sudo zerotier-cli listnetworks`. The status must be `OK`.
- **Tailscale**: a Tailscale client is on one tailnet at a time. On the laptop, run `tailscale status`. The drone must be in the list. If not, the laptop is logged in to another account or tailnet.
- **Fleet Manager VPN**: if the drone was paired with Fleet Manager and VPN, it is on your organization's network, not your personal Tailscale. Connect the laptop with the command Fleet Manager gives under **Network** (`tailscale up --login-server=… --authkey=…`) and run it **on the laptop, never on the drone**. See [Connect a ground station](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/connect-gcs/).

> **Pairing can replace the drone's VPN**
>
> When you pair a drone in Fleet Manager with **Replace existing VPN with Fleet Manager network**, the drone leaves its current Tailscale network and joins the organization's network. Laptops on the old tailnet can no longer reach it.

## Check 3: Expired Tailscale key

Tailscale device keys expire. When the drone's key expires it drops off the tailnet until it logs in again. The **Expires** field on the **Virtual Private Network** page shows the date. In the Tailscale admin console you can turn off key expiry for the drone, so it doesn't drop off in the middle of a project.

## Check 4: The drone needs internet first

The VPN runs over the drone's own internet connection. If the modem has no internet, the VPN shows as disconnected or never gets an address. Fix the connection first: [Modem connected, no internet](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/modem-no-internet/).

## Check 5: Reachable, but no data

If `ping <drone-vpn-ip>` works:

- **Web interface**: open `http://<drone-vpn-ip>/`. The live preview also needs port 8889 to be reachable over the VPN.
- **Telemetry and video**: these are sent *from* the drone *to* the address in **Ground Control Stations → Destination IP or Host**. It must be the laptop's VPN address, not the drone's, and not the laptop's Wi-Fi address. Then see [No telemetry](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-telemetry-in-gcs/) or [No video](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-video-in-gcs/).
- **Slow, but working**: Tailscale shows the **Relay** in use. A relayed connection works but adds delay. Some cellular networks don't allow direct connections, so a relay may be the best you get on that carrier.

## Still unreachable?

[Download the logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/) with **VPN Manager** selected and send them to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)**, with the output of `zerotier-cli listnetworks` or `tailscale status` from both the drone and the laptop.

Related: [VPN settings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/connectivity/vpn/) · [Fleet Manager network](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/network/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/vpn-cant-reach-drone/


---

# RTK corrections not arriving

> NTRIP stuck on Connecting, no RTCM forwarded or no RTK Fixed? Check caster host, port, mountpoint, credentials, GGA upstream and the GPS receiver.

Under **Flight Controller → NTRIP / RTK** the status does not reach **Streaming corrections**, **RTCM messages forwarded** stays at zero, or corrections flow but the flight controller never gets past **3D fix** or **RTK Float**.

The chain has four links: internet → caster → UAVcast-Pro → flight controller → GPS receiver. Find the first one that breaks.

![NTRIP / RTK tab with the status panel, counters and caster response line, and the GPS quality card](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/flight-controller--ntrip.webp)

*Flight Controller → NTRIP / RTK on a unit without a caster configured: status Disabled, counters at zero and Caster response empty. Healthy is Streaming corrections, a 200 caster response and climbing counters.*

| What you see | Likely cause | Start at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Status Connecting or Error, no caster response | Wrong host or port, TLS mismatch, or no internet | [Check 1](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/rtk-corrections-not-arriving/#check-1) |
| Caster response 401 Unauthorized | Wrong username, password or mountpoint | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/rtk-corrections-not-arriving/#check-2) |
| Log says caster returned sourcetable | The mountpoint name is wrong | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/rtk-corrections-not-arriving/#check-2) |
| Connected, but no RTCM data, reconnects every few seconds | The caster needs a GGA position first | [Check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/rtk-corrections-not-arriving/#check-3) |
| RTCM forwarded, fix stays at 3D fix | Flight controller link down, or receiver not RTK-capable | [Check 4](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/rtk-corrections-not-arriving/#check-4) |
| RTK Float, never RTK Fixed | Sky view, distance to the base, or time | [Check 5](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/rtk-corrections-not-arriving/#check-5) |

## Check 1: Reach the caster

1. Check **Caster host** and **Port**. Most public casters use plain TCP on port `2101`.
2. **Use TLS (HTTPS)** must match the caster. Commercial casters (Trimble, Hexagon, Topcon and others) often need TLS, usually still on port 2101, sometimes 2102 or 443. Public casters normally don't use TLS.
3. Make sure the drone has internet. **Dashboard → Cellular** should be connected. If not, see [Modem connected, no internet](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/modem-no-internet/).
4. Some cellular plans block unusual outbound ports. If the caster offers port 443, try it.

## Check 2: Credentials and mountpoint

1. Press **Test connection**. **Caster accepted the credentials.** means username and password are right.
2. For rtk2go.com, use a real e-mail address as **Username** and leave **Password** empty.
3. Press **Browse mountpoints** and pick a mountpoint from the list instead of typing the name. Prefer one close to where you fly.

If the caster answers with its sourcetable instead of data, the NTRIP log says *caster returned sourcetable — check mountpoint*. The mountpoint name is wrong or no longer exists.

## Check 3: Send GGA upstream

VRS and nearest-mountpoint casters only send corrections after they know where you are. The **NMEA** column in the mountpoint browser says **Required** for those mountpoints.

1. Turn on **Send GGA upstream** (on by default). **Send interval (seconds)** defaults to 10.
2. **Position source**: **Live position from flight controller** is right in flight. Until the flight controller reports a GPS fix, UAVcast-Pro uses the **Fixed manual position**, so enter a latitude and longitude near you for bench tests.
3. Watch **Last GGA sent** update.

UAVcast-Pro reconnects by itself when the caster goes quiet, and the log shows *no data from caster for …s — reconnecting*. After a short internet drop, corrections resume within seconds.

## Check 4: From UAVcast-Pro to the receiver

Corrections reach the GPS through the flight controller link, as MAVLink `GPS_RTCM_DATA`.

1. The flight controller must be **Connected** on **Flight Controller → Connection**. If not, see [No MAVLink heartbeat](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/).
2. Look at the **GPS quality** card. **No RTK status from receiver** means the flight controller has never reported RTK status. The connected GPS is usually not RTK-capable: RTK needs a carrier-phase RTK receiver such as a u-blox F9P, Here3+ or Septentrio Mosaic. A standard M8N or M10 navigation module won't do RTK.
3. **Recent message types** should include the constellations your receiver uses (for example 1077 GPS, 1087 GLONASS, 1097 Galileo, 1127 BeiDou) and a base position message (1005 or 1006).

## Check 5: Float, but never Fixed

- Give the antenna open sky. Trees, buildings and the drone's own electronics cause multipath and noise.
- Wait. A cold start can take a minute or two even in good conditions.
- Pick a closer base. Accuracy and the chance of a fix drop with distance from the base station.
- **Last correction** in **GPS quality** should stay at a few seconds. If it grows, corrections are being lost on the link.

## Still not working?

[Download the logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/) with **NTRIP Client** selected and send them, with your caster provider and GPS model, to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)**. The full setup is in [Set up RTK with an NTRIP caster](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/rtk-ntrip-caster/).

Related: [NTRIP / RTK settings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/ntrip-rtk/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/rtk-corrections-not-arriving/


---

# Undervoltage and throttling

> UAVcast-Pro warns Voltage too low or Slowed down? Size the power supply for Pi, modem and camera, fix thin cables and cooling, and stop resets.

The dashboard's **Power supply** row shows a warning, the modem drops, the flight controller link resets, or the Pi reboots in flight. On a drone, an undersized power supply causes more strange faults than any software setting.

![Dashboard status card with the Power supply row under System, reading Stable](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/dashboard--status-card.webp)

*Dashboard → status card. The Power supply row is under System; here it reads Stable. Warnings replace that text, as listed below.*

| Power supply row | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Stable** | No undervoltage or throttling since boot |
| **Voltage too low - use a stronger power supply** | The supply voltage is below what the Pi needs right now |
| **Voltage dropped since start-up** | It happened earlier, for example when the modem connected or the motors spun up |
| **Slowed down (heat or power)** | The CPU is running slower to protect itself from heat or low voltage |

The readings come from the Raspberry Pi firmware, so they are only available on a Raspberry Pi.

## Check 1: Size the supply for everything on it

The Pi powers the modem and USB camera through its USB ports. A 4G modem draws its peak current when it connects and when the signal is weak.

1. Use a 5 V BEC or regulator rated well above the total current of the Pi, modem, camera and anything else on the same rail. The official Raspberry Pi power supply specs list what each model needs.
2. Never power the Pi from the flight controller's TELEM or USB port.
3. If the modem draws more than the Pi can pass through, power the modem from the regulator directly, through a powered USB hub or a USB cable with separate power.

## Check 2: Cables and connectors

Thin or long cables lose voltage under load. Use short, thick power leads and a good USB cable for the modem. A cable that is fine for a phone charger can still cause undervoltage at peak current.

## Check 3: Heat

**Temperature** under **System Information** shows the CPU temperature. A Pi that runs video encoding inside a closed airframe in the sun gets hot. Add a heat sink or a small fan, and give the enclosure airflow. A Pi 5 needs active cooling for continuous encoding.

## Check 4: Check after the fix

**Voltage dropped since start-up** stays until the next boot. Reboot, run a typical mission on the bench (modem connected, camera streaming), and confirm the row stays **Stable**.

## Still seeing warnings?

The log download includes power and USB events from the kernel in `diagnostics.txt`. [Download the logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/) and send them to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)** with a photo of your power wiring.

Related: [Hardware requirements](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/hardware-requirements/) · [Dashboard](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/dashboard/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/undervoltage-and-throttling/


---

# Drone shows Offline in Fleet Manager

> Paired UAV shows Offline or Re-pair required in Fleet Manager? Check the drone's internet, outbound port 8883, UAVcast-Pro Fleet Management and the license.

The UAV is paired, but Fleet Manager shows it as **Offline** (grey on the fleet map), its telemetry is frozen, or it carries a **Re-pair required** badge.

Fleet Manager marks a UAV offline when it has heard nothing from it for 20 seconds. The drone talks to Fleet Manager over an encrypted MQTT connection, on its own internet connection.

| What you see | Likely cause | Start at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Offline, and UAVcast-Pro Fleet Management says Disconnected | The drone has no internet, or port 8883 is blocked | [Check 1](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/drone-offline-fleet-manager/#check-1) |
| Re-pair required badge, or This UAV must be re-paired | The drone has an old certificate | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/drone-offline-fleet-manager/#check-2) |
| Offline right after you reinstalled or reset UAVcast-Pro | The pairing was removed on the drone | [Check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/drone-offline-fleet-manager/#check-3) |
| Online, but no position or battery | Flight controller not connected to UAVcast-Pro | [Check 4](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/drone-offline-fleet-manager/#check-4) |

## Check 1: The drone's connection to Fleet Manager

1. Open UAVcast-Pro on the drone and go to **Fleet Management**. **Fleet Connection** shows **Connected** or **Disconnected**, and **Last Connected**.
2. If it is **Disconnected**, check that the drone has internet: the dashboard's **Cellular** row, or `curl -I https://fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com` on the device. Fix the link first with [Modem connected, no internet](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/modem-no-internet/).
3. The drone must be able to open an **outbound TCP connection on port 8883** (MQTT over TLS). Some company networks, public Wi-Fi and a few IoT SIM plans only allow web ports. Try another network or ask the provider to open 8883.
4. Check the date and time on the device with `date`. The connection uses certificates, which fail on a device with a wrong clock.
5. Make sure the license on the drone is still active (**Application → License Manager**).

## Check 2: Re-pair required

Fleet Manager changed how drones connect, and UAVs paired before that change must be paired once more. Nothing is lost: the UAV keeps its name and history, and you don't need to remove it in Fleet Manager.

1. In UAVcast-Pro on the drone, open **Fleet Management** and press **Disconnect from Fleet**, then confirm.
2. Press **Connect to Fleet Manager**. An 8-digit **Pairing Code** appears with a countdown.
3. In Fleet Manager, go to **Fleet → Pair Device**, choose the organization and enter the code.

## Check 3: The drone lost its pairing

A reinstall with a database reset, **Reset Database** or **Disconnect from Fleet** removes the pairing on the drone, so it stops reporting. Pair it again as in check 2. Pairing into the same organization reuses the existing UAV entry.

## Check 4: Online, but no telemetry

Position, battery and flight mode come from the flight controller. If the UAV is online but those fields are empty, UAVcast-Pro can't hear the flight controller: see [No MAVLink heartbeat](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/).

## Still offline?

[Download the logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/) from the drone with **All Logs** selected and send them to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)** with the UAV name and organization. More Fleet Manager problems are covered in [Fleet Manager troubleshooting](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/troubleshooting/).

Related: [Fleet Manager pairing in UAVcast-Pro](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/fleet-pairing/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/drone-offline-fleet-manager/


---

# Pairing code invalid or expired

> Fix Invalid pairing code, This pairing code has expired and License is not owned by any member of this organization when pairing a UAV with Fleet Manager.

You entered the code from UAVcast-Pro in Fleet Manager's **Pair Device** wizard, and it was refused.

Pairing works in this direction: **UAVcast-Pro shows the code, you type it into Fleet Manager**. The code has 8 digits and is valid for 5 minutes.

![Fleet Manager Pair UAV wizard with the error toast This pairing code has expired](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/fleet-manager/pair-device--code-expired.webp)

*Fleet Manager refusing a code: the error appears as a toast on the Pairing Code step, here This pairing code has expired.*

| Error in Fleet Manager | Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Pairing code must be 8 digits** / **Please enter a valid 8-digit code** | Too few digits, or letters | [Check 1](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/#check-1) |
| **Invalid pairing code** | A typo, or a code that never existed | [Check 1](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/#check-1) |
| **This pairing code has expired** | More than 5 minutes passed | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/#check-2) |
| **This pairing code has already been used** | The code was used once | [Check 2](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/#check-2) |
| **License is not owned by any member of this organization** | The drone's license belongs to an account outside the org | [Check 3](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/#check-3) |
| **Invalid license key** / **License has expired** / **License has been refunded** | The drone's license is not valid in the store | [Check 4](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/#check-4) |
| **This UAV is already paired to an organization** | Paired to another organization | [Check 5](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/#check-5) |
| **Too many attempts. Please wait a minute and try again.** | Rate limit after repeated tries | Wait one minute |

## Check 1: Type the current code

1. In UAVcast-Pro, go to **Fleet Management** and press **Connect to Fleet Manager**.
2. Copy the 8 digits shown under **Pairing Code**.
3. In Fleet Manager, go to **Fleet → Pair Device**, choose the organization and enter the code under **Enter Pairing Code**.

## Check 2: Get a fresh code

A code is valid for 5 minutes and works once. When **Expires in** reaches zero, press **Connect to Fleet Manager** again in UAVcast-Pro for a new code. If UAVcast-Pro can't get a code at all, it shows *Unable to connect to Fleet Manager. Please check your internet connection.*: fix the drone's internet first.

## Check 3: License owned by someone outside the organization

Fleet Manager only accepts a drone whose UAVcast-Pro license was bought by a member of the organization you pair into. The match is made on the e-mail address of the store account that owns the license.

Fix it one of these ways:

- Invite the account that bought the license to the organization (**Team**), then pair again.
- Pair into an organization where the license owner is a member.
- If the license was bought with another e-mail address of yours, ask **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)** to add that address as a license e-mail on your Fleet Manager user.

See [Licenses in Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/licenses/).

## Check 4: License not valid

Open **Application → License Manager** on the drone and check **License Status**. An expired or refunded license must be renewed on [uavmatrix.com](https://uavmatrix.com/). If UAVcast-Pro itself has no active license, it can't request a code (*No valid license found. Please activate your license first.*): see [License won't activate](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/license-activation-failed/).

## Check 5: Already paired elsewhere

A UAV belongs to one organization. To move it, remove it from the old organization first. Re-pairing into the same organization is allowed and keeps the UAV's history. See [Remove or transfer a UAV](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/fleet/remove-or-transfer/).

## Still refused?

Send the exact error text, the UAV hostname and the organization name to **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)**.

Related: [Fleet Manager pairing in UAVcast-Pro](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/fleet-pairing/) · [Pair your first UAV](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/


---

# Collect logs for support

> Download the UAVcast-Pro log archive with diagnostics.txt from Application, Logging, or over SSH, and send it to UAVmatrix support with the right details.

One log download answers most of the questions support would otherwise ask. Each archive includes the service logs you choose plus a `diagnostics.txt` snapshot: version, OS and board, settings, the generated telemetry router config, serial devices and who holds them, and power and USB events from the kernel. Passwords, keys and tokens are never included.

## Download from the web interface

1. Go to **Application** and scroll to **Logging**.
2. In the first list, keep **All Logs**, or pick the service that matches the problem (see the table).
3. In the second list, pick a time range that covers the problem. The default is **Last 2 hours**.
4. Press **Download**. Your browser saves a `.zip` file.

![Application page Logging card with the log list set to All Logs, the time range set to Last 2 hours and the Download button](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/img/screenshots/uavcast-pro/application--logging.webp)

*Application → Logging with All Logs and Last 2 hours selected.*

| Problem | Pick in the log list |
| --- | --- |
| Flight controller link, no heartbeat, no telemetry | **Mavlink Manager** |
| Camera, video, preview | **Camera Server** |
| Modem, cellular | **Modem Manager** |
| ZeroTier, Tailscale | **VPN Manager** |
| RTK, NTRIP | **NTRIP Client** |
| License | **License Manager** |
| Dynamic DNS | **DNS Manager** |
| Installation | **Application Installer** |
| Not sure | **All Logs** |

Only admins can download logs. **Prune All Logs** deletes every log file and cannot be undone, so download first.

## From the command line

If the web interface does not open, collect the logs over SSH:

```bash
sudo tar czf ~/uavcast-logs.tar.gz /opt/uavcast-pro/logs /opt/uavcast-pro/installer.log
journalctl -u uavcast-web -u uavcast-factory -u mavlink-manager -u uavcast-camera --since "2 hours ago" > ~/uavcast-journal.txt
```

Copy both files to your computer, for example with `scp`.

## Send them to support

E-mail **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)** and include:

- the log archive,
- your UAVcast-Pro version (shown at the bottom of the sidebar),
- the board, OS, flight controller, camera and modem you use,
- what you expected, what happened, and what you have already tried from these pages.

You can also ask in the [UAVmatrix Discord](https://discord.gg/xwqMTXh). Don't post log files publicly: they contain IP addresses and device names.

Related: [Application settings](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/application-settings/)

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/


---

# Frequently asked questions

> Short answers about UAVcast-Pro hardware, LTE modems, ground stations, ports, offline use, licensing, updates, recording and Fleet Manager pairing.

## Hardware and setup

### Do I need an LTE modem?

No. UAVcast-Pro works over any IP connection: 4G/LTE, Wi-Fi or Ethernet. A modem is what lets you fly beyond Wi-Fi range. Many operators test on Wi-Fi and switch to the modem before flight with **Networks → Network Priority → Modem Priority (Outdoor Mode)**.

### Which computers can run UAVcast-Pro?

Any 64-bit Linux board or PC on arm64 or amd64 running Raspberry Pi OS, Debian or Ubuntu: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W, 3, 4 and 5, NVIDIA Jetson, Orange Pi and x86 mini PCs. A Raspberry Pi 4 or 5 is the comfortable choice for video. See [Supported hardware](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/supported-hardware/).

### Which flight controllers are supported?

Any flight controller that speaks MAVLink over USB or a TELEM port: ArduPilot (Copter, Plane, Rover, VTOL and the other vehicle types) and PX4, on Pixhawk and Cube family boards, Matek and similar. Telemetry, video and routing to ground stations work with any of them. The flight-mode buttons in the Flight Map and in Fleet Manager use ArduPilot's mode names; with PX4, change modes from your ground station.

### Can I connect over the flight controller's USB port?

Yes, and it is the simplest option: plug it in and leave **Port** on **Automatic**. Use a short cable that carries data. See [No MAVLink heartbeat](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/no-mavlink-heartbeat/) if it isn't found.

## Ground stations and network

### Which ground stations work?

Any software that takes MAVLink over UDP, including QGroundControl, Mission Planner and MAVProxy. Video is H.264 over RTP/UDP, which QGroundControl and Mission Planner play directly. GStreamer and VLC work too: see [Ground stations & video](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/).

### Can several ground stations watch at the same time?

Yes. Add one destination per computer under **Ground Control Stations**, each with its own switches for video and telemetry. Use **Read Only** for stations that should only watch. See [Stream to multiple ground stations](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/multiple-ground-stations/).

### Which ports does UAVcast-Pro use?

By default telemetry goes to UDP **14550** and video to UDP **5600** on each ground station; a second camera uses the video port + 1, and audio the video port + 2. The web interface is on port **80**. The full list is in [Ports and protocols](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/ports-and-protocols/).

### Do I need port forwarding on my router?

No. Over 4G, put the drone and the ground station on the same VPN: the Fleet Manager VPN (included with your license), or your own Tailscale or ZeroTier network. The drone sends telemetry and video to the ground station's VPN address. See [Fly beyond visual range over 4G](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/bvlos-4g/).

### Can I still connect over TCP 5760?

No. Since v6.5.0, TCP 5760 is closed so only the ground stations you add get data. Add your computer as a destination and use UDP.

### Does it work without internet?

Yes. The flight controller link, telemetry and video start at power-on without waiting for internet, so a local Wi-Fi network or radio link works. Activating the license needs internet once. After that, a failed license check because of a lost connection does not disable the device.

## License and account

> You need a UAVcast-Pro license to activate the drone. Buy one in the UAVmatrix store.
>
> [Buy UAVcast-Pro](https://uavmatrix.com/checkout) · [See plans and pricing](https://uavmatrix.com/products)

### My license won't activate. What now?

See [License won't activate](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/license-activation-failed/). The usual causes are a mistyped key, no free device slot, or no internet on the device.

### What happens when my license expires?

UAVcast-Pro is locked: the web interface only opens **Application**, and telemetry, video and the other services stop until you renew. Renew in the store before the expiry date, then validate the key on the drone. See [When a license expires](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/license-activation/#when-a-license-expires).

### Is Fleet Manager included with my license?

Yes. Fleet Manager, including its VPN, is included with your UAVcast-Pro license at no extra cost.

### I replaced the SD card. Do I need a new license?

No, but the device counts as new and takes a slot. Unregister the old entry under **Application → License Manager → Activated Devices**.

### Is Fleet Manager a separate product?

Fleet Manager is UAVmatrix's web dashboard for managing many drones at [fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com](https://fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com/). It is included with your UAVcast-Pro license. You sign in with your uavmatrix.com account, and each drone you pair needs an active UAVcast-Pro license owned by a member of your organization. See [Fleet Manager](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/).

### How do I pair a drone with Fleet Manager?

In UAVcast-Pro, open **Fleet Management** and press **Connect to Fleet Manager**. Enter the 8-digit code in Fleet Manager under **Fleet → Pair Device** within 5 minutes. See [Pair your first UAV](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/fleet-manager/pair-uav/) and, if it fails, [Pairing code invalid or expired](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/pairing-code-invalid/).

## Updates and data

### How do I update UAVcast-Pro?

Go to **Application → Update Application**, pick a version in **Select version to update** and press **Update Now**. If the card shows **Pending Restart**, press **Restart Now**. You can also run the installer again.

### Can I import settings from v4 or v5?

No. v6 uses a new database, so set it up again after a fresh install. Within v6, use **Application → Database → Backup Database** and **Restore Database** to move settings between installs.

### Can UAVcast-Pro record video?

Yes, since v6.5.1. It records camera 1 and 2 from the flight map, or automatically while the drone is armed, together with a telemetry log. See [Record flights and review them](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/guides/recording-flight-review/).

### Where does UAVcast-Pro keep its files?

Under `/opt/uavcast-pro`: the database `uavcast.db`, `logs/`, `recordings/` and `missions/`. See [Services and files](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/services-and-files/).

### I forgot the admin password.

There is no password reset in the web interface. Another admin can delete your user under **Users** and create it again. If you were the only admin, recovery isn't self-service: contact **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)** with the details listed in [Forgot the admin password](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/users/#forgot-the-admin-password).

### Where do I get help?

Collect the logs as described in [Collect logs for support](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/) and e-mail **[support@uavmatrix.com](mailto:support@uavmatrix.com)**, or ask in the [UAVmatrix Discord](https://discord.gg/xwqMTXh).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/faq/

# Ports and protocols

> Every port UAVcast-Pro and Fleet Manager use: MAVLink UDP 14550, video UDP 5600, camera 2 and audio, web, preview, RTSP, NTRIP and MQTT 8883.

Use this page to set up firewalls on the ground station, on the drone's network and in company networks. Defaults are shown; where a port can be changed, the setting is named.

## Ground station: incoming traffic

UAVcast-Pro **sends** telemetry and video to each ground station. The ground station only needs to accept incoming UDP; nothing has to listen on the drone for this.

| Port (default) | Protocol | What | Setting |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **14550** | UDP | MAVLink telemetry, both directions once the GCS answers | **Ground Control Stations → Telemetry Port** |
| **5600** | UDP | Video: H.264 in RTP, payload type 96 | **Video Port** |
| **Video Port + 1** (5601) | UDP | Camera 2 video when **Dual stream** is on | **Video Port (Camera 2)** (empty = Video Port + 1) |
| **Video Port + 2** (5602) | UDP | Audio: Opus in RTP, payload type 97, when **Send audio to ground stations** is on | Follows **Video Port** |

> **TCP 5760 is closed**
>
> Since v6.5.0 the telemetry router does not listen on TCP 5760. Ground stations connect over UDP to the destinations you add.

**With Fleet Manager stream bindings**, the first drone bound to a ground station uses 5600/14550, and each additional drone gets its own block of ports: a video port with room for camera 2 and audio after it, and a telemetry port. Read the ports on each binding.

## Drone: services you connect to

| Port | Protocol | What | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **80** | TCP (HTTP) | Web interface | Change in **Application → Settings → Server Port** (80 or higher). |
| **8889** | TCP (HTTP) | Live preview in the browser (WebRTC) | Used by **Camera → Live Preview** and the Flight Map video windows. |
| 8189 | UDP | WebRTC media for the live preview | Media server default. |
| **9996** | TCP (HTTP) | Playback of recordings | Used by the recordings library and flight review player. |
| **8554** | TCP (RTSP) | RTSP copy of the camera stream (`/camera`, `/camera2`) | Available while the live preview or recording is on. |
| 8888 | TCP (HTTP) | HLS copy of the camera stream | Not used by the web interface. |
| HTTP injector | TCP (HTTP) | `http://<drone>/api/inject/<token>` | Served on the web interface port. See [Injectors](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/injectors/). |
| UDP injector | UDP | Your choice (14600 is a safe default) | Set per injector in **Flight Controller → Injectors**. |

Over a VPN, these ports must be reachable on the drone's VPN address. No port forwarding is needed on the cellular side.

## Drone: outgoing traffic

The drone opens these connections itself. Networks that only allow web traffic will block some of them.

| Destination | Port | Protocol | What |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ground stations | 14550, 5600 (+1, +2) | UDP | Telemetry, video, audio |
| `uavmatrix.com` | 443 | HTTPS | License activation and periodic checks |
| `install.uavmatrix.com` | 443 | HTTPS | Installer and updates |
| `fleet-manager.uavmatrix.com` | 443 | HTTPS | Fleet Manager pairing |
| Fleet Manager broker | **8883** | MQTT over TLS (client certificates) | Fleet Manager status, telemetry and commands |
| `vpn-connect.uavmatrix.com` | 443 | HTTPS | Fleet Manager VPN login server |
| Your NTRIP caster | 2101 (or as set) | TCP, optional TLS | RTCM corrections |
| ZeroTier / Tailscale | ZeroTier 9993, Tailscale 41641 (and 443 fallback) | UDP | VPN tunnels |
| Your DNS provider | 443 | HTTPS | Dynamic DNS updates |

## Inside the drone (local only)

These ports are used between UAVcast-Pro's own services and don't need firewall rules:

| Port | What |
| --- | --- |
| 6379 | Redis, internal message bus |
| 12550, 12551 | Telemetry router to the UAVcast-Pro app and to the NTRIP client |
| 8090 | Injector HTTP listener (reached through `/api/inject/…` on port 80) |
| 9997 | Media server API |
| 5000 | UAVcast-Pro background service API, used by the web interface |

## Firewall rules for the ground station

**Windows**

```powershell
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "MAVLink Telemetry" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 14550 -Action Allow
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "UAV Video" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 5600-5602 -Action Allow
```

**Linux (UFW)**

```bash
sudo ufw allow 14550/udp comment 'MAVLink Telemetry'
sudo ufw allow 5600:5602/udp comment 'UAV Video and audio'
```

Add more ports if you use other telemetry or video ports, or several drones through Fleet Manager stream bindings.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/ports-and-protocols/

# Settings reference

> Every UAVcast-Pro setting on one page with its exact label, default and range: flight controller, NTRIP, ground stations, camera, recording, modem, VPN.

Every setting in the UAVcast-Pro web interface, grouped by page, with the label exactly as the app shows it and the default on a fresh install. Pages that change settings live apply them straight away unless noted. The feature pages explain each area in depth; this page is for looking things up.

## Flight Controller → Connection

| Setting | Default | Values and notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Link enabled** | On | Turns the flight controller link on or off. |
| **Link type** | **USB** | **USB** (the flight controller's own USB port) or **UART / Serial** (TELEM port on GPIO pins or a USB-serial cable). |
| **Port** | **Automatic** | Automatic finds the flight controller and follows it if the device number changes. **Custom path…** takes a device such as `/dev/ttyAMA0`. |
| **Baud rate** | **Automatic** | Must match `SERIALx_BAUD` on the flight controller. Automatic tries 57600, 115200, 921600, 1500000, 460800, 230400 and 500000. Not used for USB. |

Buttons: **Auto-detect** (scan all ports and speeds and save the result), **Connect**, **Restart link**, **Stop**. Changes apply immediately, without a restart.

## Flight Controller → NTRIP / RTK

| Setting | Default | Values and notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Enable NTRIP client** | Off |  |
| **Caster host** | empty | Host name of the NTRIP caster. |
| **Port** | `2101` | Some TLS casters use 2102 or 443. |
| **Mountpoint** | empty | Pick with **Browse mountpoints**. |
| **Use TLS (HTTPS)** | Off | For casters that require TLS. |
| **Username** / **Password** | empty | rtk2go.com: e-mail address as username, no password. |
| **Send GGA upstream** | On | Needed by VRS and nearest-mountpoint casters. |
| **Send interval (seconds)** | `10` |  |
| **Position source** | **Live position from flight controller** | Or **Fixed manual position** (**Latitude**, **Longitude**, **Altitude (m)**), also used as fallback before the first GPS fix. |

## Flight Controller → Injectors

| Setting | Default | Values and notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Input type** |  | **HTTP**, **UDP** or **Serial**. Can't be changed after creation. |
| **MAVLink sysid** | `1` | Same as the flight controller. |
| **MAVLink compid** | `194` | User payload. |
| **Name prefix** | empty | Up to 8 ASCII characters, prepended to every signal name. |
| **Rate limit (Hz per signal)** |  | Maximum samples per second per signal name. |
| **Protocol** (UDP, Serial) |  | **Key=Value (line-delimited)** or **JSON** (`{name, value}`). |
| **Port** / **Bind address** (UDP) |  | Pick an unused port, for example 14600. `0.0.0.0` = all interfaces, `127.0.0.1` = local only. |
| **Device path** / **Baud rate** (Serial) |  | For example `/dev/ttyUSB0`; the baud rate must match the sender. |

## Ground Control Stations

One card per destination.

| Setting | Default on a new destination | Values and notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Name** | empty | Up to 50 characters. |
| **Destination IP or Host** | empty | An IPv4 address. Required before video or telemetry can be switched on. |
| **Telemetry Port** | `14550` | 1–65535. |
| **Video Port** | `5600` | 1–65535. |
| **Video Port (Camera 2)** | empty (= Video Port + 1) | Only shown when **Dual stream** is on. |
| **Enable Endpoint** | On | Off stops everything to this destination: telemetry, video and audio. |
| **Enable Video** | **Off** |  |
| **Enable Telemetry** | **Off** |  |
| **Read Only** | Off | The ground station receives telemetry but can't change anything on the vehicle. This applies from UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3; on earlier versions, Read Only does not block parameter writes. |

## Camera → Camera settings

| Setting | Default | Values and notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Enable Camera?** | Yes |  |
| **Select Camera** | Raspberry Pi camera | Detected CSI and USB cameras. |
| **Resolution** | 640×480 | Only sizes the camera supports are offered. |
| **Select FPS** | **Auto** | The camera negotiates. |
| **Bitrate:** | `0` (auto) | 0–10000 kbps. |
| **Stream Recovery Rate** | **Auto** | Keyframe interval. Auto = one keyframe per second. Faster levels recover sooner from packet loss and use more bandwidth. |
| **Rotation:** / **Flip Settings** | 0°, no flip | **Horizontal Flip**, **Vertical Flip**. |
| **Enable Live Preview?** | Yes | Preview on this page and in the Flight Map. |
| **Custom Pipeline** | test pipeline | Overrides the Ground Control Stations destinations. Omit the `gst-launch-1.0` prefix. |
| **Enable RC channel camera switching** | Off |  |
| **RC Channel** | 7 | PWM < 1500 = Camera 1, PWM > 1500 = Camera 2. |
| **Match Camera 1 Resolution** | Off | Camera 2 captures at camera 1's resolution. |
| **Dual stream** | Off | Streams both cameras at once. |
| **Audio** | Off | Opus audio in the preview. |
| **Audio device** | **Auto (camera microphone if present)** | Or a capture device, or **Test tone (no microphone needed)**. |
| **Bitrate** (audio) | 64 kbps |  |
| **Send audio to ground stations** | Off | RTP/Opus to each video destination on Video Port + 2. |

## Camera → Recordings → Settings

| Setting | Default | Values and notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Storage location** | **Internal storage** | A USB drive or SSD, or **Or another folder**. |
| **Keep free** | 2 GB | 0.5–1000 GB. |
| **Delete oldest recordings when space runs low** | On | Off = recording stops when the disk is full. |
| **Delete recordings older than** | 0 days | 0 keeps them until the space is needed. |
| **Record automatically when armed** | On |  |
| **Record camera 1** / **Record camera 2** | On / On | Camera 2 only with dual stream. |
| **File length** | 1 min | 1–30 minutes per file. |
| **Record telemetry** | **While armed** | **Always while connected** or **Off**. |

## Modem

| Setting | Default | Values and notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Enable cellular Modem?** | Yes |  |
| **Modem type** | **Traditional (PPP)** | Or **HiLink**. |
| **Access Point Name (Optional)** | empty (**Automatic**) | Leave empty to detect it automatically. |
| **Username (Optional)** / **Password (Optional)** | empty | Most carriers need neither. |
| **PIN code (Optional)** | empty | SIM PIN, unless PIN is disabled. |

## Virtual Private Network

| Setting | Default | Values and notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Enable VPN** | No |  |
| **Services** | **ZeroTier** | **ZeroTier** or **Tailscale**. |
| **Network ID** (ZeroTier) | empty | From your own ZeroTier controller. |
| **Auth Key** / **Hostname (Optional)** (Tailscale) | empty | Or log in with **Web Login**, or the **Fleet Manager** tab after pairing. |

## Dynamic DNS

| Setting | Default | Values and notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Enable Dynamic DNS?** | No |  |
| **DNS System** | `noip` | `generic` (with **DNS URL**), `noip`, `dyndns`, `duck`. |
| Username, **Password**, **Alias** | empty | From your DNS provider. |

## Networks

| Setting | Default | Values and notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Network Priority** | system routing | **WiFi Priority (Indoor Mode)**, **Modem Priority (Outdoor Mode)** or **Auto (System Default)**. |

## Fleet Management

| Setting | Default | Values and notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Device Name** | empty | Shown in Fleet Manager. Without it, the hostname is used. |

## Users

| Setting | Values and notes |
| --- | --- |
| **Role** | **Admin - Full access** or **Read Only - View only**. The first user must be an admin. |

## Application

| Setting | Default | Values and notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Server Port** | `80` | 80 or higher. **Submit and restart server** applies it; the address becomes `http://<device>:<port>/`. |
| **Language** | Browser language | English, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Turkish, Russian, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional). |
| **Dark Theme** |  |  |
| **Logging**: log list / time range | **All Logs** / **Last 2 hours** | See [Collect logs](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/troubleshooting/collect-logs/). |

**Database** offers **Backup Database**, **Restore Database** (a `.db` file) and **Reset Database**, which deletes all settings.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/settings/
