# Supported hardware

> Boards, operating systems, flight controllers, cameras, LTE modems and RTK receivers that work with UAVcast-Pro v6: Raspberry Pi, Jetson and other arm64 boards, and x86 PCs.

UAVcast-Pro v6 runs on any 64-bit Linux computer that runs Raspberry Pi OS, Debian or Ubuntu, on **arm64** or **amd64** (arm64 boards other than a Raspberry Pi from UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3). The tables below list what is detected and tested. For power supplies, wiring and buying advice, see [Hardware requirements](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/get-started/hardware-requirements/).

## Companion computers

| Board | Architecture | Serial port for TELEM | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Raspberry Pi 5 | arm64 | GPIO UART (`uart0`) | Best video performance. Needs active cooling for continuous encoding. |
| Raspberry Pi 4 | arm64 | GPIO UART | Recommended all-round choice. |
| Raspberry Pi 3 | arm64 | GPIO UART | Fine for telemetry and one camera at moderate settings. |
| Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W | arm64 | GPIO UART | Works, but slow to install and limited for video. One camera, low resolution. |
| Raspberry Pi Compute Module | arm64 | Depends on carrier board | Installer support fixed in v6.3.1. |
| NVIDIA Jetson (Nano, Orin Nano, Xavier NX, AGX, TX2) | arm64 | `ttyTHS*` on the 40-pin header | USB cameras. Jetson CSI cameras aren't handled by the camera server; they need a hand-written **Custom Pipeline**. |
| Orange Pi (Zero, Zero 2, 3, 4, 5, Plus) | arm64 | `ttyS*`, model dependent | USB cameras. The UART may need enabling in the device tree. |
| Banana Pi and other arm64 boards | arm64 | Model dependent | USB cameras. |
| x86 mini PC, Intel NUC, laptop | amd64 | USB-serial adapter | USB cameras. |

> **Non-Raspberry Pi arm64 boards**
>
> Jetson, Orange Pi, Banana Pi and other arm64 boards that aren't a Raspberry Pi need UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3 or later. Older installers stop on them with *Device is not a Raspberry Pi*.

**Raspberry Pi only:** CSI cameras (rpicam/libcamera) need a Raspberry Pi, and on a Pi the installer enables the UART, removes the serial console and, on Pi 3/4/Zero 2 W, disables Bluetooth so the full UART is free.

## Operating systems

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| Raspberry Pi OS (64-bit) | Recommended on Raspberry Pi. Needed for CSI cameras. |
| Debian (64-bit) | Supported. |
| Ubuntu (64-bit), including Ubuntu for Raspberry Pi | Supported. CSI cameras on a Pi don't work on Ubuntu, because the Raspberry Pi camera stack isn't packaged; USB cameras do. |
| Any 32-bit OS | **Not supported.** The installer stops with *No installation candidate*. |

## Flight controllers

UAVcast-Pro v6 works with any MAVLink flight controller over USB or a TELEM port: ArduPilot (Copter, Plane, Rover, VTOL and other vehicle types) and PX4, on Pixhawk and Cube family boards, Matek, Holybro, CUAV and others. Flight-mode names and mode buttons in the Flight Map and Fleet Manager follow ArduPilot; with PX4, change modes from your ground station.

## Cameras

| Type | Examples | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Raspberry Pi CSI | Camera Module 2 and 3, HQ Camera, other libcamera sensors (imx219, imx708 …) | Raspberry Pi OS or Debian. Two CSI cameras on boards with two connectors (Pi 5, Compute Module). |
| USB (UVC) | Logitech C920, C615 and most UVC webcams | Any OS. |
| Other sources | IP cameras, HDMI capture | Through a **Custom Pipeline**. |

Up to two cameras, switched or streamed at the same time. Audio from a USB microphone or a camera's built-in microphone.

## LTE / 4G modems

| Type | How it works | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **HiLink** | The modem is a small router and appears as a network adapter (`cdc_ether`, `huawei_cdc_ncm`, `rndis_host` drivers) | Huawei E3372h, E8372h |
| **Traditional (PPP)** | Managed by ModemManager; UAVcast-Pro connects it, picks the APN and reconnects | Huawei E3372s, Quectel and Sierra Wireless modules on USB carriers |

Traditional modems must be supported by ModemManager: see the [ModemManager supported devices list](https://www.freedesktop.org/wiki/Software/ModemManager/SupportedDevices/). Pick a model whose bands match your carrier.

## RTK GPS receivers

NTRIP corrections need an RTK-capable (carrier-phase) receiver on the flight controller, for example u-blox ZED-F9P based modules, CubePilot Here3+ or Septentrio Mosaic. Standard navigation modules such as M8N, M9N or M10 can't use RTK corrections.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/supported-hardware/


---

# Services, files and installer options

> The systemd services UAVcast-Pro installs, where it keeps its database, logs and recordings, installer options for versions, and handy SSH commands.

For when you work on the device over SSH: which services make up UAVcast-Pro, where its files live, and how to install a particular version.

## Services

UAVcast-Pro runs as a set of systemd services. Each restarts itself if it fails.

| Service | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `uavcast-web` | The web interface (Node.js). Listens on port 80 unless you changed **Server Port**. |
| `uavcast-factory` | Background API: license, modem, VPN, network, logs, recording storage and the Fleet Manager connection. |
| `mavlink-manager` | Flight controller link and telemetry router to the ground stations. Starts without waiting for internet. |
| `uavcast-camera` | Camera capture, H.264 encoding and the UDP video stream. Starts without waiting for internet. |
| `mediamtx` | Media server for the browser preview, RTSP and recordings. |
| `uavcast-ntrip` | NTRIP client for RTK corrections. |
| `uavcast-dns` | Dynamic DNS updater. |
| `redis-server` | Internal message bus that the other services depend on. |
| `zerotier-one`, `tailscaled` | VPN clients, installed by the UAVcast-Pro installer. |

Useful commands:

```bash
sudo systemctl status uavcast-web            # is it running?
sudo systemctl restart uavcast-camera        # restart one service
journalctl -u mavlink-manager -f             # follow a service's log live
journalctl -u uavcast-web --since yesterday  # read recent history
```

## Files and folders

Everything lives under `/opt/uavcast-pro`.

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `/opt/uavcast-pro/uavcast.db` | Settings database (SQLite). Back it up from **Application → Database → Backup Database**. |
| `/opt/uavcast-pro/logs/` | Service logs, rotated automatically. Download them from **Application → Logging**. |
| `/opt/uavcast-pro/recordings/` | Camera recordings and telemetry logs on internal storage (unless **Storage location** points to a USB drive or another folder). |
| `/opt/uavcast-pro/missions/` | Saved missions. |
| `/opt/uavcast-pro/installer.log` | Log of the last installation. |
| `/etc/systemd/system/uavcast-web.service` | Web interface service, including `SERVER_PORT`. |

## Installer options

The installer is a single command. Run it again at any time to repair or update an installation.

```bash
# Install or update to the latest version
curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | sudo bash

# List the versions available for this device's architecture
curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | bash -s -- -l

# Install a specific version
curl -fsSL https://install.uavmatrix.com | sudo bash -s -- -b 6.5.2
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-l` | List available versions for this architecture (arm64 or amd64). |
| `-b <version>` | Install that version instead of the latest. |

The installer detects the architecture and OS, installs system packages, ZeroTier, Tailscale and the camera packages, configures the Raspberry Pi UART, sets up the services and starts the web interface. Its log is `/opt/uavcast-pro/installer.log`.

You can also update from the web interface: **Application → Update Application**, pick a version in **Select version to update**, then **Update Now**.

## Integration points

UAVcast-Pro has no public REST API. To integrate with it, use:

- **MAVLink over UDP** to each ground station destination (port 14550 by default), for any MAVLink-capable software.
- **Video** over RTP/UDP (port 5600) or RTSP from the drone (port 8554). See [VLC and RTSP](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/ground-stations/vlc-and-rtsp/).
- **Injectors** to push your own sensor values into the MAVLink stream over HTTP, UDP or serial. See [Injectors](https://docs.uavmatrix.com/uavcast-pro/flight-controller/injectors/).

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/services-and-files/


---

# Glossary

> Plain explanations of terms in the UAVcast-Pro and Fleet Manager docs: MAVLink, GCS, heartbeat, APN, HiLink, NTRIP, RTCM, VRS, ZeroTier, Tailscale.

### AGL / AMSL

Altitude above ground level (here: above the take-off point) and above mean sea level. UAVcast-Pro uses these terms since v6.5.0, replacing REL and MSL.

### APN (Access Point Name)

The name of the carrier's gateway a cellular modem connects through. UAVcast-Pro detects it automatically when **Access Point Name (Optional)** is empty.

### ArduPilot

Open-source autopilot firmware for multicopters, planes, VTOL, rovers and boats. UAVcast-Pro works with ArduPilot and with any other MAVLink flight controller, such as PX4. Its flight-mode buttons use ArduPilot's mode names.

### Auth key

A Tailscale key that logs a device in to a tailnet without a browser. Fleet Manager uses auth keys to put ground stations on the organization's VPN.

### Bitrate

How many bits per second the video encoder produces. It has to fit inside the uplink of your connection, with headroom.

### CSI camera

A camera on the Raspberry Pi's ribbon-cable connector, such as Camera Module 3.

### Destination

In UAVcast-Pro, a ground station entry under **Ground Control Stations**: an IP address with a telemetry port and a video port.

### Dual stream

Streaming two cameras to the ground station at the same time, on two video ports.

### Fleet Manager

UAVmatrix's web dashboard for monitoring and controlling many UAVcast-Pro drones in one organization.

### GCS (ground control station)

The software, and the computer it runs on, that you use to monitor and command the drone: QGroundControl, Mission Planner, MAVProxy.

### GCS failsafe

A flight controller setting that makes the drone act on its own (return, land, loiter) when it stops hearing the ground station.

### GGA

An NMEA sentence with your position. VRS and nearest-mountpoint NTRIP casters need it to compute corrections for your location.

### H.264

The video compression format UAVcast-Pro sends. Every common ground station can decode it.

### Heartbeat

The MAVLink message a flight controller sends about once per second to say "I'm here". *No heartbeat* means the link carries no readable MAVLink.

### HiLink modem

A USB modem with a built-in router that connects by itself and appears to Linux as a network adapter.

### Injector

A UAVcast-Pro listener (HTTP, UDP or serial) that turns your own sensor values into MAVLink `NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT` messages.

### Keyframe

A complete video frame the decoder can start from. More frequent keyframes recover faster from packet loss. Set with **Stream Recovery Rate**.

### MAVLink

The messaging protocol between flight controllers and ground stations.

### Mountpoint

A named correction stream on an NTRIP caster, usually tied to one base station or a VRS service.

### MQTT

The messaging protocol drones use to talk to Fleet Manager, encrypted with TLS on port 8883.

### NTRIP / NTRIP caster

A protocol, and the server, for streaming GNSS corrections over the internet.

### Pairing code

The 8-digit code UAVcast-Pro shows when you connect a drone to Fleet Manager. Valid for 5 minutes, once.

### Read Only (destination)

A ground station destination that receives telemetry but can't change anything on the vehicle: commands, mode changes, parameter and mission writes from it are blocked. This applies from UAVcast-Pro 6.5.3; on earlier versions, Read Only does not block parameter writes.

### Read Only (user)

A UAVcast-Pro user role that can view pages but can't change settings or control the drone.

### RTCM3

The standard message format for GNSS corrections.

### RTK, RTK Float, RTK Fixed

Real-time kinematic positioning with corrections. Float is an approximate solution; Fixed is the centimetre-level solution.

### RTP / UDP

The transport UAVcast-Pro uses for video and telemetry: fast, no retransmissions, which keeps latency low.

### SERIALx_PROTOCOL / SERIALx_BAUD

ArduPilot parameters that set what a serial port speaks (2 = MAVLink2) and how fast.

### Stream binding

In Fleet Manager, a link that sends one drone's video and telemetry to one ground station on its own ports.

### sysid / compid

MAVLink system ID (which vehicle) and component ID (which part of it). The flight controller is usually sysid 1, compid 1.

### Tailnet

A private Tailscale network.

### Tailscale

A WireGuard-based VPN. UAVcast-Pro can join your tailnet, or the Fleet Manager organization network.

### UAVnet

UAVmatrix's hosted ZeroTier network controller at uavnet.uavmatrix.com. It is being discontinued in favour of the Fleet Manager VPN; existing users should move to Fleet Manager.

### VRS (virtual reference station)

A correction service that computes corrections for your position from a network of base stations. Needs GGA upstream.

### ZeroTier

A peer-to-peer VPN. UAVcast-Pro can join your own ZeroTier network.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/glossary/


---

# Changelog

> What changed in each UAVcast-Pro v6 release, from the Rust rewrite in v6.0.0 to recording, flight review, audio, RTK over NTRIP and Fleet Manager.

All UAVcast-Pro v6 releases, newest first. Update from **Application → Update Application**, or run the installer again.

## v6.5.2 (21 Nov 2026)

- Fixed: enabling the camera could show **"Insufficient permissions"**.
- Fixed: the camera stopped when the **live preview** was switched off while recording was on. Video to the ground station now keeps running, and preview and recording come back by themselves when the video server is available again.
- Fixed: the camera service could hang after an automatic video restart until the service was restarted.

## v6.5.1 (16 Nov 2026)

**New**

- **Camera recording**: record camera 1 and camera 2 with one click from the flight map, or automatically while the drone is armed. Recording uses the stream that is already encoded, so it costs no extra CPU and never interrupts the live video to the ground station.
- **Storage management**: record to the internal disk or a USB drive or SSD, keep a free-space reserve, and remove the oldest recordings automatically before the disk fills up (or stop recording instead).
- **Camera → Recordings** page: every flight with its video and telemetry, thumbnails, a live badge while recording, MP4 downloads, and delete (video only, or video and telemetry).
- **Flight review player**: a flight's video together with the map track, the cockpit view and the flight data on one timeline, with arm/disarm and flight-mode markers, 0.5×–4× speed and two-camera layouts.
- **Record telemetry** setting: while armed (default), always while connected, or off.
- **ARM / DISARM** button on the flight map, always behind a confirmation. The flight controller's own safety checks still decide.
- **Messages** list on the flight map: every flight controller message, with the current pre-arm problems shown separately. Messages that arrive in bursts are no longer lost.
- **Automatic APN**: leave the APN empty and UAVcast-Pro finds the right one for your SIM and remembers it.

**Improved**

- **Clear mission** now deletes the mission from the flight controller and waits for its confirmation; before, it only hid it on the map.
- **AGL** altitude now shows the height above the take-off point (it showed the height above sea level).
- **Cockpit view** redesigned so no text overlaps at any panel size; the side panel has a visible handle to resize it.
- **Camera window** redesigned: keeps the camera's own shape (no black bars), with controls that appear on hover.
- **Lower video latency on Raspberry Pi 5**: about half the CPU, no frame buffering, and full frame rate on CSI cameras.
- The live preview recovers by itself if the video server restarts.
- **Read-only users** can watch everything but can no longer control the drone or recordings.
- Modem auto-connect fixed on Ubuntu and other netplan systems; a plugged-in modem now connects automatically by default.
- More robust modem connections, including modems that connected without getting an internet address.
- The modem page shows its information as soon as it opens.
- The installed version is shown in the sidebar.

## v6.5.0 (9 Nov 2026)

- New **camera audio**: sound from a USB microphone or a USB camera's built-in microphone, encoded as Opus. The camera's own microphone is picked automatically when it has one.
- Audio is carried in the **live preview** (unmute the player to hear it) and can be sent to every ground station as a separate RTP/Opus stream on **Video Port + 2** for GStreamer or VLC receivers.
- New **audio indicator** on the Camera page: live level meter, the active device, and a plain-language reason if audio could not start. A failing microphone never interrupts video.
- Selecting a camera that cannot deliver the configured resolution no longer stops video: the stream falls back to the largest supported size and the log says which resolution to pick.
- A fatal video error now restarts the pipeline automatically.
- **Faster NTRIP/RTK recovery**: after a brief internet drop, corrections resume within seconds instead of up to about 18 minutes. A silent caster connection is detected within 15 s and reconnected.
- **Telemetry toggle now fully controls access**: the telemetry router no longer accepts TCP connections on port 5760, so a ground station with telemetry disabled gets no data. If you connected over TCP 5760, add your PC as a ground station and connect over UDP.
- Turning off **Enable Endpoint** on a ground station now also stops its video and audio, not just telemetry.
- The flight map's Light and Dark layers no longer show "API key required".
- Altitude labels renamed to aviation terms: **REL → AGL** and **MSL → AMSL**.
- Fixed service actions (live preview toggle, camera start/stop) failing in development installs.

## v6.4.3 (2 Oct 2026)

- **Flight controller connection rebuilt for reliability**: the link reconnects by itself after a flight controller reboot, a USB glitch or a late power-up.
- New **automatic port and baud rate** (the default, also after upgrading): UAVcast-Pro finds the flight controller, remembers what worked and follows it if the device name changes.
- New **Auto-detect** button and live **Connection check** on the Flight Controller page, showing step by step whether the device is found, data is arriving and telemetry reaches each ground station, with a plain-language fix for the first problem found.
- Telemetry and video **start at power-on without waiting for internet** and begin streaming as soon as the connection is up, however long the modem takes.
- Redesigned **dashboard status card** with an overall health summary, GPS fix type, battery, cellular signal, ground station traffic and a power supply (undervoltage) warning.
- **Log downloads** now include a `diagnostics.txt` snapshot (settings, serial ports, power and USB events).
- Controller type selection removed (ArduPilot only); connection settings apply instantly without a restart.

## v6.4.2 (26 Jul 2026)

- More reliable installs on low-power boards (Pi Zero 2 W), with a realistic time estimate.
- Complete, persistent logging across all services, bundled into the downloadable log archive, and clearer flight controller connection logging.
- Fixed: a missing or invalid destination IP address could break the flight controller connection. Such addresses are now rejected in the UI and skipped by the telemetry router.

## v6.4.1 (9 Jul 2026)

- New **dual camera streaming**: stream two cameras at the same time, each with its own resolution, FPS and bitrate.
- New **CPU load indicator** on the Camera page, which warns when software H.264 encoding nears the limit.
- The **flight map** shows a video window per active stream, which you can hide as tabs at the bottom of the map.
- The installer resolves the renamed camera packages (`rpicam-apps` → `rpicam-apps-core`) and GStreamer plugins, fixing installs on newer Raspberry Pi OS and Debian.
- CSI streaming falls back to a GStreamer x264 pipeline when rpicam-apps lacks H.264 support (Raspberry Pi OS Lite / Debian trixie on Pi 5).
- Multi-camera and dual stream start reliably on every supported OS, with automatic recovery if the stream stalls.
- Unsupported resolutions no longer stop the camera from starting (including **Match Camera 1 Resolution**): capture falls back and the output is scaled.

## v6.4.0 (20 May 2026)

- New **Data Streams** page: custom telemetry dashboards with charts, gauges, sparklines and numeric tiles bound to any MAVLink value or `NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT` signal. Multiple boards, drag-and-resize layout, history kept across page reloads.
- New **Telemetry Injectors** (Flight Controller → Injectors): feed external sensor data into the MAVLink stream over HTTP, UDP or serial as `NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT` / `NAMED_VALUE_INT`. Listeners start at boot without the web interface open.
- New **NTRIP / RTK** tab: connect to an NTRIP caster, browse its mountpoints and stream RTCM corrections to the flight controller, including TLS casters.
- Thanks to Bobby Russell for the feature request and feedback from his high-altitude balloon flights, which inspired Data Streams and injectors.

## v6.3.2 (13 Apr 2026)

- Dependency updates for security and performance (Vite, Axios, backend and frontend libraries, Rust crates).

## v6.3.1 (20 Mar 2026)

- Fixed the installer on Raspberry Pi Compute Module.
- More baud rate options for serial telemetry.
- Better error handling and feedback.
- Dependency updates.

## v6.3.0 (19 Feb 2026)

- New **Fleet Management**: connect UAVcast-Pro devices to Fleet Manager to monitor and manage the whole fleet from one place.
- Consistent look across UAVcast-Pro, Fleet Manager and the store.
- Live preview for custom pipelines with RTSP streams on the Camera page.

## v6.2.3 (12 Jan 2026)

- Multiple CSI cameras each appear as a separate device (for example "Raspberry Pi Camera 0 - imx219" and "Raspberry Pi Camera 1 - imx708").
- CSI camera resolutions and maximum FPS are detected from the connected sensor.

## v6.2.2 (5 Jan 2026)

- Sidebar categories.
- Fixed restoring the application from a database backup.
- Improved flight map icons.
- Link to the changelog in the update card.
- Fixed recordings being saved in the wrong folder.
- The installer adds `rpicam-apps` on Ubuntu and Debian on Raspberry Pi for CSI cameras, and raises CMA memory (128 MB → 512 MB) in `config.txt` for multi-camera setups.
- Fixed manual camera switching after disabling RC channel switching.
- Fixed MAVLink data not loading on the Radio and Inspector tabs without a page reload.

## v6.2.1 (29 Dec 2025)

- Chinese (Traditional) language.
- Improved license validation; some users could not unregister old devices.

## v6.2.0 (20 Dec 2025)

- **arm64 and amd64 support**: UAVcast-Pro is no longer limited to Raspberry Pi and runs on NVIDIA Jetson, x86/x64 computers and other arm64/amd64 devices.

## v6.1.0 (7 Dec 2025)

- **Dual camera support** with instant switching from the UI or an RC channel (channels 1–18).

## v6.0.5

- Fixed the telemetry port not being saved when it differed from 14550.
- Fixed endpoint name conflicts with several destinations on the same IP and different ports.

## v6.0.4

- Support for all ArduPilot vehicle types, including VTOL.
- More stable MAVLink connection handling.

## v6.0.3

- New **Flight Analytics** page with MAVLink data in graphs.
- MAVLink recording to a file for analysis.
- Tighter permissions for read-only users.

## v6.0.2

- MAVLink system ID and MAVLink version are detected from the flight controller.

## v6.0.1

- More reliable installer on low-resource devices such as Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W.
- Improved UART setup on Pi Zero 2 W.

## v6.0.0

- Major release: the backend was rewritten in Rust for performance and lower resource use, and the package is about 70% smaller.
- New **Flight Map**, **Mission Planner**, **MAVLink Inspector** and **Radio** pages.
- New **network priority** setting to choose between Wi-Fi and modem.
- New **User Management** with roles.
- New camera handling and live preview based on MediaMTX.
- v6 uses a new database: settings from v4 and v5 can't be imported.

Source: https://docs.uavmatrix.com/reference/changelog/
